sec04-card-f37.expected_back: Motor vehicles and trailers need fenders, wheel covers or flaps that prevent wheel-thrown material from reaching other vehicles.

sec04-card-f38.front: What rear red lamps must a trailer manufactured from nineteen fifty-six onward carry?
sec04-card-f38.expected_back: A trailer or semitrailer built on or after January first, nineteen fifty-six needs at least two red rear lamps, one on each side, visible from five hundred feet behind.

sec04-card-r10.front: Besides crash protection, how do safety belts help the driver on rough, winding roads or sudden swerves?
sec04-card-r10.expected_back: Safety belts help the driver keep control on winding or rough roads and during collision-avoidance maneuvers.

sec04-card-r11.front: Which vehicles are the only ones allowed to carry red and blue emergency lights?
sec04-card-r11.expected_back: Red and blue emergency lights are permitted only on emergency vehicles.

sec04-card-r12.front: Which three audible warning devices are prohibited on ordinary motor vehicles?
sec04-card-r12.expected_back: Sirens, bells and whistles are listed as prohibited equipment for ordinary vehicles.

sec04-card-r13.front: What rule applies to a muffler cutout or bypass that boosts exhaust noise?
sec04-card-r13.expected_back: A muffler cutout or bypass that increases exhaust noise is prohibited.

sec04-card-r14.front: At most how many spotlights may a motor vehicle have?
sec04-card-r14.expected_back: A vehicle must not have more than two spotlights.

sec04-card-r15.front: What is the maximum number of front auxiliary lights permitted on a vehicle?
sec04-card-r15.expected_back: A vehicle must not have more than two front auxiliary lights.

sec04-card-r16.front: At most how many front fog lights is a vehicle allowed to carry?
sec04-card-r16.expected_back: A vehicle must not have more than two front fog lights.

sec04-card-r17.front: What is the maximum number of cowl or fender lights permitted on a motor vehicle?
sec04-card-r17.expected_back: A vehicle must not have more than two cowl or fender lights.

sec04-card-r23.front: What must a driver clear from the windows before driving so visibility stays open in every direction?
sec04-card-r23.expected_back: Before driving, the driver must clear ice, snow and dirt from the windows to preserve visibility in every direction.

sec05-card-f05.front: Where must you bring your vehicle to a halt at a stop sign when a painted stop line is on the pavement?
sec05-card-f05.expected_back: At a stop sign, stop at the clearly marked stop line when one is present.

sec05-card-f06.front: Where must you stop for a stop sign when no stop line is painted on the road?
sec05-card-f06.expected_back: At a stop sign without a stop line, stop before the crosswalk on the near side of the intersection.

sec05-card-f07.front: Where do you stop at a stop sign when neither a stop line nor a crosswalk exists?
sec05-card-f07.expected_back: At a stop sign with neither a stop line nor a crosswalk, stop before entering the intersecting highway at the nearest point where approaching traffic can be seen.

sec05-card-f08.front: What actions does a Yield sign require toward vehicles and pedestrians in the intersection or roadway ahead?
sec05-card-f08.expected_back: A Yield sign requires slowing and yielding to vehicles and pedestrians in the intersection being crossed or on the road being entered.

sec05-card-f09.front: When must a driver come to a complete stop at a Yield sign?
sec05-card-f09.expected_back: At a Yield sign, stop before crossing the intersection or entering the highway if that is necessary to yield safely.

sec05-card-f10.front: What movement does a Do Not Enter sign forbid?
sec05-card-f10.expected_back: A Do Not Enter sign prohibits entry to that highway section from the direction being traveled.

sec05-card-f11.front: Under what driving conditions does a speed-limit sign state the maximum speed allowed?
sec05-card-f11.expected_back: A speed-limit sign states the maximum speed for that road section under ideal driving conditions.

sec05-card-f12.front: Which side of an approaching island or barrier must you pass when directed by a Keep Right of Island sign?
sec05-card-f12.expected_back: A Keep Right of Island sign directs traffic to the right of the island or barrier ahead.

sec05-card-f13.front: What color and types of channelizing or warning devices commonly identify a highway work zone?
sec05-card-f13.expected_back: Work zones commonly use orange signs, cones, drums, barricades or flashing arrow panels to identify the area.

sec05-card-f14.front: Which road-surface and equipment hazards should you scan for inside a work zone?
sec05-card-f14.expected_back: In a work zone, watch for hazards such as uneven pavement, narrow lanes, heavy equipment and gravel.

sec05-card-f15.front: Which two colors are used on work-zone warning signs?
sec05-card-f15.expected_back: Work-zone warning signs use orange and black.

sec05-card-f16.front: What is the rule about moving or driving around barriers and signs blocking a closed road?
sec05-card-f16.expected_back: Do not move or go around barriers or signs to cross onto a road closed to traffic.

sec05-card-f17.front: How should you position your vehicle when a work-zone lane-shift sign redirects every lane?
sec05-card-f17.expected_back: When a lane-shift sign redirects all lanes, remain in the same lane while following its shift.

sec05-card-f18.front: How must you respond when you encounter a Be Prepared to Stop work-zone sign?
sec05-card-f18.expected_back: A Be Prepared to Stop sign calls for slowing and readiness to stop for road work ahead.

sec05-card-f19.front: What driving adjustment is required when you see a slow-moving-vehicle warning?
sec05-card-f19.expected_back: A slow-moving-vehicle warning calls for reducing speed and approaching the vehicle cautiously.

sec05-card-f21.front: Who is allowed past a Road Closed sign into a work zone?
sec05-card-f21.expected_back: A Road Closed sign prohibits entry to the work zone except by authorized personnel.

sec05-card-f22.front: When may residential or commercial drivers enter a work zone posted Local Traffic Only or Closed to Thru Traffic?
sec05-card-f22.expected_back: A closure marked Local Traffic Only or Closed to Thru Traffic permits local residential or commercial traffic only when it has a reason to stop within the work zone.

sec05-card-f23.front: What kind of trip is prohibited by properly posted work-zone closure signs?
sec05-card-f23.expected_back: Properly posted work-zone closure signs prohibit continuous trips through the closed work zone.

sec05-card-f24.front: What happens to speeding fines in work zones posted with penalty-increase signs?
sec05-card-f24.expected_back: Work-zone speeding fines are increased where signs indicate the increase.

sec05-card-f25.front: Why must you scan closely for highway crews whenever driving through a work zone?
sec05-card-f25.expected_back: Watch closely for work-zone personnel because they may work near traffic during both daytime and nighttime.

sec05-card-f26.front: How much following distance should you keep behind the vehicle ahead inside a work zone?
sec05-card-f26.expected_back: Leave ample space behind the vehicle ahead while traveling through a work zone.

sec05-card-f27.front: How should you manage travel time and cabin distractions like phones or stereos in work zones?
sec05-card-f27.expected_back: In work zones, allow extra time and reduce distractions such as phones and the stereo.

sec05-card-f02.front: Which three groups of people directing traffic must drivers obey on the road?
sec05-card-f02.expected_back: Drivers must obey traffic directions given by law enforcement officers, highway personnel and school crossing guards.

sec05-card-f29.front: How must motorists respond to traffic directions from a school safety patrol official?
sec05-card-f29.expected_back: Motorists must follow directions from a school safety patrol official.

sec05-card-f30.front: What three items identify a school-appointed safety patrol official on duty?
sec05-card-f30.expected_back: School-appointed safety patrol officials identify their duty through a badge, appropriate clothing or School Patrol insignia.

sec05-card-f31.front: What do school safety patrol officials display where schoolchildren cross public roads?
sec05-card-f31.expected_back: School safety patrol officials display stop or other directional signs where schoolchildren cross public roads.

sec05-card-f32.front: What shape and colors do most standard warning signs use?
sec05-card-f32.expected_back: Most warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on yellow.

sec05-card-f33.front: Which high-visibility color may school warning signs use?
sec05-card-f33.expected_back: School warning signs may use fluorescent yellow-green.

sec05-card-f34.front: What road situation does a warning sign alert you to prepare for?
sec05-card-f34.expected_back: A warning sign indicates an unexpected condition that may require slowing or another response.

sec05-card-f35.front: What does an Open Range warning mean about fencing and right-of-way for livestock?
sec05-card-f35.expected_back: An Open Range sign identifies an area where livestock may roam unfenced and have the right of way.

sec05-card-f36.front: What road layout does a T-intersection warning describe for your lane of travel?
sec05-card-f36.expected_back: The handbook's T-intersection warning describes a junction where the driver must turn left or right.

sec05-card-f37.front: What must you do before turning at the T-intersection described by the warning sign?
sec05-card-f37.expected_back: At the T-intersection described by the handbook's warning, stop and yield to drivers approaching from either crossing direction.

sec05-card-f38.front: What action does an intersection or crossroads warning call for as you approach?
sec05-card-f38.expected_back: An intersection or crossroads warning calls for watching for cross-traffic from the road crossing ahead.

sec05-card-f39.front: What does a Traffic Signal Ahead warning announce, and on what kinds of roads is it placed?
sec05-card-f39.expected_back: A Traffic Signal Ahead sign warns of an upcoming signalized intersection and is used on roads with higher speeds or blocked views of the intersection or signal.

sec05-card-r01.front: What nearby hazard does a School Zone sign warn drivers to watch for?
sec05-card-r01.expected_back: A School Zone sign warns of a nearby school crossing where drivers should watch for children.

sec05-card-r02.front: What consequence applies to violating a posted school-zone speed limit?
sec05-card-r02.expected_back: Violating a school-zone speed limit carries increased penalties.

sec05-card-r03.front: Which two background colors are valid for a School Zone sign?
sec05-card-r03.expected_back: A School Zone sign may be yellow or fluorescent yellow-green.

sec05-card-r04.front: What road layout and lane-change hazard does an Added Lane warning describe?
sec05-card-r04.expected_back: An Added Lane sign describes highways converging and warns that traffic from the left lane may move into the right lane.

sec05-card-r05.front: What two steps must you take before moving left near an added-lane area?
sec05-card-r05.expected_back: When moving left near an added-lane area, first check that the lane is clear and signal the lane change.

sec05-card-r06.front: What highway transition does a Two-Way Traffic warning announce?
sec05-card-r06.expected_back: A Two-Way Traffic sign warns that a divided multilane highway changes to a two-lane road carrying traffic in both directions.

sec05-card-r07.front: When posted on the main road, what does a Merging Traffic warning tell you?
sec05-card-r07.expected_back: On the main road, a Merging Traffic sign warns that other vehicles may enter the driver's lane.

sec05-card-r08.front: What does a Lane Ends or Merge Left warning mean about lane count and right-of-way?
sec05-card-r08.expected_back: A Lane Ends or Merge Left sign warns that two lanes become one and that merging traffic must yield.

sec05-card-r10.front: What separation disappears ahead after a Divided Highway Ends warning?
sec05-card-r10.expected_back: A Divided Highway Ends sign warns that opposing traffic will no longer be separated by a center strip.

sec05-card-r11.front: Which three actions are required when approaching a School Crossing warning?
sec05-card-r11.expected_back: At a School Crossing warning, watch for children, slow down and obey the crossing guard.

sec05-card-r13.front: What does a Pedestrian Crossing warning tell you about right-of-way and stopping?
sec05-card-r13.expected_back: A Pedestrian Crossing sign warns of crossing pedestrians who have the right of way and may require the driver to stop.

sec05-card-r14.front: What color and active feature may a Pedestrian Crossing warning use when someone crosses?
sec05-card-r14.expected_back: A Pedestrian Crossing sign may be fluorescent yellow-green and may use flashing lights to show that a pedestrian is crossing.

sec05-card-r15.front: What road change ahead does a Divided Highway Begins warning announce?
sec05-card-r15.expected_back: A Divided Highway Begins sign warns that a center strip will separate the two directions of traffic ahead.

sec05-card-r16.front: What does a Share the Road plaque beneath a bicycle symbol tell drivers and cyclists?
sec05-card-r16.expected_back: A Share the Road sign below a bicycle symbol warns drivers and bicyclists to share a highway where bicycle lanes are absent.

sec05-card-r17.front: Under what lane, shoulder, or traffic conditions are Share the Road signs commonly posted?
sec05-card-r17.expected_back: Share the Road signs may be placed where lanes or shoulders are narrow or traffic volume or speed is high.

sec05-card-r18.front: Where is the pennant-shaped No Passing Zone sign mounted, and what does it mean?
sec05-card-r18.expected_back: The pennant-shaped No Passing Zone sign stands on the left side and warns that passing is prohibited for that lane.

sec05-card-r19.front: What should a driver check upon seeing a steep downhill warning?
sec05-card-r19.expected_back: A downhill warning directs drivers to check their brakes before descending the steep hill ahead.

sec05-card-r20.front: What hazard and driver action does a Slippery When Wet warning indicate?
sec05-card-r20.expected_back: A Slippery When Wet sign warns that wet weather may make the road slippery and calls for slowing under those conditions.

sec05-card-r21.front: What readiness does a railroad advance warning require as you approach the crossing?
sec05-card-r21.expected_back: A railroad advance warning calls for readiness to stop before the tracks if a train approaches the crossing.

sec05-card-r22.front: What should you watch for when passing an Animal Crossing warning?
sec05-card-r22.expected_back: An Animal Crossing warning calls for watching for animals crossing the highway.

sec05-card-r23.front: Where is a railroad Emergency Notification System sign posted, and what two numbers does it list?
sec05-card-r23.expected_back: A railroad Emergency Notification System sign is posted at or near a crossing and provides the railroad phone number and that crossing's identifying number.

sec05-card-r24.front: What two kinds of problems is the railroad emergency sign designed to help you report?
sec05-card-r24.expected_back: The railroad emergency sign supplies the information needed to report an emergency or a warning-device malfunction to the railroad.

sec05-card-r25.front: What two types of navigation details do white-on-green guide signs provide?
sec05-card-r25.expected_back: White-on-green guide signs provide direction and distance information.

sec05-card-r26.front: What category of roadside information appears on white-on-blue guide signs?
sec05-card-r26.expected_back: White-on-blue guide signs identify motorist services.

sec05-card-r27.front: What destinations do white-on-brown guide signs point out?
sec05-card-r27.expected_back: White-on-brown guide signs identify cultural, historical or scenic points of interest.

sec05-card-r28.front: What visibility feature may barricades carry, especially after dark?
sec05-card-r28.expected_back: Barricades may carry flashing lights, especially at night.

sec05-card-r29.front: How do permanent barricade colors differ from temporary barricade colors in the Idaho handbook?
sec05-card-r29.expected_back: The handbook describes permanent barricades as red and white and temporary barricades as orange and white.

sec05-card-r30.front: Does switching between red-and-white and orange-and-white barricade colors change what the stripe angles mean?
sec05-card-r30.expected_back: Different barricade colors do not change the directions their patterns give drivers.

sec05-card-r31.front: What does a V-shaped stripe pattern on a barricade tell approaching traffic?
sec05-card-r31.expected_back: A V-shaped barricade pattern means the road is closed and traffic cannot proceed farther.

sec05-card-r32.front: On which side should you pass a barricade whose stripes slant downward toward the left?
sec05-card-r32.expected_back: Barricade stripes slanting down toward the left direct traffic past the barricade on its left side.

sec05-card-r33.front: On which side should you pass a barricade whose stripes slant downward toward the right?
sec05-card-r33.expected_back: Barricade stripes slanting down toward the right direct traffic past the barricade on its right side.

sec05-card-f01.front: What collective term covers traffic signals, highway signs, and pavement markings?
sec05-card-f01.expected_back: Traffic signals, signs and pavement markings are traffic-control devices.

sec05-card-f03.front: Which three visual traits should you learn so you can recognize traffic signs quickly?
sec05-card-f03.expected_back: Learn to recognize traffic signs by their color, shape and written message or symbol.

sec05-card-f04.front: Which color combinations are normally used on regulatory traffic signs?
sec05-card-f04.expected_back: Regulatory signs are usually black and white, although some use red and white.

sec05-card-f20.front: What kinds of vehicles mainly display the slow-moving-vehicle sign according to the handbook?
sec05-card-f20.expected_back: The handbook says the slow-moving-vehicle sign is used mainly on off-road equipment such as farm and construction vehicles.

sec05-card-f28.front: Which four driver errors are cited as major contributors to work-zone crashes?
sec05-card-f28.expected_back: Speeding, inattention, failure to yield and improper lane changes contribute to work-zone crashes.

sec05-card-r09.front: What hazard above the roadway does a Low Clearance sign warn about?
sec05-card-r09.expected_back: A Low Clearance sign warns of very low overhead clearance above the highway.

sec05-card-r12.front: Which two colors may be used for a School Crossing sign?
sec05-card-r12.expected_back: A School Crossing sign may be yellow or fluorescent yellow-green.

sec06-card-f04.front: Where must you come to a complete stop when facing a steady circular red light?
sec06-card-f04.expected_back: A steady circular red signal requires a complete stop before the stop line, crosswalk or intersection.

sec06-card-f05.front: What movement is forbidden when a No Turn on Red notice is posted at a signal?
sec06-card-f05.expected_back: A No Turn on Red notice prohibits the red-light turn discussed in the handbook's circular-red guidance.

sec06-card-f06.front: What three steps must you follow at a flashing red traffic light?
sec06-card-f06.expected_back: At a flashing red signal, stop completely, yield to crossing traffic and pedestrians, and proceed only when clear.

sec06-card-f07.front: May you turn in the direction of a steady red arrow after stopping, or what must happen first?
sec06-card-f07.expected_back: A steady red arrow forbids a turn in its direction until a green or yellow indication permits that movement.

sec06-card-f08.front: What signal change does a steady circular yellow light warn is about to happen?
sec06-card-f08.expected_back: A yellow circular signal warns that the indication is about to become red.

sec06-card-f09.front: What should a driver do before entering an intersection when the circular light turns yellow?
sec06-card-f09.expected_back: Before entering on a yellow circular signal, a driver should stop when a safe stop is possible.

sec06-card-f10.front: What should you do if the light turns circular yellow after you are already inside the intersection?
sec06-card-f10.expected_back: A driver already in the intersection on a circular yellow should keep moving and clear it safely.

sec06-card-f11.front: How should you drive through a flashing circular yellow light?
sec06-card-f11.expected_back: A flashing circular yellow signal calls for slowing, checking carefully for hazards and continuing cautiously.

sec06-card-f12.front: What does a solid yellow arrow tell drivers in a turn lane?
sec06-card-f12.expected_back: A solid yellow arrow warns that the turn signal is changing.

sec06-card-f13.front: What should you do if a solid yellow arrow appears before you enter the intersection?
sec06-card-f13.expected_back: Before entering on a solid yellow arrow, a driver should stop if it can be done safely.

sec06-card-f14.front: How should you finish when a solid yellow arrow appears while you are already in the intersection turning?
sec06-card-f14.expected_back: A driver already in the intersection on a solid yellow arrow should continue the turn and clear the intersection safely.

sec06-card-f15.front: Under what condition does a flashing yellow arrow allow you to turn?
sec06-card-f15.expected_back: A flashing yellow arrow permits a turn only after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians in crosswalks.

sec06-card-f16.front: What movement does a steady circular green indication allow?
sec06-card-f16.expected_back: A circular green indication allows forward travel.

sec06-card-f17.front: Who has the right-of-way when you turn left from a left-turn lane on a circular green light?
sec06-card-f17.expected_back: A driver turning left from a left-turn lane on circular green must first yield to oncoming traffic and crosswalk pedestrians.

sec06-card-f18.front: Why must you hold back even on a green light when traffic ahead is backed up?
sec06-card-f18.expected_back: Even on a signal allowing movement, a driver should not enter unless there is enough room beyond the intersection for the entire vehicle to clear it.

sec06-card-f19.front: Which turning movement commonly uses a five-lens doghouse traffic signal?
sec06-card-f19.expected_back: A doghouse signal is commonly used for a protected left turn.

sec06-card-f20.front: What does the yellow indication on a doghouse signal tell left-turning drivers?
sec06-card-f20.expected_back: The yellow indication on a doghouse signal means the protected left-turn movement is ending.

sec06-card-f21.front: How must drivers treat an intersection when the traffic signals stop working?
sec06-card-f21.expected_back: Treat an intersection with a nonfunctioning traffic signal as a four-way stop.

sec06-card-f22.front: How are the colored lenses arranged on a pedestrian hybrid beacon?
sec06-card-f22.expected_back: A pedestrian hybrid beacon has two red lenses above one yellow lens.

sec06-card-f23.front: Where are pedestrian hybrid beacon lights mounted at a crossing?
sec06-card-f23.expected_back: Pedestrian hybrid beacon lights are mounted over the highway on a mast arm and along the roadside.

sec06-card-f24.front: How is a stop-controlled side street affected when a pedestrian hybrid beacon operates on the main road?
sec06-card-f24.expected_back: A side street controlled by a stop sign remains stop-controlled when a pedestrian hybrid beacon is installed.

sec06-card-f25.front: Who must you check for right before turning around a street corner?
sec06-card-f25.expected_back: Before turning a corner, watch for people who are about to cross the street.

sec06-card-f26.front: What does a pedestrian hybrid beacon display before anyone presses the crossing button?
sec06-card-f26.expected_back: The pedestrian hybrid beacon remains dark until a pedestrian presses the crossing button.

sec06-card-f27.front: What does the flashing yellow phase on a pedestrian hybrid beacon tell approaching drivers?
sec06-card-f27.expected_back: A pedestrian hybrid beacon's flashing yellow phase warns approaching drivers to slow down.

sec06-card-f28.front: What does a pedestrian hybrid beacon instruct drivers to do when flashing yellow turns steady yellow?
sec06-card-f28.expected_back: The pedestrian hybrid beacon changes from flashing yellow to steady yellow to tell drivers to prepare to stop.

sec06-card-f29.front: What action do two steady red lights on a pedestrian hybrid beacon require?
sec06-card-f29.expected_back: Two steady red lights at a pedestrian hybrid beacon require a complete stop at the stop line.

sec06-card-f30.front: How should you respond when a pedestrian hybrid beacon switches to alternating flashing red lights?
sec06-card-f30.expected_back: When a pedestrian hybrid beacon alternates flashing red lights, stop, yield to crosswalk pedestrians and proceed only when the crosswalk is clear.

sec06-card-f31.front: When a pedestrian hybrid beacon finishes its cycle and goes dark again, what may drivers do?
sec06-card-f31.expected_back: When the pedestrian hybrid beacon returns to darkness, drivers may proceed if the crosswalk is clear.

sec06-card-r02.front: Who may cross a single dashed yellow center line to pass?
sec06-card-r02.expected_back: A dashed yellow center line may be crossed from either lane when doing so is safe.

sec06-card-r03.front: When a solid yellow line runs beside a dashed yellow line, which lane is allowed to pass?
sec06-card-r03.expected_back: With one solid yellow line beside one dashed yellow line, only traffic on the dashed-line side may cross the lines to pass.

sec06-card-r04.front: What passing rule do double solid yellow center lines enforce?
sec06-card-r04.expected_back: Double solid yellow center lines prohibit passing from either traffic lane.

sec06-card-r05.front: Under what circumstance may you cross double solid yellow center lines?
sec06-card-r05.expected_back: Double solid yellow lines may be crossed for a turn only when it is safe.

sec06-card-r06.front: Which roadside entrances may you enter or leave by turning left across double yellow lines when safe?
sec06-card-r06.expected_back: When it is safe, a driver may cross double yellow lines to turn left into or out of a driveway or business entrance.

sec06-card-r07.front: Which maneuvers are allowed from a shared center turn lane?
sec06-card-r07.expected_back: A shared center lane is reserved for left turns, or U-turns where permitted, from either direction of travel.

sec06-card-r08.front: How are the pavement lines painted along each edge of a shared center turn lane?
sec06-card-r08.expected_back: A shared center turn lane has a solid yellow line and a dashed yellow line along each side.

sec06-card-r09.front: What type of driving is forbidden inside a shared center turn lane?
sec06-card-r09.expected_back: Do not use a shared center turn lane for through travel.

sec06-card-r10.front: How must you behave toward another vehicle already preparing to turn from a shared center turn lane?
sec06-card-r10.expected_back: Do not interfere with a vehicle preparing to turn from a shared center turn lane.

sec06-card-r11.front: What traffic directions are separated by broken white lane lines on a multilane road?
sec06-card-r11.expected_back: Broken white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction on a multilane road.

sec06-card-r12.front: How should you position your vehicle relative to broken white lane boundaries?
sec06-card-r12.expected_back: Drive inside the broken white lane boundaries rather than straddling them.

sec06-card-r13.front: When may you cross a broken white lane line?
sec06-card-r13.expected_back: Cross a broken white lane line only for a lane change that can be made safely.

sec06-card-r14.front: What boundary do solid white edge lines mark on a roadway?
sec06-card-r14.expected_back: Solid white edge lines mark the side boundary of the road.

sec06-card-r15.front: When are solid white edge lines especially helpful for keeping your vehicle on the road?
sec06-card-r15.expected_back: White edge lines help drivers stay on the road at night or in poor weather.

sec06-card-r16.front: How should you treat a single solid white line separating same-direction traffic lanes?
sec06-card-r16.expected_back: Avoid changing between same-direction traffic lanes where a solid white line separates them.

sec06-card-r19.front: What rule applies where double solid white lines separate lanes?
sec06-card-r19.expected_back: Double solid white lane markings prohibit lane changes where they are present.

sec06-card-r17.front: What do a solid white boundary line and a painted bicycle symbol designate?
sec06-card-r17.expected_back: A solid white boundary with a bicycle symbol designates an area for bicycle traffic only.

sec06-card-r18.front: Which direction must bicyclists ride inside a designated bicycle lane?
sec06-card-r18.expected_back: Bicycles in the designated bicycle area must travel in the same direction as adjacent traffic.

sec06-card-r20.front: What two merging movements are permitted where a bicycle-lane stripe turns dashed?
sec06-card-r20.expected_back: A dashed bicycle-lane boundary allows a right-turning driver to merge right and a left-turning bicyclist to merge left.

sec06-card-r21.front: At which roadway locations does the handbook place dashed bicycle-lane lines?
sec06-card-r21.expected_back: The handbook places dashed bicycle-lane lines at intersections or some driveway areas.

sec06-card-f01.front: What is the main function of traffic signals, and where do they chiefly operate?
sec06-card-f01.expected_back: Traffic signals regulate traffic flow, chiefly through intersections.

sec06-card-f02.front: From top to bottom, how are red, yellow, and green arranged on a vertical traffic light?
sec06-card-f02.expected_back: A vertical traffic signal places red above yellow, with green at the bottom.

sec06-card-f03.front: From left to right, how are red, yellow, and green positioned on a horizontal traffic signal?
sec06-card-f03.expected_back: A horizontal traffic signal places red on the far left, yellow in the middle and green on the far right.

sec06-card-r01.front: Besides separating lanes, what five rules or zones do pavement markings identify?
sec06-card-r01.expected_back: Pavement markings separate lanes and identify passing restrictions, lane-change restrictions, turn lanes, pedestrian areas and stopping places.

sec07-card-f07.front: How should you use your senses when approaching any railroad crossing?
sec07-card-f07.expected_back: At a railroad crossing, drivers should listen and look in both directions for trains and their warning signals.

sec07-card-f08.front: When is a driver allowed to proceed across railroad tracks?
sec07-card-f08.expected_back: Do not proceed through a railroad crossing until certain that doing so is safe.

sec07-card-f09.front: How many feet from the nearest rail must you stop when a railroad crossing stop is required?
sec07-card-f09.expected_back: When a railroad stop is required, the handbook says the driver should stop at least fifteen feet and no more than fifty feet from the nearest rail.

sec07-card-f14.front: What must you do when red railroad crossing warning lights are actively flashing?
sec07-card-f14.expected_back: Active flashing railroad warning lights require a stop, and further movement is allowed only when safe.

sec07-card-f15.front: What is the rule whenever a railroad crossing gate is down or starting to lower?
sec07-card-f15.expected_back: Never drive through, beneath or around a railroad gate that is down or being lowered.

sec07-card-f17.front: May you ever stop with any part of your vehicle resting on railroad tracks?
sec07-card-f17.expected_back: Never stop while any part of the vehicle is on railroad tracks.

sec07-card-f18.front: In slow or backed-up traffic, what must you confirm before driving onto a railroad crossing?
sec07-card-f18.expected_back: In traffic, do not enter a railroad crossing unless there is enough room beyond it for the vehicle's full length.

sec07-card-f19.front: May you ignore active railroad signals or circle lowered gates if you cannot see a train coming?
sec07-card-f19.expected_back: Do not ignore a railroad warning signal or drive around lowered gates even when no approaching train is visible.

sec07-card-f20.front: Why must you never shift gears while your vehicle is crossing railroad tracks?
sec07-card-f20.expected_back: Do not change gears while crossing railroad tracks because doing so may stall the vehicle there.

sec07-card-f21.front: What rule applies to trying to outrun an approaching train to a crossing?
sec07-card-f21.expected_back: Never try to beat a train to a crossing.

sec07-card-f22.front: What must you check before crossing where two or more sets of railroad tracks run side by side?
sec07-card-f22.expected_back: Before proceeding over multiple railroad tracks, make sure another train is not approaching on a different track.

sec07-card-f23.front: Why should you stay alert behind buses and large trucks approaching railroad crossings?
sec07-card-f23.expected_back: Watch for buses and trucks that are required to stop at railroad crossings, since some must stop at every crossing.

sec07-card-f24.front: Why must you still look both ways at railroad tracks when the flashing lights are dark?
sec07-card-f24.expected_back: Look in both directions when approaching railroad tracks even if the flashing warning signal is not working.

sec07-card-f25.front: How is a roundabout defined by travel flow and turn direction at entry and exit?
sec07-card-f25.expected_back: A roundabout is a one-way circular junction entered and exited by turning right.

sec07-card-f27.front: Who holds the right-of-way between a driver entering a roundabout and vehicles already inside it?
sec07-card-f27.expected_back: Drivers entering a roundabout must yield to vehicles already circulating in it.

sec07-card-f28.front: Which rotational direction do you follow inside a roundabout when going straight, left, or making a U-turn?
sec07-card-f28.expected_back: Enter a roundabout counterclockwise and merge into its circulating traffic regardless of whether the desired route is right, left, straight or a U-turn.

sec07-card-f29.front: How should you manage your speed on the approach to and inside a roundabout?
sec07-card-f29.expected_back: Slow down when approaching a roundabout and keep the speed low while using it.

sec07-card-f30.front: What roadside and pavement controls must you follow at a roundabout?
sec07-card-f30.expected_back: Obey the traffic signs and pavement markings at a roundabout.

sec07-card-f31.front: When must you yield to pedestrians and bicyclists at a roundabout?
sec07-card-f31.expected_back: Yield to pedestrians and bicyclists both when entering and when leaving a roundabout.

sec07-card-f32.front: From which side does circulating roundabout traffic approach as you wait to enter?
sec07-card-f32.expected_back: Yield to traffic approaching from the left that is already circulating in a roundabout.

sec07-card-f33.front: Which turn signal should you activate as your roundabout exit approaches?
sec07-card-f33.expected_back: Use the right turn signal as the roundabout exit approaches.

sec07-card-f01.front: What must a right-turning driver do when a bicyclist is already in the bike-and-turn merging area?
sec07-card-f01.expected_back: A right-turning driver must yield when a bicycle already occupies the bicycle and turning-vehicle merging area.

sec07-card-f02.front: Where should a bicyclist go when a right-turning car already occupies the merging area ahead?
sec07-card-f02.expected_back: A bicyclist must move left when a car already occupies the bicycle and turning-vehicle merging area.

sec07-card-f03.front: What traffic condition does green-colored pavement emphasize?
sec07-card-f03.expected_back: Green pavement emphasizes places where different traffic movements cross one another.

sec07-card-f04.front: Why are some bicycle lanes and intersection extensions painted bright green?
sec07-card-f04.expected_back: Some bicycle lanes and their extensions through intersections are painted green for added emphasis.

sec07-card-f05.front: What must drivers watch for at a green-painted bicycle-lane crossing area?
sec07-card-f05.expected_back: At a green bicycle-lane crossing area, drivers must watch for bicycles.

sec07-card-f06.front: What must bicyclists keep in mind while riding across a green bicycle-lane crossing area?
sec07-card-f06.expected_back: Bicyclists in a green bicycle-lane crossing area must be aware that vehicles cross the bicycle lane there.

sec07-card-r01.front: Which turning movement does a thru-turn intersection prohibit directly at the main junction?
sec07-card-r01.expected_back: A thru-turn intersection manages traffic by prohibiting direct left turns.

sec07-card-r02.front: What four-step path replaces a direct left turn at a thru-turn intersection?
sec07-card-r02.expected_back: For a left turn at a thru-turn intersection, first continue through, use the marked U-turn at the next signal downstream, return toward the intersection and turn right.

sec07-card-r03.front: How does a single point urban interchange control turning traffic?
sec07-card-r03.expected_back: A single point urban interchange controls turns from a single signal-controlled point at the interchange center.

sec07-card-r04.front: Why is stopping behind the painted stop lines critical at a single point urban interchange?
sec07-card-r04.expected_back: At the described single point urban interchange, stop at the stop lines so the vehicle does not extend into cross-traffic.

sec07-card-r05.front: Which lanes do you use to go straight across the handbook's single point urban interchange?
sec07-card-r05.expected_back: To go straight through the described single point urban interchange, stay in either of its two through lanes.

sec07-card-r06.front: Which lanes take you left onto the freeway at a single point urban interchange?
sec07-card-r06.expected_back: To turn left onto the highway at the described single point urban interchange, use the lanes marked for left turns.

sec07-card-r07.front: How does the off-ramp divide traffic at a single point urban interchange?
sec07-card-r07.expected_back: The single point urban interchange's exit ramp separates traffic into left-turn and right-turn lanes.

sec07-card-r08.front: What must you do if you exit by mistake at a single point urban interchange instead of going straight across?
sec07-card-r08.expected_back: After mistakenly exiting at the described single point urban interchange, do not cross straight to reenter; turn left or right onto the intersecting highway and find a safe turnaround to the correct freeway entrance.

sec07-card-r09.front: How do you complete a right turn after leaving the interstate at a single point urban interchange?
sec07-card-r09.expected_back: For a right turn after exiting the interstate at the described single point urban interchange, remain in the right lane, yield, turn right, merge and watch for pedestrians.

sec07-card-r10.front: How do you turn left onto the cross highway from a single point urban interchange off-ramp?
sec07-card-r10.expected_back: For a left turn after exiting the interstate at the single point urban interchange, use the left exit lane, merge onto the highway and watch for pedestrians.

sec07-card-r11.front: Which three features serve people walking or biking through the described single point urban interchange?
sec07-card-r11.expected_back: The described single point urban interchange provides crosswalks, bicycle paths and pedestrian signals.

sec07-card-r12.front: Where do signalized crossings direct pedestrians and cyclists mid-way across a single point urban interchange?
sec07-card-r12.expected_back: Pedestrians and bicyclists at the described single point urban interchange use the signalized crossing and are directed to the central pedestrian island.

sec07-card-r13.front: How does a diverging diamond interchange shift lanes, and what benefit does that provide?
sec07-card-r13.expected_back: A diverging diamond interchange temporarily moves traffic lanes to the highway's left side to provide direct interstate access.

sec07-card-r14.front: Where do opposing lanes cross over each other at a diverging diamond interchange?
sec07-card-r14.expected_back: At a diverging diamond interchange, opposing traffic crosses at the signals on either side of the bridge or overpass.

sec07-card-r15.front: Which four roadway guides steer you safely through a diverging diamond interchange?
sec07-card-r15.expected_back: Follow the road signs, signals, raised islands and pavement markings through a diverging diamond interchange.

sec07-card-r16.front: Why must you stop right at the painted stop lines inside a diverging diamond interchange?
sec07-card-r16.expected_back: At a diverging diamond interchange, stop at the stop lines to avoid blocking cross-traffic, pedestrians or bicyclists.

sec07-card-r17.front: How do you drive straight across a diverging diamond interchange from entry to exit?
sec07-card-r17.expected_back: To travel straight through the described diverging diamond interchange, follow the lane to the opposite side at the entrance signal, then through the next signal back to the road's right side.

sec07-card-r18.front: Which steps take you left onto the freeway through a diverging diamond interchange?
sec07-card-r18.expected_back: For the described diverging diamond highway entry, approach in the left lane, follow it through the entrance signal to the opposite side, cross the bridge and turn left onto the highway.

sec07-card-f10.front: How far does a one-hundred-fifty-car freight train going fifty miles an hour need to stop?
sec07-card-f10.expected_back: In the handbook's stated scenario, a freight train with one hundred fifty cars traveling fifty miles an hour has a stopping distance of seven thousand feet, given as one and one-third miles.

sec07-card-f11.front: What large symbol and letter pair are commonly painted on the lane ahead of a railroad crossing?
sec07-card-f11.expected_back: Railroad approaches are often marked on the pavement with an X and the letters RR.

sec07-card-f12.front: Which white X-shaped sign is posted right at most railroad crossings?
sec07-card-f12.expected_back: Railroad crossbuck signs are found at most crossings.

sec07-card-f13.front: What active warning device is often paired with crossbuck signs on busy roads?
sec07-card-f13.expected_back: Flashing railroad warning lights are often combined with crossbuck signs at busy road crossings.

sec07-card-f16.front: When should you expect a train when approaching any railroad track?
sec07-card-f16.expected_back: Expect a train at any time and approach every railroad crossing carefully.

sec07-card-f26.front: What symbol appears on the common advance warning sign for a roundabout?
sec07-card-f26.expected_back: The common roundabout warning sign shows an arrow in a circular pattern.

sec08-card-f01.front: What does Idaho's basic speed rule require on every road, even where maximum or minimum limits are posted?
sec08-card-f01.expected_back: Idaho's basic speed rule requires a reasonable and prudent speed at all times, including roads with legal or posted maximum and minimum limits.

sec08-card-f02.front: Which road, traffic, and visibility factors must guide how fast you drive?
sec08-card-f02.expected_back: Choose speed with regard to other traffic, pedestrians, bicycles, road surface, intersection hazards, visibility, oncoming traffic and curves.

sec08-card-f03.front: How can driving below the posted speed limit still violate Idaho's basic speed rule?
sec08-card-f03.expected_back: Driving too slowly for existing conditions while impeding safe traffic flow violates the basic speed rule even below the posted limit.

sec08-card-f04.front: What is Idaho's standard maximum speed limit on interstate highways unless posted otherwise?
sec08-card-f04.expected_back: The handbook's interstate maximum is seventy-five miles an hour unless a different limit is posted.

sec08-card-f05.front: When is eighty miles an hour lawful on an Idaho interstate?
sec08-card-f05.expected_back: An interstate limit of eighty miles an hour may be allowed where it is posted.

sec08-card-f06.front: What is the standard state-highway speed limit in Idaho, and what higher limit applies where posted?
sec08-card-f06.expected_back: The stated state-highway maximum is sixty-five miles an hour, with seventy allowed where posted.

sec08-card-f07.front: What is the maximum speed in residential, business, or urban districts unless posted otherwise?
sec08-card-f07.expected_back: The maximum in a residential, business or urban district is thirty-five miles an hour unless posted otherwise.

sec08-card-f08.front: What is the rule against driving unusually slowly in normal traffic?
sec08-card-f08.expected_back: Do not drive so slowly that normal traffic flow is disrupted.

sec08-card-f09.front: What is forbidden when driving in the extreme left lane of a multilane road?
sec08-card-f09.expected_back: Do not remain in the extreme left lane in a way that impedes traffic traveling at a lawful speed.

sec08-card-f10.front: What speed rule applies inside a posted school zone?
sec08-card-f10.expected_back: Obey the posted speed limit in a school zone.

sec08-card-f11.front: What speed rule applies through designated highway work zones?
sec08-card-f11.expected_back: Obey posted speed limits in designated work zones.

sec08-card-f12.front: What financial consequence can follow a work-zone speeding violation?
sec08-card-f12.expected_back: A work-zone speed violation may result in an enhanced fixed penalty.

sec08-card-f14.front: Which traffic sign matches how you must treat a flashing red signal?
sec08-card-f14.expected_back: A flashing red indication requires stopping and is treated like a stop sign.

sec08-card-f15.front: What must you do at a steady red arrow, and when may you turn in that arrow's direction?
sec08-card-f15.expected_back: A steady red arrow requires a stop and forbids a turn in the arrow's direction until a green or yellow indication allows it.

sec08-card-f16.front: Where must your vehicle stop and wait at a steady circular red signal with a stop line?
sec08-card-f16.expected_back: At a steady circular red signal, stop completely and remain behind the stop line.

sec08-card-f17.front: Where must you stop at a steady circular red light if no stop line is painted?
sec08-card-f17.expected_back: If there is no stop line at a steady circular red signal, stop before entering the crosswalk.

sec08-card-f18.front: Which movement is allowed when a green arrow lights up alongside a steady circular red?
sec08-card-f18.expected_back: A green arrow displayed with a steady red indication permits movement only in the green arrow's direction.

sec08-card-f19.front: Apart from a legal turn on red or a lit green arrow, when may you move from a steady circular red?
sec08-card-f19.expected_back: Except for a permitted red-light turn or movement authorized by a green arrow, wait for green before proceeding from a steady circular red.

sec08-card-f20.front: How must you respond to a pedestrian inside either a marked or unmarked intersection crosswalk?
sec08-card-f20.expected_back: At an intersection, stop or slow as needed to yield to a pedestrian within a marked or unmarked crosswalk.

sec08-card-f21.front: Which railway warnings or sights require a driver to stop at a crossing?
sec08-card-f21.expected_back: Stop at a railway crossing for an approaching train or when a wigwag, flashing signal, gate or watchman indicates that a train is approaching.

sec08-card-f22.front: Where must you stop and whom must you yield to when emerging from a driveway, alley, building, or private road?
sec08-card-f22.expected_back: Before joining a street from a private road, driveway, building or alley, stop short of the sidewalk and yield to both pedestrians and other traffic.

sec08-card-f23.front: What must you do whenever a police officer signals or requests you to stop?
sec08-card-f23.expected_back: Stop when a police officer requests it.

sec08-card-f24.front: Where and how long must you stop when an emergency or police vehicle approaches with siren or flashing red-or-blue lights?
sec08-card-f24.expected_back: For an emergency or police vehicle using a siren or flashing red or blue lights, pull to the nearest right edge or curb clear of intersections and stay stopped until it passes or an officer permits movement.

sec08-card-f25.front: What immediate action is required by law if you are involved in a traffic crash?
sec08-card-f25.expected_back: Stop when involved in a crash.

sec08-card-f26.front: When must you stop for a school bus with flashing upper red lights or an extended stop arm, and what is the one highway exception?
sec08-card-f26.expected_back: For a school bus loading or unloading students, stop and remain stopped while its upper red lights flash or its stop arm is extended, except for opposite-direction traffic on a highway with four or more lanes and two lanes in each direction.

sec08-card-f27.front: Once stopped for a school bus, when are you legally allowed to start moving again?
sec08-card-f27.expected_back: A driver who has to stop for a school bus cannot move on until every child is clear of both the bus and the roadway.

sec08-card-f28.front: What exact lane configuration excuses opposite-direction drivers from stopping for a school bus?
sec08-card-f28.expected_back: Opposite-direction traffic need not stop for the school bus on a highway with four or more lanes when two lanes go in each direction.

sec08-card-f29.front: Which two methods let you signal drivers behind you when slowing down or stopping?
sec08-card-f29.expected_back: When slowing or stopping, signal other drivers using the rear brake-operated lights or an arm signal.

sec08-card-f30.front: Which two critical time windows change as your travel speed rises?
sec08-card-f30.expected_back: Travel speed affects the available reaction time and the time needed to stop.

sec08-card-f32.front: What visual landmark tells you that you left a safe gap when stopped behind another car?
sec08-card-f32.expected_back: When stopped behind another vehicle, a safe habit is to leave enough space to see where its rear tires touch the ground.

sec08-card-f33.front: How does leaving the rear-tire gap help if a distracted driver rear-ends your stopped car?
sec08-card-f33.expected_back: Leaving the recommended stopped-vehicle gap may prevent striking the vehicle ahead if another vehicle hits from behind.

sec08-card-f34.front: How does the rear-tire stopped gap help if the vehicle ahead stalls in your lane?
sec08-card-f34.expected_back: The recommended stopped-vehicle gap may provide room to go around a stalled vehicle without backing into a traffic hazard.

sec08-card-r01.front: When shifting lanes or overtaking another vehicle, what must you activate?
sec08-card-r01.expected_back: Use a turn signal when changing lanes or passing another vehicle.

sec08-card-r02.front: What must you do with your turn signal when exiting a roundabout?
sec08-card-r02.expected_back: Use a turn signal when leaving a roundabout.

sec08-card-r03.front: Does turning into a private driveway require a turn signal just like turning at an intersection?
sec08-card-r03.expected_back: Signal a turn at an intersection or into a driveway.

sec08-card-r04.front: When must you use your turn signal on freeway or interstate ramps?
sec08-card-r04.expected_back: Use a turn signal when entering or leaving a freeway or interstate highway.

sec08-card-r05.front: What must you do before pulling from a parked roadside spot into a live travel lane?
sec08-card-r05.expected_back: Signal when pulling from a parked roadside position into the traffic lane.

sec08-card-r06.front: What must you do before pulling over to the side of the road?
sec08-card-r06.expected_back: Signal before pulling over to the side of the road.

sec08-card-r07.front: How far ahead must you signal in a business or residential area, and what exception applies right past an intersection?
sec08-card-r07.expected_back: In a business or residential area, signal at least one hundred feet before a turn or lane change, except that a turn just beyond an intersection is signaled after passing through it.

sec08-card-r08.front: How many seconds ahead must you signal on a freeway or highway, and when do you wait?
sec08-card-r08.expected_back: On a freeway or highway, signal at least five seconds before a turn or lane change, except that a turn just beyond an intersection is signaled after passing through it.

sec08-card-r09.front: When should you turn on your signal if your intended turn sits immediately beyond an intersection?
sec08-card-r09.expected_back: For a turn planned just beyond an intersection, signal after going through that intersection to avoid confusing other drivers.

sec08-card-r10.front: Which two types of turn signals may an Idaho driver legally use?
sec08-card-r10.expected_back: A driver may use electric turn signals or arm signals.

sec08-card-r11.front: Which maneuver is signaled by extending your left arm and hand straight out the window?
sec08-card-r11.expected_back: Extending the arm and hand straight out the window signals a left turn.

sec08-card-r12.front: Which maneuver is signaled by extending your left arm and hand upward out the window?
sec08-card-r12.expected_back: Extending the arm and hand upward out the window signals a right turn.

sec08-card-r13.front: What does extending your left arm and hand downward out the window tell drivers behind you?
sec08-card-r13.expected_back: Extending the arm and hand downward out the window signals slowing or stopping.

sec08-card-r14.front: Which lane and curb position should you take when approaching to make a right turn?
sec08-card-r14.expected_back: For a right turn, signal and approach in the right lane as close to the curb as reasonably possible.

sec08-card-r15.front: Whom must you yield to right before turning right at a corner?
sec08-card-r15.expected_back: Before turning right, yield to pedestrians and vehicles that have the right of way.

sec08-card-r16.front: Where must you check for approaching bicycles before executing a right turn?
sec08-card-r16.expected_back: Before turning right, watch for bicycles approaching between the vehicle's right side and the curb.

sec08-card-r17.front: Into which lane must you complete a right turn, and what steering error must you avoid?
sec08-card-r17.expected_back: Complete a right turn into the cross street's right lane without swinging wide.

sec08-card-r18.front: Which lane should you signal into and approach from for a left turn?
sec08-card-r18.expected_back: For a left turn, signal and approach in the farthest-left lane open to traffic moving in the driver's direction.

sec08-card-r19.front: Where within your lane should you position your vehicle before turning left on a two-lane road?
sec08-card-r19.expected_back: On a two-lane road, a driver preparing to turn left should move to the left side of the current lane.

sec08-card-r20.front: Which two road users must you yield to before turning left?
sec08-card-r20.expected_back: Before a left turn, yield to pedestrians and oncoming vehicles.

sec08-card-r21.front: Which target lane must you enter when completing a left turn, and what shortcut must you avoid?
sec08-card-r21.expected_back: When safe, complete a left turn into the nearest lane carrying traffic in the intended direction without cutting the corner.

sec08-card-r22.front: Under what conditions is a right turn permitted at a steady circular red light?
sec08-card-r22.expected_back: At a steady red light, a right turn may be made after stopping and yielding to cross-traffic and pedestrians with the right of way, unless signs prohibit the turn.

sec08-card-r23.front: Between what kinds of streets may you turn left on a steady circular red light unless posted otherwise?
sec08-card-r23.expected_back: A left turn from a one-way street onto another one-way street may be made on steady red after stopping and yielding to cross-traffic and pedestrians, unless posted otherwise.

sec08-card-r24.front: What does a posted No U-turn sign prohibit?
sec08-card-r24.expected_back: A posted No U-turn sign prohibits making a U-turn.

sec08-card-r25.front: How much clear sight distance in both directions is required to make a U-turn near a curve or hillcrest?
sec08-card-r25.expected_back: Do not make a U-turn on a curve or near or approaching a hillcrest where approaching drivers from either direction cannot see the vehicle within five hundred feet.

sec08-card-r26.front: Are U-turns allowed inside a marked no-passing zone?
sec08-card-r26.expected_back: A U-turn is prohibited in a no-passing zone.

sec08-card-r27.front: What must you do regarding all other traffic before completing a U-turn?
sec08-card-r27.expected_back: Stop and yield to all traffic before completing a U-turn.

sec08-card-r28.front: What do solid painted markings in the center of the road tell you about making a U-turn?
sec08-card-r28.expected_back: Solid markings in the road's center indicate that a U-turn is prohibited.

sec08-card-r29.front: What is the first step in the handbook's permitted U-turn procedure on an open road?
sec08-card-r29.expected_back: For a permitted U-turn using the handbook's procedure, first move to the far-right edge of the road and stop.

sec08-card-r30.front: Where must you check, and how do you steer, once stopped at the right edge for a handbook U-turn?
sec08-card-r30.expected_back: In the handbook’s U-turn procedure, check ahead, behind and the blind spot to the left rear; if the path is clear, signal and steer sharply left at low speed.

sec08-card-r31.front: What two actions complete the handbook's U-turn procedure once your vehicle points in the new direction?
sec08-card-r31.expected_back: Once the vehicle points in the intended direction during the stated U-turn procedure, check behind again and accelerate to traffic speed.

sec08-card-r32.front: Which six driving situations allow an exception to Idaho's general keep-right rule?
sec08-card-r32.memory_hook: Left-turns, passing, slow-lanes, hazards, one-ways, multilanes
sec08-card-r32.expected_back: The general keep-right rule has stated exceptions for left-turn preparation, same-direction passing, a designated slow-traffic lane on a highway with more than two lanes, temporary hazard avoidance, one-way roads and multiple same-direction lanes.

sec08-card-r33.front: How does preparing for a left turn interact with the general keep-far-right rule?
sec08-card-r33.expected_back: Preparing for a left turn is an exception to the general keep-far-right rule.

sec08-card-r34.front: How does overtaking a slower same-direction vehicle affect the keep-far-right rule?
sec08-card-r34.expected_back: Passing another vehicle traveling in the same direction is an exception to the general keep-far-right rule.

sec08-card-r35.front: When does a designated slow-traffic lane create an exception to keeping far right?
sec08-card-r35.expected_back: The keep-far-right rule has an exception on a highway with more than two lanes when the right lane is designated for slow traffic.

sec08-card-r36.front: When may you temporarily enter the left lane on a road normally governed by the keep-far-right rule?
sec08-card-r36.expected_back: Temporarily entering the left lane to avoid an obstruction, pedestrian or animal is an exception to the general keep-far-right rule.

sec08-card-r37.front: Does the general keep-far-right rule apply on a street restricted to one-way traffic?
sec08-card-r37.expected_back: A road restricted to one-way traffic is an exception to the general keep-far-right rule.

sec08-card-r38.front: How many lanes moving in your direction make a road an exception to the keep-far-right rule?
sec08-card-r38.expected_back: A road with at least two lanes moving in the same direction is an exception to the general keep-far-right rule.

sec08-card-r40.front: When must motor vehicles yield to a pedestrian at an intersection crosswalk?
sec08-card-r40.expected_back: Motor vehicles must yield to a pedestrian within a marked or unmarked intersection crosswalk.

sec08-card-r41.front: Who holds the right-of-way when a vehicle enters a street from an alley or driveway?
sec08-card-r41.expected_back: A vehicle entering a street from an alley or driveway must yield to pedestrians.

sec08-card-r42.front: How do you identify a blind pedestrian to whom motor vehicles must always yield?
sec08-card-r42.expected_back: Motor vehicles must yield to a blind pedestrian walking with a white cane or a guide dog.

sec08-card-r43.front: Who must yield when a pedestrian crosses away from both a crosswalk and an intersection?
sec08-card-r43.expected_back: A pedestrian crossing away from both a crosswalk and an intersection must yield to motor vehicles.

sec08-card-r44.front: When must a pedestrian at an intersection yield to motor vehicles?
sec08-card-r44.expected_back: A pedestrian must yield to motor vehicles when an intersection or crosswalk signal directs that yielding.

sec08-card-r45.front: Which three actions apply when approaching a Yield sign?
sec08-card-r45.expected_back: When approaching a Yield sign, slow down, be ready to stop and yield to other drivers.

sec08-card-r46.front: After stopping at an alley, driveway, or garage exit, what must you do before pulling onto the street?
sec08-card-r46.expected_back: After stopping to enter a street from an alley, driveway or garage, yield to other drivers.

sec08-card-r47.front: After coming to a full stop at a two-way stop intersection, whom must you yield to?
sec08-card-r47.expected_back: After stopping at a two-way stop, yield to cross-traffic.

sec08-card-r48.front: Who has the right-of-way when vehicles arrive at different times at a four-way stop?
sec08-card-r48.expected_back: At a four-way stop, the first vehicle to arrive has the right of way.

sec08-card-r49.front: Who yields when two vehicles reach a four-way stop at the exact same moment?
sec08-card-r49.expected_back: If two vehicles reach a four-way stop together, the vehicle on the left must yield to the one on the right.

sec08-card-r50.front: Who must yield when two drivers arrive simultaneously at an intersection with no signs or signals?
sec08-card-r50.expected_back: At an intersection with no signs or signals, simultaneous arrivals require the driver on the left to yield to the driver on the right.

sec08-card-r51.front: What must a driver on the ending street do at an uncontrolled T-intersection before turning left or right?
sec08-card-r51.expected_back: At an uncontrolled T-intersection where the driver must turn left or right, the handbook requires stopping, yielding, or both for traffic approaching from the other two directions.

sec08-card-f13.front: Where are vehicle racing, speed exhibitions, and speed contests illegal in Idaho?
sec08-card-f13.expected_back: Vehicle racing, speed exhibitions and speed contests are illegal on public roads, streets and highways.

sec08-card-f31.front: Which three kinds of problems combine dangerously with excessive speed to cause crashes?
sec08-card-f31.expected_back: The handbook warns that excessive speed contributes to crashes and can combine dangerously with other violations, mechanical failures or judgment errors.

sec08-card-r39.front: How does the Idaho handbook frame right-of-way between giving it and taking it?
sec08-card-r39.expected_back: The handbook describes right of way as something drivers give rather than take.

sec09-card-f09.front: Where do hills, curves, and roadside obstructions forbid passing on a two-lane road?
sec09-card-f09.expected_back: Do not pass on a two-lane road at or near a hill, curve or obstruction that blocks the view of potentially hazardous oncoming vehicles.

sec09-card-f10.front: Unless traffic controls permit it, within how many feet of an intersection is passing banned?
sec09-card-f10.expected_back: Passing within one hundred feet of an intersection is prohibited unless traffic-control devices indicate otherwise.

sec09-card-f11.front: Within what distance of a railroad crossing is overtaking prohibited unless traffic controls say otherwise?
sec09-card-f11.expected_back: Passing within one hundred feet of a railroad crossing is prohibited unless traffic-control devices indicate otherwise.

sec09-card-f12.front: What visibility condition bars overtaking within 100 feet of any bridge or tunnel?
sec09-card-f12.expected_back: Do not pass within one hundred feet of a bridge or tunnel when the view is obstructed.

sec09-card-f13.front: Is overtaking allowed when a stopped school bus is loading or unloading passengers?
sec09-card-f13.expected_back: Do not overtake a school bus stopped to load or unload passengers.

sec09-card-f14.front: Why must you never overtake a vehicle stopped ahead at a marked or unmarked crosswalk?
sec09-card-f14.expected_back: Do not pass a vehicle that has stopped ahead at a marked or unmarked crosswalk to let a pedestrian cross.

sec09-card-f15.front: Is a pass ever lawful if completing it forces your wheels off the pavement or roadway?
sec09-card-f15.expected_back: A pass that requires leaving the pavement or roadway is prohibited.

sec09-card-f04.front: Which two vehicles must your passing maneuver avoid interfering with?
sec09-card-f04.expected_back: Pass only when the maneuver will not interfere with oncoming traffic or the vehicle being overtaken.

sec09-card-f05.front: What certainty must you have before pulling out to overtake?
sec09-card-f05.expected_back: Wait to pass until certain there is enough time to complete it safely.

sec09-card-f06.front: What signal and mirror check come before steering back into your original lane after passing?
sec09-card-f06.expected_back: Before returning to the original lane after a pass, signal and wait until the overtaken vehicle is visible in the rear-view mirror.

sec09-card-f07.front: What is the safest move if you realize mid-pass that you cannot finish safely?
sec09-card-f07.expected_back: If a pass cannot be completed safely after it begins, fall back and wait for another opening.

sec09-card-f08.front: Even outside No Passing signs or solid stripes, who holds final responsibility for judging a safe pass?
sec09-card-f08.expected_back: Passing signs and pavement markings identify prohibited or unsafe locations, but the driver must still determine whether a pass is safe.

sec09-card-f16.front: Under what exact road, vehicle, towing, zone, and return rules does Idaho allow exceeding the limit by up to fifteen miles per hour to pass?
sec09-card-f16.expected_back: A passenger vehicle or pickup that is not towing may pass a vehicle traveling below the posted limit on a two-lane road posted at least fifty-five miles an hour by exceeding that limit by at most fifteen miles an hour outside a work zone, then returning to the right lane and the posted limit as soon as practicable.

sec09-card-f17.front: When is passing on the right allowed on a two-lane two-way road?
sec09-card-f17.expected_back: On a two-lane two-way road, passing on the right is allowed only when the vehicle ahead signals a left turn and the move is safe without leaving the roadway.

sec09-card-f18.front: When may you pass on the right on a one-way or multilane street?
sec09-card-f18.expected_back: On a one-way or multilane street with at least two lanes in the driver's direction, passing on the right is allowed only if safe and without leaving the roadway.

sec09-card-f19.front: Why must you check mirrors and blind spots before pulling left to overtake?
sec09-card-f19.expected_back: Before moving left to pass, check mirrors and blind spots for another vehicle that may already be trying to pass.

sec09-card-f20.front: What communication step precedes steering into the left lane to pass?
sec09-card-f20.expected_back: Signal left before moving into the left lane to pass.

sec09-card-f21.front: Walk through the exact mirror and signal sequence for returning to the right lane after overtaking?
sec09-card-f21.expected_back: After overtaking, wait until the passed vehicle appears in the rear-view mirror, then signal right before returning to the right lane.

sec09-card-f22.front: How should you respond if the vehicle you are overtaking begins drifting toward your lane?
sec09-card-f22.expected_back: Use the horn if the vehicle being passed starts drifting toward the passing vehicle.

sec09-card-f23.front: How much distance ahead of an oncoming vehicle must remain when you finish a pass?
sec09-card-f23.memory_hook: Clear lane before two hundred feet
sec09-card-f23.expected_back: Finish a pass before reaching a point within two hundred feet of oncoming traffic.

sec09-card-f24.front: Where must your pass be completely finished relative to an upcoming No Passing zone?
sec09-card-f24.expected_back: Complete a pass before entering a No Passing zone identified by signs or pavement markings.

sec09-card-f25.front: Where inside your lane should you ease when another driver overtakes you, and why?
sec09-card-f25.expected_back: When another vehicle passes, move toward the right side of the current lane to provide more room and a better view ahead.

sec09-card-f26.front: What speed rule applies to your right foot while another vehicle is overtaking you?
sec09-card-f26.expected_back: Do not accelerate while being passed; keep a steady speed or reduce it.

sec09-card-f27.front: Why should you stay alert to the overtaking driver's progress while being passed?
sec09-card-f27.expected_back: While being passed, watch for the other driver's misjudgment because a quick response can reduce crash risk.

sec09-card-r01.front: When, if ever, may an uninvited motorist join or drive between vehicles in a funeral procession?
sec09-card-r01.memory_hook: Never cut in unless police direct
sec09-card-r01.expected_back: Do not join a funeral procession or drive between its vehicles unless a police officer authorizes it.

sec09-card-r02.front: When is passing a funeral procession in the right lane allowed on a multilane highway?
sec09-card-r02.expected_back: On a multilane highway, do not pass a funeral procession in the right lane unless the procession occupies the farthest-left lane.

sec09-card-r03.front: May you drive through an intersection across an active funeral procession when your traffic signal turns green?
sec09-card-r03.expected_back: Do not enter an intersection across a funeral procession's path while it is passing through, regardless of the traffic signal's color.

sec09-card-r04.front: Who holds the right-of-way when you encounter a funeral procession in Idaho?
sec09-card-r04.expected_back: Give funeral processions the right of way.

sec09-card-r05.front: Which exterior lights must every vehicle inside a funeral procession turn on?
sec09-card-r05.expected_back: Every funeral-procession vehicle must use its headlights and taillights.

sec09-card-r06.front: How do the first and last vehicles in an Idaho funeral procession mark the line's start and finish?
sec09-card-r06.expected_back: The first and last vehicles in a funeral procession must also flash warning lights to mark its endpoints.

sec09-card-r07.front: How many delayed trailing vehicles require a slow driver on a rural or two-lane highway to pull off?
sec09-card-r07.expected_back: A vehicle below normal traffic speed that delays at least three vehicles in a rural area or on a two-lane highway must pull off wherever safe to let them pass.

sec09-card-r08.front: During what daylight window may vehicles capped at twenty-five miles per hour use public highways, and what exception applies?
sec09-card-r08.expected_back: A vehicle designed for no more than twenty-five miles an hour may use public highways only from thirty minutes before sunrise to thirty minutes after sunset, except snow-removal or farm equipment on non-interstate highways with flashing lights visible for five hundred feet.

sec09-card-r09.front: Which two controls and rear marker must slow-moving vehicles carry?
sec09-card-r09.expected_back: Slow-moving vehicles must have a foot brake and turn signals and display the approved slow-vehicle emblem.

sec09-card-r10.front: What does tailgating mean, and how does it rank among collision causes?
sec09-card-r10.expected_back: Tailgating means following too closely and is a common cause of crashes.

sec09-card-r11.front: What basic stopping standard governs how much space you leave behind the car ahead?
sec09-card-r11.expected_back: When following another car, leave enough space to stop when needed.

sec09-card-r12.front: What mechanical system must stay in good working order for your following gap to protect you?
sec09-card-r12.expected_back: Keep the brakes in good working condition when relying on a following gap.

sec09-card-r13.front: Why should you know and test brake feel across changing surfaces, especially wet, icy, or snowy pavement?
sec09-card-r13.expected_back: Know the brakes' stopping performance in different conditions and test them often, especially on wet, icy or snowy roads.

sec09-card-r14.front: What minimum following interval does the Idaho handbook recommend, and when do you add more?
sec09-card-r14.expected_back: The handbook's minimum recommended following interval is three seconds, with more distance needed at high speeds or in bad weather.

sec09-card-r15.front: What kind of roadside marker do you pick to run the three-second following check?
sec09-card-r15.expected_back: For the recommended following-gap check, select a stationary reference ahead of the lead vehicle, such as a tree or roadside sign.

sec09-card-r16.front: At what exact moment do you start counting your three-second following check?
sec09-card-r16.expected_back: Begin counting three seconds when the vehicle ahead passes the chosen object.

sec09-card-r17.front: How long should your count take before reaching the reference object in good weather versus bad weather?
sec09-card-r17.expected_back: In the handbook's reference-object check, the interval before reaching the object should be at least three seconds and several times longer in bad weather.

sec09-card-r18.front: Why should you preserve open space on all sides of your vehicle, not only ahead?
sec09-card-r18.expected_back: Maintain space around the vehicle on all sides to provide time to react to danger.

sec09-card-r19.front: Where within your lane should you track, and what two options should your front space preserve?
sec09-card-r19.expected_back: Stay near the center of the lane and leave enough space ahead to stop or pass safely.

sec09-card-r20.front: What is the calmest way to handle a driver following your rear bumper too closely?
sec09-card-r20.expected_back: If another vehicle follows too closely, slow down and allow it to pass.

sec09-card-r21.front: How close and in what orientation must you park along a public curb or road edge?
sec09-card-r21.expected_back: On a public road, park parallel to and within eighteen inches of the curb or road edge, facing the traffic direction on that side.

sec09-card-r22.front: Which transmission setting secures a parked automatic vehicle versus a manual-shift vehicle?
sec09-card-r22.expected_back: For a parked vehicle with an automatic transmission, shift to Park; for a manual transmission, leave it in gear.

sec09-card-r23.front: What final anti-theft and safety step applies every time you leave a parked vehicle?
sec09-card-r23.expected_back: Remove the keys and secure the parked vehicle.

sec09-card-f01.front: Unless a green arrow or sign directs otherwise, whom must a left-turning driver yield to?
sec09-card-f01.expected_back: A left-turning driver must yield to oncoming intersection traffic unless a traffic-control device directs otherwise.

sec09-card-f02.front: Whom must motorists yield to inside an active highway construction zone?
sec09-card-f02.expected_back: In a work zone, yield to vehicles and pedestrians working on the highway construction project.

sec09-card-f03.front: Which intersection rules govern traffic when a signal goes dark during a power outage?
sec09-card-f03.expected_back: If a traffic light fails during a power outage, apply the yielding rules of a four-way stop.

sec10-card-f04.front: What rule applies to parking on a sidewalk or inside a dedicated bicycle lane?
sec10-card-f04.expected_back: Parking in a bicycle lane or on a sidewalk is prohibited.

sec10-card-f05.front: What violation occurs when you park alongside the street-facing side of an already parked car?
sec10-card-f05.expected_back: Parking beside the street-facing side of another parked vehicle is prohibited double parking.

sec10-card-f06.front: Is parking ever allowed inside an intersection?
sec10-card-f06.expected_back: Do not park in an intersection.

sec10-card-f07.front: Within how many feet of railroad tracks is parking prohibited?
sec10-card-f07.expected_back: Do not park within fifty feet of railroad tracks.

sec10-card-f08.front: Where on bridges and overpasses is parking allowed?
sec10-card-f08.expected_back: Parking on a bridge or overpass is prohibited.

sec10-card-f09.front: What parking rule protects driveway entrances?
sec10-card-f09.expected_back: Do not park in front of a driveway.

sec10-card-f10.front: How much curb space around a fire hydrant must stay completely clear of parked vehicles?
sec10-card-f10.expected_back: Leave at least the prohibited fifteen-foot area around a fire hydrant free of parked vehicles.

sec10-card-f11.front: Within what distance of a crosswalk is parking prohibited?
sec10-card-f11.expected_back: Do not park within twenty feet of a crosswalk.

sec10-card-f12.front: How far back from a stop sign, yield sign, or traffic signal is parking barred?
sec10-card-f12.expected_back: Parking is barred within thirty feet of a stop sign, yield sign or traffic signal.

sec10-card-f13.front: What no-parking distance applies beside a fire-station driveway?
sec10-card-f13.expected_back: Keep parked vehicles out of the twenty-foot area by a fire-station driveway.

sec10-card-f14.front: May you park along a freeway or other controlled-access highway for non-emergencies?
sec10-card-f14.expected_back: Do not park on a controlled-access highway, including a freeway.

sec10-card-f15.front: What do a no-parking sign or a red-painted curb indicate in Idaho?
sec10-card-f15.expected_back: A prohibitory parking sign or red-painted curb means parking is not allowed there.

sec10-card-f01.front: Which way must you turn your front wheels when parking downhill?
sec10-card-f01.expected_back: When parking downhill, turn the front wheels sharply toward the curb or road edge to help prevent rolling into traffic.

sec10-card-f02.front: Which way do front wheels point when parking uphill next to a curb?
sec10-card-f02.expected_back: When parking uphill with a curb, point the front wheels sharply away from the curb.

sec10-card-f03.front: How do you angle your wheels when parking uphill where no curb exists?
sec10-card-f03.expected_back: When parking uphill where there is no curb, turn the wheels sharply toward the road's edge.

sec10-card-f16.front: What vehicle credential is required to use disability-reserved stalls, and what faces unauthorized drivers?
