sec03-card-r32.teaching_text: Correctional escorts follow the same three exception checkpoints of age eighteen, valid identification, and a signed liability waiver.

sec03-card-r33.question_text: Under what conditions may a religious missionary companion ride along on a skills test when requested?
sec03-card-r33.teaching_text: Missionaries whose rules require a companion can bring one along once age eighteen, valid ID, and waiver rules are met.

sec03-card-r43.question_text: What road environments and maneuvers are included on an Idaho skills test?
sec03-card-r43.teaching_text: Expect city streets, curves, freeway merges, lane shifts, parking lots, turns, U-turns, and both stall and curb parking.

sec03-card-r44.question_text: Which nine driving fundamentals make up Idaho's skills-test scoring rubric?
sec03-card-r44.teaching_text: Examiners grade car control, scanning, space cushions, blinkers, speed, braking, lane placement, parking, and yielding throughout the drive.

sec03-card-r52.question_text: Which intersection types, crossings, and circular junctions are included in the skills test?
sec03-card-r52.teaching_text: Practicing controlled and uncontrolled intersections alongside railroad tracks and roundabouts keeps complex right-of-way spots stress-free.

sec03-card-r53.question_text: How is any dangerous action during the skills test classified?
sec03-card-r53.teaching_text: Putting nearby drivers, pedestrians, or cabin occupants in danger triggers an automatic fail regardless of your point tally.

sec03-card-r54.question_text: What happens on your skills score if you disobey an emergency or safety vehicle?
sec03-card-r54.teaching_text: Failing to pull right and stop for sirens or flashing safety rigs ends your road evaluation on the spot.

sec03-card-r55.question_text: How is disobeying police or safety personnel classified during the skills test?
sec03-card-r55.teaching_text: Human directions from police officers or work-zone safety personnel override lights and signs, so ignoring them fails instantly.

sec03-card-r56.question_text: How is ignoring a traffic sign or traffic light scored on the skills test?
sec03-card-r56.teaching_text: Blowing past a stop octagon, yield triangle, or red traffic light immediately ends your skills evaluation.

sec03-card-r57.question_text: How is driving onto a curb or sidewalk scored during the skills test?
sec03-card-r57.teaching_text: Clipping or climbing a curb on a tight corner or parking pull-in crosses into pedestrian space and fails automatically.

sec03-card-r58.question_text: What happens if the examiner has to intervene or you disobey the examiner during the skills test?
sec03-card-r58.teaching_text: Forcing the examiner to grab the wheel or give a corrective safety warning ends the road evaluation immediately.

sec03-card-r59.question_text: How does Idaho classify committing a lane violation during the skills test?
sec03-card-r59.teaching_text: Turning into the wrong lane, straddling solid lines, or drifting across centerlines counts as an automatic-fail critical error.

sec03-card-r60.question_text: What happens if an authorized passenger interferes during the skills test?
sec03-card-r60.teaching_text: Even a parent or translator riding legally must stay out of driving decisions, because coaching or gesturing fails the drive.

sec03-card-r61.question_text: How is speeding scored during an Idaho skills test?
sec03-card-r61.teaching_text: Creeping above posted school, residential, or highway limits is not a one-point deduction—it ends your road evaluation.

sec03-card-r62.question_text: How is striking any object classified during the skills test?
sec03-card-r62.teaching_text: Bumping a parking cone, fence post, or parked bumper during maneuvers triggers an immediate critical failure.

sec03-card-r63.question_text: What condition must the windshield meet on a skills-test vehicle?
sec03-card-r63.teaching_text: Spiderweb cracks or dangling mirror charms across the windshield can disqualify your car before the road route starts.

sec03-card-r64.question_text: What mirror setup must a vehicle have to qualify for the skills test?
sec03-card-r64.teaching_text: Missing an interior center mirror is fine only when both left and right exterior mirrors are intact.

sec03-card-r65.question_text: What rule applies to critical dashboard warning lights or gauges on a skills-test vehicle?
sec03-card-r65.teaching_text: Glowing brake, airbag, overheating, or oil alerts signal mechanical trouble and prevent the examiner from taking the car out.

sec03-card-r66.question_text: What caution does the handbook give about third-party online practice quizzes versus ITD's website samples?
sec03-card-r66.teaching_text: Generic websites often mix in other states' numbers, whereas ITD's own website sample items match Idaho's handbook rules.

sec04-card-f02.question_text: What rule applies to driving a mechanically unsafe vehicle in Idaho?
sec04-card-f02.teaching_text: Taking a car onto public streets with failing brakes, steering, or tires puts everyone around you at immediate risk.

sec04-card-f03.question_text: Who is responsible for fixing dangerous defects, missing required equipment, or needed vehicle repairs?
sec04-card-f03.teaching_text: Blaming a prior owner or skipped shop visit will not shield the driver when required safety gear is missing.

sec04-card-f06.question_text: Why must an Idaho motor vehicle have two independent brake systems?
sec04-card-f06.teaching_text: Keeping hydraulic service brakes separate from the mechanical parking brake leaves you stopping power if one system fails.

sec04-card-f07.question_text: Within how many feet must the foot brake stop a vehicle going twenty miles per hour on dry pavement?
sec04-card-f07.teaching_text: Taking longer than twenty-five feet from twenty miles per hour on dry asphalt signals worn pads or weak hydraulics.

sec04-card-f08.question_text: Within how many feet must the emergency or parking brake stop a car from twenty miles per hour on dry pavement?
sec04-card-f08.teaching_text: Compare twenty-five feet on the foot pedal with fifty-five feet on the backup brake—exam traps love swapping them.

sec04-card-f09.question_text: What stationary holding test must a vehicle's parking brake meet on sloped ground?
sec04-card-f09.teaching_text: Relying only on the transmission pawl on steep grades invites rollaway crashes when a weak parking cable slips.

sec04-card-f10.question_text: How many headlamps does a vehicle need, and which beam settings must they provide?
sec04-card-f10.teaching_text: Driving one-eyed or missing either beam mode leaves oncoming drivers guessing your width and cuts night visibility.

sec04-card-f11.question_text: How must headlamps light the roadway ahead with respect to oncoming drivers?
sec04-card-f11.teaching_text: Misaligned lamps aimed too high blind approaching traffic right when two vehicles close on each other after dark.

sec04-card-f12.question_text: At least how far ahead must high beams reveal people and vehicles?
sec04-card-f12.teaching_text: Spotting deer, walkers, or unlit cars three hundred fifty feet out gives stopping room on dark rural highways.

sec04-card-f13.question_text: At least how many feet of roadway ahead must low-beam headlights illuminate?
sec04-card-f13.teaching_text: Even dipped for oncoming traffic, low beams must still light at least one hundred feet ahead of your bumper.

sec04-card-f14.question_text: What types of covers or materials must never be placed over vehicle headlights?
sec04-card-f14.teaching_text: Blackout tints, mirrored films, and non-transparent covers choke beam output when you need crisp night illumination most.

sec04-card-f15.question_text: What colors are permitted for brake lights, and from how far behind must they show in normal sunlight?
sec04-card-f15.teaching_text: Bright red or amber stop lamps visible one hundred feet back in daylight give following drivers instant braking cues.

sec04-card-f16.question_text: When must a motor vehicle's brake lights turn on?
sec04-card-f16.teaching_text: A faulty brake-pedal switch leaves trailing traffic with zero warning that your vehicle is slowing down.

sec04-card-f18.question_text: How many red rear lamps are needed on a car manufactured prior to nineteen fifty-six?
sec04-card-f18.teaching_text: Classic pre-nineteen-fifty-six cars were manufactured with a single rear lamp, so Idaho preserves a one-lamp rule for them.

sec04-card-f19.question_text: For passenger vehicles built on or after January first, nineteen fifty-six, what red rear lights and visibility distance apply?
sec04-card-f19.teaching_text: One red lamp on each rear corner visible five hundred feet back outlines your car's full lane width.

sec04-card-f20.question_text: What electric turn-signal setup and visibility distance apply to motor vehicles built after January first, nineteen fifty-five?
sec04-card-f20.teaching_text: Driver-controlled flashing left and right blinkers front and rear must show clearly from one hundred feet away.

sec04-card-f21.question_text: Which two colors are legal for front electric turn signals on vehicles built after January first, nineteen fifty-five?
sec04-card-f21.teaching_text: Restricting front turn blinkers to white or amber prevents oncoming traffic from confusing your front end with taillights.

sec04-card-f22.question_text: Which two colors are legal for rear electric turn signals on vehicles built after January first, nineteen fifty-five?
sec04-card-f22.teaching_text: White lights at the rear mean reverse, so rear turn blinkers stick strictly to red or amber.

sec04-card-f23.question_text: At least how much tread depth should every tire on your vehicle keep?
sec04-card-f23.teaching_text: Shallow tread under two thirty-seconds of an inch loses water-channeling grooves and hydroplanes fast on wet Idaho pavement.

sec04-card-f24.question_text: From at least how many feet away must a motor vehicle's horn be audible?
sec04-card-f24.teaching_text: A working horn heard two hundred feet away warns drifting drivers or distracted pedestrians before paths cross.

sec04-card-f25.question_text: What rule governs horns that make an unreasonably loud or harsh noise?
sec04-card-f25.teaching_text: Train-blast air horns or screeching novelty horns startle nearby drivers rather than giving a clear safety alert.

sec04-card-f26.question_text: What kind of glass must be used in vehicle windows and windshields?
sec04-card-f26.teaching_text: Approved automotive safety glass resists shattering into jagged household shards during rock strikes or crashes.

sec04-card-f27.question_text: When must damaged window or windshield glass be replaced?
sec04-card-f27.teaching_text: Once cracks, pitting, or star breaks cut across your sightline, replacing the damaged pane becomes mandatory.

sec04-card-f28.question_text: Which decals or posters are permitted on vehicle windows and windshields?
sec04-card-f28.teaching_text: Extra decals and posters create blind spots on glass where cyclists or pedestrians can vanish.

sec04-card-f29.question_text: What restriction applies to items placed on the dash or hung inside the cabin?
sec04-card-f29.teaching_text: Oversized air fresheners, plush charms, or dash clutter swing across your sightline right when someone steps off a curb.

sec04-card-f30.question_text: What weather and road buildup must be cleared off vehicle glass?
sec04-card-f30.teaching_text: Peeking through a tiny scraped porthole leaves intersections and blind spots completely hidden behind frost or mud.

sec04-card-f31.question_text: What visual effects are prohibited for window and windshield tint or treatments, even when viewed from outside?
sec04-card-f31.teaching_text: Reflective or overly dark glass blocks eye contact at four-way stops and hides cabin visibility from officers outside.

sec04-card-f32.question_text: What weather-clearing equipment does every motor vehicle need on its windshield?
sec04-card-f32.teaching_text: Streaking or dead wipers turn sudden mountain rain or wet snow into an instant whiteout across your glass.

sec04-card-f33.question_text: At least how far behind the vehicle must a rear-view mirror show the highway?
sec04-card-f33.teaching_text: Seeing two hundred feet behind lets you judge fast-closing highway traffic before signaling a lane change.

sec04-card-f34.question_text: What extra mirrors are required when cargo or a towed trailer blocks the normal rear-window view?
sec04-card-f34.teaching_text: Hauling a tall camper or stacked cargo blinds your center mirror, making both left and right side mirrors essential.

sec04-card-f35.question_text: What mirror equipment is required on a vehicle that lacks an interior rear-view mirror?
sec04-card-f35.teaching_text: Box vans and utility rigs without an inside center mirror rely on dual exterior mirrors to cover rear lanes.

sec04-card-r01.question_text: Children of what age must ride in approved child safety seats in non-commercial cars?
sec04-card-r01.teaching_text: Adult lap and shoulder straps ride dangerously high on small frames until children outgrow the six-and-under rule.

sec04-card-r02.question_text: Which safety benchmark must an approved child safety seat meet?
sec04-card-r02.teaching_text: Checking for the federal compliance label confirms the carrier passed crash-impact testing rather than acting as a booster prop.

sec04-card-r03.question_text: How must a child fit inside the child safety seat's own harness straps?
sec04-card-r03.teaching_text: Slack harness webbing lets a child slide or eject forward during sudden hard braking.

sec04-card-r04.question_text: Besides strapping the child in snugly, how must the safety seat itself be positioned?
sec04-card-r04.teaching_text: Even a snug five-point harness cannot protect a toddler if the shell itself is sitting loose on the bench.

sec04-card-r05.question_text: How often must a required child safety seat be used when driving with a young child?
sec04-card-r05.teaching_text: Many neighborhood collisions happen minutes from home, so short grocery runs still require buckling the child seat.

sec04-card-r06.question_text: Which two guides does the handbook recommend reading for child-seat height, weight, and installation rules?
sec04-card-r06.teaching_text: Pairing the seat maker's weight limits with your car manual's anchor positions avoids hidden installation mistakes.

sec04-card-r07.question_text: For children younger than what age does the handbook recommend riding in the rear seat?
sec04-card-r07.teaching_text: Keeping kids twelve and under in the back row shields growing bones from front-impact forces and airbags.

sec04-card-r08.question_text: Where must you never place a rear-facing child safety seat?
sec04-card-r08.teaching_text: An inflating front airbag strikes the back of a rear-facing infant carrier with devastating force.

sec04-card-r09.question_text: Which safety belts and shoulder straps does Idaho law require vehicle occupants to wear?
sec04-card-r09.teaching_text: Every rider must fasten both the lap strap and shoulder harness originally installed for their seating position.

sec04-card-r18.question_text: During what daily period must headlamps and taillamps be turned on?
sec04-card-r18.teaching_text: Running full headlights and taillights from sunset until sunrise ensures drivers spot you from ahead and behind.

sec04-card-r19.question_text: Besides sunset to sunrise, when else must you switch on headlamps and taillamps?
sec04-card-r19.teaching_text: Daytime fog, smoke, blowing snow, or heavy rain hides gray cars unless headlights and taillights are switched on.

sec04-card-r20.question_text: How many feet before meeting an oncoming vehicle must you dim your high-beam headlights?
sec04-card-r20.teaching_text: Dropping to low beams five hundred feet out stops your high beams from blinding the driver heading toward you.

sec04-card-r21.question_text: How many feet before overtaking another vehicle from behind must you dim your headlights?
sec04-card-r21.teaching_text: High beams within two hundred feet bounce straight off the lead car's mirrors and blind the driver ahead.

sec04-card-r22.question_text: May you drive using only parking lights whenever driving conditions require lights?
sec04-card-r22.teaching_text: Dim amber corner markers neither light the pavement ahead nor warn fast traffic in dusk or fog.

sec04-card-r24.question_text: What two things must passengers and cargo never do inside a moving vehicle?
sec04-card-r24.teaching_text: Piling boxes high or crowding the driver's elbows compromises both sightlines and emergency steering or braking.

sec04-card-r25.question_text: What daytime warning marker is required when a load extends four feet or more past the rear of a vehicle?
sec04-card-r25.teaching_text: Long lumber or pipe blends into pavement depth perception unless a bright red marker hangs on its tip.

sec04-card-r26.question_text: At least what dimensions must the red daytime flag have on a load projecting four feet or more behind?
sec04-card-r26.teaching_text: Tying a tiny ribbon onto protruding lumber falls short because Idaho requires an eighteen-inch-square red warning cloth.

sec04-card-r27.question_text: What replaces the daytime red cloth at night on a load projecting four feet or more behind, and from what distance must it show?
sec04-card-r27.teaching_text: Cloth markers disappear in darkness, so night hauling swaps in a red lamp visible five hundred feet back.

sec04-card-r28.question_text: How far is a vehicle's load allowed to stick out past the left-side fenders?
sec04-card-r28.teaching_text: Left-side cargo sits right next to oncoming centerline traffic, so zero projection past the left fenders is allowed.

sec04-card-r29.question_text: Up to how many inches may a vehicle's load extend beyond the right-side fenders?
sec04-card-r29.teaching_text: Contrast zero inches on the left with at most six inches past the right fenders—a classic DMV pair.

sec04-card-r30.question_text: On which surfaces does Idaho ban reckless driving showing willful disregard for safety?
sec04-card-r30.teaching_text: Doing donuts or stunt speeding in a private shopping lot still triggers reckless-driving charges just like public highways.

sec04-card-r31.question_text: How much attention must an Idaho driver give to operating the vehicle safely?
sec04-card-r31.teaching_text: Splitting focus with cabin distractions, food, or screens steals the reaction seconds needed when traffic stops ahead.

sec04-card-r32.question_text: What citation can follow if a driver fails to pay proper attention to safe vehicle operation?
sec04-card-r32.teaching_text: Drifting or reacting late from distraction exposes you to an Idaho inattentive-driving citation even without a crash.

sec04-card-r33.question_text: Where does the handbook tell you to check when installing a child seat with a seat belt or LATCH?
sec04-card-r33.teaching_text: Both manuals spell out whether a given seating position uses lower anchors or belt routing and top tethers.

sec04-card-r34.question_text: What do the five letters in the child-restraint acronym LATCH stand for?
sec04-card-r34.teaching_text: Built-in lower anchor bars and upper tether hooks let parents clip compatible child seats directly to the frame.

sec04-card-r35.question_text: Why does ITD sometimes adjust the seasonal dates for studded snow tires?
sec04-card-r35.teaching_text: Early fall blizzards or lingering spring mountain ice can prompt ITD to extend legal studded-tire windows.

sec04-card-f01.question_text: What crime grade applies to joyriding someone's car without consent for temporary use rather than theft?
sec04-card-f01.teaching_text: Taking a car without permission—even intending to bring it right back—still carries criminal misdemeanor charges.

sec04-card-f04.question_text: Does Idaho require motor vehicles to pass a yearly state safety inspection?
sec04-card-f04.teaching_text: Because no annual shop sticker checks your car automatically, keeping brakes, tires, and lights roadworthy stays on you.

sec04-card-f05.question_text: What may a law-enforcement officer do if a stopped vehicle has unsafe conditions or missing required equipment?
sec04-card-f05.teaching_text: Skipping annual inspections does not make broken lights or bald tires free—officers cite unsafe vehicles during stops.

sec04-card-f17.question_text: How should you maintain your vehicle's brake-light lenses?
sec04-card-f17.teaching_text: Road salt, slush, and mud cake over tail housings quickly, dimming your stop lamps right when roads turn slick.

sec04-card-f36.question_text: What exhaust equipment must every motor vehicle carry to control noise?
sec04-card-f36.teaching_text: Rusted-out or straight-piped exhausts violate Idaho's requirement for a working muffler that stops unusual or loud noise.

sec04-card-f37.question_text: Why must cars and towed trailers carry fenders, flaps, or wheel covers?
sec04-card-f37.teaching_text: Uncovered spinning tires hurl gravel, slush, and water straight into trailing windshields without proper fenders or mudflaps.

sec04-card-f38.question_text: What rear red lamps must a trailer manufactured from nineteen fifty-six onward carry?
sec04-card-f38.teaching_text: Towed trailers match modern passenger cars with one red lamp on each side visible five hundred feet behind.

sec04-card-r10.question_text: Besides crash protection, how do safety belts help the driver on rough, winding roads or sudden swerves?
sec04-card-r10.teaching_text: Staying anchored behind the wheel keeps your hands and feet squarely on controls during sharp swerves or washboard bumps.

sec04-card-r11.question_text: Which vehicles are the only ones allowed to carry red and blue emergency lights?
sec04-card-r11.teaching_text: Mounting red or blue strobes on a personal pickup or sedan impersonates emergency responders and is strictly barred.

sec04-card-r12.question_text: Which three audible warning devices are prohibited on ordinary motor vehicles?
sec04-card-r12.teaching_text: Reserving sirens, bells, and whistles away from everyday cars keeps emergency response signals unmistakable in traffic.

sec04-card-r13.question_text: What rule applies to a muffler cutout or bypass that boosts exhaust noise?
sec04-card-r13.teaching_text: Valves or bypass pipes that route exhaust around the muffler to roar louder are illegal on Idaho roads.

sec04-card-r14.question_text: At most how many spotlights may a motor vehicle have?
sec04-card-r14.teaching_text: Idaho caps extra lamp groups in pairs so custom lighting rigs do not overwhelm oncoming drivers.

sec04-card-r15.question_text: What is the maximum number of front auxiliary lights permitted on a vehicle?
sec04-card-r15.teaching_text: Adding off-road light pods beyond two front auxiliary lamps crosses Idaho's legal equipment cap.

sec04-card-r16.question_text: At most how many front fog lights is a vehicle allowed to carry?
sec04-card-r16.teaching_text: Just like spotlights and auxiliary lamps, front fog lamps top out at a pair of two.

sec04-card-r17.question_text: What is the maximum number of cowl or fender lights permitted on a motor vehicle?
sec04-card-r17.teaching_text: Every extra front lamp category—spotlights, auxiliary, fog, and cowl or fender lights—shares the same two-lamp ceiling.

sec04-card-r23.question_text: What must a driver clear from the windows before driving so visibility stays open in every direction?
sec04-card-r23.teaching_text: Scraping every window before shifting out of park preserves full three-sixty sightlines for merges and backing.

sec05-card-f05.question_text: Where must you bring your vehicle to a halt at a stop sign when a painted stop line is on the pavement?
sec05-card-f05.teaching_text: Rolling past the painted stripe pushes your bumper into pedestrian and cross-traffic space and fails road exams fast.

sec05-card-f06.question_text: Where must you stop for a stop sign when no stop line is painted on the road?
sec05-card-f06.teaching_text: Stopping inside the walkway forces people on foot to step out into moving lanes to get around your hood.

sec05-card-f07.question_text: Where do you stop at a stop sign when neither a stop line nor a crosswalk exists?
sec05-card-f07.teaching_text: Pulling out into the crossroad before checking sightlines exposes the front of your car to high-speed cross-traffic.

sec05-card-f08.question_text: What actions does a Yield sign require toward vehicles and pedestrians in the intersection or roadway ahead?
sec05-card-f08.teaching_text: Treating a yield triangle like a merge at full speed cuts off drivers and walkers who legally own the lane.

sec05-card-f09.question_text: When must a driver come to a complete stop at a Yield sign?
sec05-card-f09.teaching_text: Test-takers often think yield means never stopping, even though heavy cross-traffic makes a full halt mandatory.

sec05-card-f10.question_text: What movement does a Do Not Enter sign forbid?
sec05-card-f10.teaching_text: Driving past a Do Not Enter notice puts you nose-to-nose against oncoming highway or ramp traffic.

sec05-card-f11.question_text: Under what driving conditions does a speed-limit sign state the maximum speed allowed?
sec05-card-f11.teaching_text: Rain, snow, darkness, or heavy traffic require dropping below the posted number to stay safe and lawful.

sec05-card-f12.question_text: Which side of an approaching island or barrier must you pass when directed by a Keep Right of Island sign?
sec05-card-f12.teaching_text: Passing left of a raised median island can trap your car in opposing lanes or against concrete curbing.

sec05-card-f13.question_text: What color and types of channelizing or warning devices commonly identify a highway work zone?
sec05-card-f13.teaching_text: Spotting bright orange gear early gives you extra seconds to ease off the gas before lanes tighten.

sec05-card-f14.question_text: Which road-surface and equipment hazards should you scan for inside a work zone?
sec05-card-f14.teaching_text: Loose stone, sudden pavement lips, and heavy rigs entering narrow lanes punish drivers who tailgate or speed.

sec05-card-f15.question_text: Which two colors are used on work-zone warning signs?
sec05-card-f15.teaching_text: Knowledge exams frequently contrast orange temporary construction warnings against standard yellow permanent hazard diamonds.

sec05-card-f16.question_text: What is the rule about moving or driving around barriers and signs blocking a closed road?
sec05-card-f16.teaching_text: Bypassing closure barricades can drop your wheels into open trenches, washed-out bridges, or active crews.

sec05-card-f17.question_text: How should you position your vehicle when a work-zone lane-shift sign redirects every lane?
sec05-card-f17.teaching_text: Swapping lanes mid-curve while every lane bends together is a classic cause of sideswipe collisions in construction.

sec05-card-f18.question_text: How must you respond when you encounter a Be Prepared to Stop work-zone sign?
sec05-card-f18.teaching_text: Flaggers or backed-up queues can sit just around the bend, leaving zero margin if you approach at highway pace.

sec05-card-f19.question_text: What driving adjustment is required when you see a slow-moving-vehicle warning?
sec05-card-f19.teaching_text: Closing distance shrinks startlingly fast when highway traffic overtakes farm or construction gear crawling ahead.

sec05-card-f21.question_text: Who is allowed past a Road Closed sign into a work zone?
sec05-card-f21.teaching_text: Unlike local-traffic closures, a plain Road Closed notice bans every everyday motorist without exception.

sec05-card-f22.question_text: When may residential or commercial drivers enter a work zone posted Local Traffic Only or Closed to Thru Traffic?
sec05-card-f22.teaching_text: Using a local-only work zone as a shortcut without an actual destination inside breaks closure law and crowds crews.

sec05-card-f23.question_text: What kind of trip is prohibited by properly posted work-zone closure signs?
sec05-card-f23.teaching_text: Drivers who try cutting all the way through a closed zone often hit dead-end excavations with nowhere to turn around.

sec05-card-f24.question_text: What happens to speeding fines in work zones posted with penalty-increase signs?
sec05-card-f24.teaching_text: Higher penalties deter fast traffic just feet away from roadside workers who have no steel cab protecting them.

sec05-card-f25.question_text: Why must you scan closely for highway crews whenever driving through a work zone?
sec05-card-f25.teaching_text: Assuming road crews go home after sunset blinds drivers to night-shift paving and flagging teams right beside the lane.

sec05-card-f26.question_text: How much following distance should you keep behind the vehicle ahead inside a work zone?
sec05-card-f26.teaching_text: Rear-end crashes spike in construction corridors whenever sudden flagger stops catch tailgaters off guard.

sec05-card-f27.question_text: How should you manage travel time and cabin distractions like phones or stereos in work zones?
sec05-card-f27.teaching_text: Glancing at a phone or cranking music steals the split-second focus needed when cones narrow your lane.

sec05-card-f02.question_text: Which three groups of people directing traffic must drivers obey on the road?
sec05-card-f02.teaching_text: Live directions from authorized people on the pavement always override green lights or ordinary right-of-way habits.

sec05-card-f29.question_text: How must motorists respond to traffic directions from a school safety patrol official?
sec05-card-f29.teaching_text: Ignoring a patrol member's stop paddle puts young students in immediate danger inside active school crossings.

sec05-card-f30.question_text: What three items identify a school-appointed safety patrol official on duty?
sec05-card-f30.teaching_text: Recognizing official patrol gear early lets you slow smoothly before reaching the student crosswalk.

sec05-card-f31.question_text: What do school safety patrol officials display where schoolchildren cross public roads?
sec05-card-f31.teaching_text: Handheld patrol paddles make student crossing moments unmistakable to drivers approaching from both directions.

sec05-card-f32.question_text: What shape and colors do most standard warning signs use?
sec05-card-f32.teaching_text: Even when snow or glare hides a symbol, spotting a yellow diamond tells you a hazard sits ahead.

sec05-card-f33.question_text: Which high-visibility color may school warning signs use?
sec05-card-f33.teaching_text: Fluorescent yellow-green stands out sharply in dawn, dusk, or overcast light when kids walk to class.

sec05-card-f34.question_text: What road situation does a warning sign alert you to prepare for?
sec05-card-f34.teaching_text: Warning signs give advance notice so you can ease off the accelerator before reaching the curve, merge, or crossing.

sec05-card-f35.question_text: What does an Open Range warning mean about fencing and right-of-way for livestock?
sec05-card-f35.teaching_text: Striking cattle or horses on rural Idaho highways can be fatal, and roaming livestock legally own the right-of-way.

sec05-card-f36.question_text: What road layout does a T-intersection warning describe for your lane of travel?
sec05-card-f36.teaching_text: Missing a T-intersection warning at night or in fog risks running straight off the far side of the crossroad.

sec05-card-f37.question_text: What must you do before turning at the T-intersection described by the warning sign?
sec05-card-f37.teaching_text: Drivers on the continuing crossroad do not stop for your terminating road, so pulling out early causes T-bone wrecks.

sec05-card-f38.question_text: What action does an intersection or crossroads warning call for as you approach?
sec05-card-f38.teaching_text: Rural crossroads often hide behind crops or hills where entering drivers might misjudge your highway speed.

sec05-card-f39.question_text: What does a Traffic Signal Ahead warning announce, and on what kinds of roads is it placed?
sec05-card-f39.teaching_text: Curves, hills, or highway speeds can hide red lights until braking distance is nearly gone without advance warning.

sec05-card-r01.question_text: What nearby hazard does a School Zone sign warn drivers to watch for?
sec05-card-r01.teaching_text: Young kids can dart off curbs unpredictably without checking traffic speed or braking distance.

sec05-card-r02.question_text: What consequence applies to violating a posted school-zone speed limit?
sec05-card-r02.teaching_text: Idaho raises penalties in school zones because even small speed increases multiply pedestrian injury severity.

sec05-card-r03.question_text: Which two background colors are valid for a School Zone sign?
sec05-card-r03.teaching_text: Older postings still use standard yellow while newer installations use bright yellow-green, and both carry full force.

sec05-card-r04.question_text: What road layout and lane-change hazard does an Added Lane warning describe?
sec05-card-r04.teaching_text: Even though your entering lane continues without merging, mainline drivers on your left may drift right into your space.

sec05-card-r05.question_text: What two steps must you take before moving left near an added-lane area?
sec05-card-r05.teaching_text: Cutting left right as roadways join risks clipping faster traffic already holding the adjacent highway lane.

sec05-card-r06.question_text: What highway transition does a Two-Way Traffic warning announce?
sec05-card-r06.teaching_text: Forgetting you left a multilane divided highway can lead to pulling into the left lane straight into oncoming cars.

sec05-card-r07.question_text: When posted on the main road, what does a Merging Traffic warning tell you?
sec05-card-r07.teaching_text: Adjusting speed or creating a gap early prevents side-by-side conflicts at busy on-ramps.

sec05-card-r08.question_text: What does a Lane Ends or Merge Left warning mean about lane count and right-of-way?
sec05-card-r08.teaching_text: Drivers in the ending lane who force their way over without yielding cause high-speed sideswipes.

sec05-card-r10.question_text: What separation disappears ahead after a Divided Highway Ends warning?
sec05-card-r10.teaching_text: Once the center divider ends, oncoming headlights sit just across painted centerlines instead of across a median.

sec05-card-r11.question_text: Which three actions are required when approaching a School Crossing warning?
sec05-card-r11.teaching_text: Combining lower speed, active scanning, and compliance with the guard keeps busy school hours crash-free.

sec05-card-r13.question_text: What does a Pedestrian Crossing warning tell you about right-of-way and stopping?
sec05-card-r13.teaching_text: Mid-block or intersection crosswalks often appear where drivers least expect to brake to a complete standstill.

sec05-card-r14.question_text: What color and active feature may a Pedestrian Crossing warning use when someone crosses?
sec05-card-r14.teaching_text: Flashing beacons paired with bright yellow-green borders grab driver attention immediately when someone steps off the curb.

sec05-card-r15.question_text: What road change ahead does a Divided Highway Begins warning announce?
sec05-card-r15.teaching_text: Keeping right of the starting divider island prevents accidentally entering the wrong side of the split roadway.

sec05-card-r16.question_text: What does a Share the Road plaque beneath a bicycle symbol tell drivers and cyclists?
sec05-card-r16.teaching_text: Where dedicated bike stripes are missing, cyclists legally ride in the roadway and need safe passing room.

sec05-card-r17.question_text: Under what lane, shoulder, or traffic conditions are Share the Road signs commonly posted?
sec05-card-r17.teaching_text: Tight pavement and heavy or fast traffic shrink passing room, requiring patient timing before overtaking a rider.

sec05-card-r18.question_text: Where is the pennant-shaped No Passing Zone sign mounted, and what does it mean?
sec05-card-r18.teaching_text: Placing the yellow pennant on the left side keeps it visible even when a tall truck blocks right-shoulder signs.

sec05-card-r19.question_text: What should a driver check upon seeing a steep downhill warning?
sec05-card-r19.teaching_text: Testing brakes and downshifting before the crest prevents brake fade on long mountain grades across Idaho.

sec05-card-r20.question_text: What hazard and driver action does a Slippery When Wet warning indicate?
sec05-card-r20.teaching_text: Rain mixes with road oil to slash tire grip, turning normal dry-weather curve speeds into hydroplaning skids.

sec05-card-r21.question_text: What readiness does a railroad advance warning require as you approach the crossing?
sec05-card-r21.teaching_text: Circular railroad warnings appear well ahead of the rails so you can brake smoothly if a train approaches.

sec05-card-r22.question_text: What should you watch for when passing an Animal Crossing warning?
sec05-card-r22.teaching_text: Deer, elk, and other wildlife cross swiftly near dawn and dusk and frequently travel in groups after the first animal.

sec05-card-r23.question_text: Where is a railroad Emergency Notification System sign posted, and what two numbers does it list?
sec05-card-r23.teaching_text: Giving dispatchers the exact crossing identifier lets them halt approaching trains on the right stretch of track immediately.

sec05-card-r24.question_text: What two kinds of problems is the railroad emergency sign designed to help you report?
sec05-card-r24.teaching_text: Calling the posted railroad number first for a stalled vehicle or broken gate stops oncoming trains fastest.

sec05-card-r25.question_text: What two types of navigation details do white-on-green guide signs provide?
sec05-card-r25.teaching_text: Reading highway exit directions and mileage early prevents dangerous last-second swerves across gore areas.

sec05-card-r26.question_text: What category of roadside information appears on white-on-blue guide signs?
sec05-card-r26.teaching_text: Fuel, food, lodging, hospital, and rest-area notices all use blue backgrounds so travelers spot help fast.

sec05-card-r27.question_text: What destinations do white-on-brown guide signs point out?
sec05-card-r27.teaching_text: Knowledge tests regularly pair green, blue, and brown guide colors to check whether you know parks and historic sites.

sec05-card-r28.question_text: What visibility feature may barricades carry, especially after dark?
sec05-card-r28.teaching_text: Amber or red flashers catch your eye in darkness long before headlights illuminate striped barricade boards.

sec05-card-r29.question_text: How do permanent barricade colors differ from temporary barricade colors in the Idaho handbook?
sec05-card-r29.teaching_text: Matching orange-and-white to temporary construction and red-and-white to permanent closures is a favorite exam distinction.

sec05-card-r30.question_text: Does switching between red-and-white and orange-and-white barricade colors change what the stripe angles mean?
sec05-card-r30.teaching_text: Whether a barricade is temporary or permanent, the downward slant of its stripes always points toward the open side.

sec05-card-r31.question_text: What does a V-shaped stripe pattern on a barricade tell approaching traffic?
sec05-card-r31.teaching_text: Stripes slanting inward from both sides leave no open travel side, signaling that nobody may proceed farther.

sec05-card-r32.question_text: On which side should you pass a barricade whose stripes slant downward toward the left?
sec05-card-r32.teaching_text: Picture a ball rolling down the angled stripes to remember which side of the barricade stays open.

sec05-card-r33.question_text: On which side should you pass a barricade whose stripes slant downward toward the right?
sec05-card-r33.teaching_text: Downward-right diagonal stripes funnel your lane cleanly around the right edge of the hazard.

sec05-card-f01.question_text: What collective term covers traffic signals, highway signs, and pavement markings?
sec05-card-f01.teaching_text: Every light, sign, and painted stripe works together as an official traffic-control system that drivers must obey.

sec05-card-f03.question_text: Which three visual traits should you learn so you can recognize traffic signs quickly?
sec05-card-f03.teaching_text: Knowing shapes and colors lets you decode faded, snow-covered, or distant signs before reading a single word.

sec05-card-f04.question_text: Which color combinations are normally used on regulatory traffic signs?
sec05-card-f04.teaching_text: Black-and-white posts speed and lane laws, while red-and-white highlights critical stop, yield, and entry bans.

sec05-card-f20.question_text: What kinds of vehicles mainly display the slow-moving-vehicle sign according to the handbook?
sec05-card-f20.teaching_text: Tractors and heavy graders move far below highway pace, so their rear emblem warns you to brake early.

sec05-card-f28.question_text: Which four driver errors are cited as major contributors to work-zone crashes?
sec05-card-f28.teaching_text: Almost every construction wreck traces back to rushing, looking away, forcing merges, or refusing to yield.

sec05-card-r09.question_text: What hazard above the roadway does a Low Clearance sign warn about?
sec05-card-r09.teaching_text: Tall pickups, campers, or roof-rack loads can wedge under low bridges if the driver ignores clearance numbers.

sec05-card-r12.question_text: Which two colors may be used for a School Crossing sign?
sec05-card-r12.teaching_text: Both classic yellow and fluorescent yellow-green crossing pentagons demand the same slow speed and child watchfulness.

sec06-card-f04.question_text: Where must you come to a complete stop when facing a steady circular red light?
sec06-card-f04.teaching_text: Creeping past the stop bar or crosswalk edges your bumper into cross-traffic and pedestrian paths.

sec06-card-f05.question_text: What movement is forbidden when a No Turn on Red notice is posted at a signal?
sec06-card-f05.teaching_text: Even after a full stop with an empty lane, turning against a posted No Turn on Red sign earns an instant ticket.

sec06-card-f06.question_text: What three steps must you follow at a flashing red traffic light?
sec06-card-f06.teaching_text: Waiting forever at a flashing red blocks traffic behind you, while rolling through without stopping risks a T-bone crash.

sec06-card-f07.question_text: May you turn in the direction of a steady red arrow after stopping, or what must happen first?
sec06-card-f07.teaching_text: Many drivers confuse a steady red arrow with a circular red light, illegally turning right or left before the arrow changes.

sec06-card-f08.question_text: What signal change does a steady circular yellow light warn is about to happen?
sec06-card-f08.teaching_text: Punching the gas on yellow often puts your car inside the intersection right after cross-traffic gets a green.

sec06-card-f09.question_text: What should a driver do before entering an intersection when the circular light turns yellow?
sec06-card-f09.teaching_text: Yellow means clear the approach safely by braking, not racing the light to beat the red.

sec06-card-f10.question_text: What should you do if the light turns circular yellow after you are already inside the intersection?
sec06-card-f10.teaching_text: Slamming the brakes or reversing mid-intersection strands your vehicle directly in the path of cross-traffic.

sec06-card-f11.question_text: How should you drive through a flashing circular yellow light?
sec06-card-f11.teaching_text: Stopping dead on a flashing yellow surprises drivers behind you, while barreling through ignores cross-street hazards.

sec06-card-f12.question_text: What does a solid yellow arrow tell drivers in a turn lane?
sec06-card-f12.teaching_text: Assuming oncoming traffic still faces red as a solid yellow arrow fades leads to severe left-turn collisions.

sec06-card-f13.question_text: What should you do if a solid yellow arrow appears before you enter the intersection?
sec06-card-f13.teaching_text: Halting smoothly behind the line keeps you from turning late against fast oncoming straight-through traffic.

sec06-card-f14.question_text: How should you finish when a solid yellow arrow appears while you are already in the intersection turning?
sec06-card-f14.teaching_text: Hesitating halfway through a turn blocks lanes just as opposing traffic prepares to launch.

sec06-card-f15.question_text: Under what condition does a flashing yellow arrow allow you to turn?
sec06-card-f15.teaching_text: Unlike a green arrow, a flashing yellow arrow gives oncoming cars a green light at the exact same moment.

sec06-card-f16.question_text: What movement does a steady circular green indication allow?
sec06-card-f16.teaching_text: Even when forward movement is permitted, glancing left and right catches red-light runners before you roll out.

sec06-card-f17.question_text: Who has the right-of-way when you turn left from a left-turn lane on a circular green light?
sec06-card-f17.teaching_text: Forgetting that circular green offers zero left-turn protection is one of the top crash errors among new drivers.

sec06-card-f18.question_text: Why must you hold back even on a green light when traffic ahead is backed up?
sec06-card-f18.teaching_text: Stopping with your rear bumper hanging inside the intersection traps cross-traffic and emergency vehicles when lights cycle.

sec06-card-f19.question_text: Which turning movement commonly uses a five-lens doghouse traffic signal?
sec06-card-f19.teaching_text: Recognizing the five-section housing helps you anticipate transitions between protected arrows and circular lights.

sec06-card-f20.question_text: What does the yellow indication on a doghouse signal tell left-turning drivers?
sec06-card-f20.teaching_text: Once protected left time ends on a doghouse cluster, oncoming lanes either start moving or cross-traffic gets green.

sec06-card-f21.question_text: How must drivers treat an intersection when the traffic signals stop working?
sec06-card-f21.teaching_text: Power outages turn busy arterials chaotic fast if main-road drivers breeze through without stopping.

sec06-card-f22.question_text: How are the colored lenses arranged on a pedestrian hybrid beacon?
sec06-card-f22.teaching_text: Knowing the three-lens triangle layout prevents confusion when encountering mid-block crosswalk beacons.

sec06-card-f23.question_text: Where are pedestrian hybrid beacon lights mounted at a crossing?
sec06-card-f23.teaching_text: Dual overhead and roadside mounting keeps the red stop phases visible even around larger vehicles.

sec06-card-f24.question_text: How is a stop-controlled side street affected when a pedestrian hybrid beacon operates on the main road?
sec06-card-f24.teaching_text: A dark beacon on the main street never cancels the octagonal stop sign facing drivers on the side street.

sec06-card-f25.question_text: Who must you check for right before turning around a street corner?
sec06-card-f25.teaching_text: Looking only at oncoming vehicle gaps causes turning drivers to miss walkers stepping off the corner curb.

sec06-card-f26.question_text: What does a pedestrian hybrid beacon display before anyone presses the crossing button?
sec06-card-f26.teaching_text: Unlike a power-outage traffic light, a resting hybrid beacon stays dark on purpose until activated by a walker.

sec06-card-f27.question_text: What does the flashing yellow phase on a pedestrian hybrid beacon tell approaching drivers?
sec06-card-f27.teaching_text: Someone just pressed the crosswalk button, so easing off the gas early avoids hard last-second braking.

sec06-card-f28.question_text: What does a pedestrian hybrid beacon instruct drivers to do when flashing yellow turns steady yellow?
sec06-card-f28.teaching_text: Solid yellow signals that twin red stop lights are seconds away so pedestrians can enter the crosswalk.

sec06-card-f29.question_text: What action do two steady red lights on a pedestrian hybrid beacon require?
sec06-card-f29.teaching_text: Twin solid reds protect the start of the walk interval when pedestrians step directly across traffic lanes.

sec06-card-f30.question_text: How should you respond when a pedestrian hybrid beacon switches to alternating flashing red lights?
sec06-card-f30.teaching_text: Wigwag flashing reds work like a stop sign, letting traffic clear out once every pedestrian finishes crossing.

sec06-card-f31.question_text: When a pedestrian hybrid beacon finishes its cycle and goes dark again, what may drivers do?
sec06-card-f31.teaching_text: Always double-check for slower pedestrians still finishing the crossing even after the overhead lenses shut off.

sec06-card-r02.question_text: Who may cross a single dashed yellow center line to pass?
sec06-card-r02.teaching_text: Broken yellow centerlines allow passing both ways only when sight distance is long and oncoming space is wide open.

sec06-card-r03.question_text: When a solid yellow line runs beside a dashed yellow line, which lane is allowed to pass?
sec06-card-r03.teaching_text: Crossing with the solid yellow stripe on your side puts you into blind curves or hills with hidden oncoming traffic.

sec06-card-r04.question_text: What passing rule do double solid yellow center lines enforce?
sec06-card-r04.teaching_text: Double yellow stripes mark restricted sightlines or busy corridors where overtaking oncoming lanes is unlawful.

sec06-card-r05.question_text: Under what circumstance may you cross double solid yellow center lines?
sec06-card-r05.teaching_text: Test questions love testing that double yellow bars passing yet still permits safe left turns.

sec06-card-r06.question_text: Which roadside entrances may you enter or leave by turning left across double yellow lines when safe?
sec06-card-r06.teaching_text: Yielding to oncoming traffic first makes turning into homes or storefronts across double yellow legal and predictable.

sec06-card-r07.question_text: Which maneuvers are allowed from a shared center turn lane?
sec06-card-r07.teaching_text: Using the center lane solely for turning maneuvers keeps slowing vehicles out of fast through lanes.

sec06-card-r08.question_text: How are the pavement lines painted along each edge of a shared center turn lane?
sec06-card-r08.teaching_text: Solid outer yellow with dashed inner yellow distinguishes a two-way turn lane from ordinary passing lanes.

sec06-card-r09.question_text: What type of driving is forbidden inside a shared center turn lane?
sec06-card-r09.teaching_text: Using a two-way turn lane to pass congestion sets up head-on collisions with opposing left-turners.

sec06-card-r10.question_text: How must you behave toward another vehicle already preparing to turn from a shared center turn lane?
sec06-card-r10.teaching_text: Pulling into the same center pocket beside or nose-to-nose with a waiting car blocks sightlines and causes crashes.

sec06-card-r11.question_text: What traffic directions are separated by broken white lane lines on a multilane road?
sec06-card-r11.teaching_text: Remembering white means same-way traffic and yellow means opposing traffic keeps you oriented on unfamiliar roads.

sec06-card-r12.question_text: How should you position your vehicle relative to broken white lane boundaries?
sec06-card-r12.teaching_text: Straddling dashed stripes occupies two lanes at once and invites sideswipes from passing drivers.

sec06-card-r13.question_text: When may you cross a broken white lane line?
sec06-card-r13.teaching_text: Checking mirrors, blind spots, and signaling first ensures a dashed white stripe stays a safe lane-change zone.

sec06-card-r14.question_text: What boundary do solid white edge lines mark on a roadway?
sec06-card-r14.teaching_text: Knowing where travel pavement ends keeps your right tires off soft gravel shoulders or steep drop-offs.

sec06-card-r15.question_text: When are solid white edge lines especially helpful for keeping your vehicle on the road?
sec06-card-r15.teaching_text: Watching the right white fog line shields your eyes from oncoming high-beam glare in rain, snow, or darkness.

sec06-card-r16.question_text: How should you treat a single solid white line separating same-direction traffic lanes?
sec06-card-r16.teaching_text: Single solid white lines appear near intersections and ramps where last-second lane swaps trigger rear-end and side crashes.

sec06-card-r19.question_text: What rule applies where double solid white lines separate lanes?
sec06-card-r19.teaching_text: Unlike a single solid white stripe that discourages crossing, twin solid white lines ban lane changes outright.

sec06-card-r17.question_text: What do a solid white boundary line and a painted bicycle symbol designate?
sec06-card-r17.teaching_text: Driving or parking a motor vehicle inside a solid-striped bike lane forces riders unexpectedly into fast traffic.

sec06-card-r18.question_text: Which direction must bicyclists ride inside a designated bicycle lane?
sec06-card-r18.teaching_text: Riding with traffic flow makes cyclists predictable at driveways, corners, and green lights.

sec06-card-r20.question_text: What two merging movements are permitted where a bicycle-lane stripe turns dashed?
sec06-card-r20.teaching_text: Weaving cleanly before the corner prevents the classic right-hook crash where a car turns across a straight-going cyclist.

sec06-card-r21.question_text: At which roadway locations does the handbook place dashed bicycle-lane lines?
sec06-card-r21.teaching_text: Dashing the bike stripe right where cars turn alerts both riders and motorists to check mirrors and yield.

sec06-card-f01.question_text: What is the main function of traffic signals, and where do they chiefly operate?
sec06-card-f01.teaching_text: Assigning clear turns by light phase keeps crossing streams of vehicles and pedestrians moving safely.

sec06-card-f02.question_text: From top to bottom, how are red, yellow, and green arranged on a vertical traffic light?
sec06-card-f02.teaching_text: Standard lens positions allow color-blind drivers and glare-affected motorists to read signal state instantly by height.

sec06-card-f03.question_text: From left to right, how are red, yellow, and green positioned on a horizontal traffic signal?
sec06-card-f03.teaching_text: Knowing red sits on the far left prevents misreading sideways signals under low overpasses or high winds.

sec06-card-r01.question_text: Besides separating lanes, what five rules or zones do pavement markings identify?
sec06-card-r01.teaching_text: Reading painted road lines tells you legal passing, turning, pedestrian, and stopping rules even before spotting a sign.

sec07-card-f07.question_text: How should you use your senses when approaching any railroad crossing?
sec07-card-f07.teaching_text: Loud cabin music or a quick one-way glance can hide a fast train or active crossing bell until too late.

sec07-card-f08.question_text: When is a driver allowed to proceed across railroad tracks?
sec07-card-f08.teaching_text: Guessing on sightlines or following the car ahead blindly onto rails leaves zero escape path if a train appears.

sec07-card-f09.question_text: How many feet from the nearest rail must you stop when a railroad crossing stop is required?
sec07-card-f09.teaching_text: Stopping closer than fifteen feet puts your hood inside the overhang zone of wide locomotives and freight cars.

sec07-card-f14.question_text: What must you do when red railroad crossing warning lights are actively flashing?
sec07-card-f14.teaching_text: Treating active red rail flashers like a yellow caution light is a deadly gamble against high-speed trains.

sec07-card-f15.question_text: What is the rule whenever a railroad crossing gate is down or starting to lower?
sec07-card-f15.teaching_text: Weaving around descending gates traps vehicles right on the rails as the train closes the remaining distance in seconds.

sec07-card-f17.question_text: May you ever stop with any part of your vehicle resting on railroad tracks?
sec07-card-f17.teaching_text: Even an overhanging tailpipe or bumper can be clipped by a passing train while traffic ahead holds you pinned.

sec07-card-f18.question_text: In slow or backed-up traffic, what must you confirm before driving onto a railroad crossing?
sec07-card-f18.teaching_text: Entering tracks behind a stopped line of cars can strand you across the rails when a red light holds ahead.

sec07-card-f19.question_text: May you ignore active railroad signals or circle lowered gates if you cannot see a train coming?
sec07-card-f19.teaching_text: Curves, brush, darkness, or parked railcars can hide a fast-approaching locomotive even when tracks look empty.

sec07-card-f20.question_text: Why must you never shift gears while your vehicle is crossing railroad tracks?
sec07-card-f20.teaching_text: Missing a shift mid-crossing can stall the engine right on the rails when seconds matter most.

sec07-card-f21.question_text: What rule applies to trying to outrun an approaching train to a crossing?
sec07-card-f21.teaching_text: Large locomotives always look slower and farther away than they really are, making racing the crossing fatal.

sec07-card-f22.question_text: What must you check before crossing where two or more sets of railroad tracks run side by side?
sec07-card-f22.teaching_text: The caboose or tail of a passing train often hides a second train approaching fast from the opposite direction.

sec07-card-f23.question_text: Why should you stay alert behind buses and large trucks approaching railroad crossings?
sec07-card-f23.teaching_text: School buses and hazmat tankers must halt even when lights are dark, catching tailgaters by surprise.

sec07-card-f24.question_text: Why must you still look both ways at railroad tracks when the flashing lights are dark?
sec07-card-f24.teaching_text: Power loss or sensor faults can silence crossing flashers even while a train is bearing down on the road.

sec07-card-f25.question_text: How is a roundabout defined by travel flow and turn direction at entry and exit?
sec07-card-f25.teaching_text: Turning left directly upon entering sends a car wrong-way head-on into circulating traffic.

sec07-card-f27.question_text: Who holds the right-of-way between a driver entering a roundabout and vehicles already inside it?
sec07-card-f27.teaching_text: Circulating vehicles never stop for entering lanes, so forcing your way in triggers immediate side impacts.

sec07-card-f28.question_text: Which rotational direction do you follow inside a roundabout when going straight, left, or making a U-turn?
sec07-card-f28.teaching_text: Every destination uses the same counterclockwise circle around the center island before peeling off to the right.

sec07-card-f29.question_text: How should you manage your speed on the approach to and inside a roundabout?
sec07-card-f29.teaching_text: Low steady speeds make merging gaps smooth and give plenty of time to spot crosswalk users.

sec07-card-f30.question_text: What roadside and pavement controls must you follow at a roundabout?
sec07-card-f30.teaching_text: Multilane roundabouts assign turn and straight lanes beforehand, so ignoring lane arrows causes exit sideswipes.

sec07-card-f31.question_text: When must you yield to pedestrians and bicyclists at a roundabout?
sec07-card-f31.teaching_text: Drivers often remember the entry crosswalk yet forget to scan the exit crosswalk as they accelerate away.

sec07-card-f32.question_text: From which side does circulating roundabout traffic approach as you wait to enter?
sec07-card-f32.teaching_text: Because traffic circles counterclockwise around the island, your conflict vehicles always come from your left.

sec07-card-f33.question_text: Which turn signal should you activate as your roundabout exit approaches?
sec07-card-f33.teaching_text: Signaling right lets waiting drivers at the next approach know you are peeling off rather than staying in the circle.

sec07-card-f01.question_text: What must a right-turning driver do when a bicyclist is already in the bike-and-turn merging area?
sec07-card-f01.teaching_text: Cutting right in front of a cyclist already holding the weave zone causes a dangerous right-hook collision.

sec07-card-f02.question_text: Where should a bicyclist go when a right-turning car already occupies the merging area ahead?
sec07-card-f02.teaching_text: Passing on the left of a right-turning car avoids squeezing into the blind curb gap as the car turns.

sec07-card-f03.question_text: What traffic condition does green-colored pavement emphasize?
sec07-card-f03.teaching_text: Bright green paint alerts everyone that motor vehicles and bikes cross paths right across that strip.

sec07-card-f04.question_text: Why are some bicycle lanes and intersection extensions painted bright green?
sec07-card-f04.teaching_text: Green extensions keep the cyclist path obvious across wide intersections where solid lane stripes break.

sec07-card-f05.question_text: What must drivers watch for at a green-painted bicycle-lane crossing area?
sec07-card-f05.teaching_text: Checking right mirrors and blind spots before crossing green paint catches fast-rolling cyclists early.

sec07-card-f06.question_text: What must bicyclists keep in mind while riding across a green bicycle-lane crossing area?
sec07-card-f06.teaching_text: Green paint boosts visibility, not physical protection, so riders still watch for turning or merging cars.

sec07-card-r01.question_text: Which turning movement does a thru-turn intersection prohibit directly at the main junction?
sec07-card-r01.teaching_text: Eliminating direct left phases cuts intersection wait times and removes high-impact oncoming left-turn crashes.

sec07-card-r02.question_text: What four-step path replaces a direct left turn at a thru-turn intersection?
sec07-card-r02.teaching_text: Using the downstream signalized U-turn lets you reach the cross street cleanly via a right turn.

sec07-card-r03.question_text: How does a single point urban interchange control turning traffic?
sec07-card-r03.teaching_text: Instead of two separate ramp signals, one central signal phases opposing left turns simultaneously.

sec07-card-r04.question_text: Why is stopping behind the painted stop lines critical at a single point urban interchange?
sec07-card-r04.teaching_text: Stop bars sit farther back than normal so wide dual left-turn paths do not clip your front bumper.

sec07-card-r05.question_text: Which lanes do you use to go straight across the handbook's single point urban interchange?
sec07-card-r05.teaching_text: Getting trapped in an outer or inner turn-only lane forces you onto the freeway ramp instead of straight ahead.

sec07-card-r06.question_text: Which lanes take you left onto the freeway at a single point urban interchange?
sec07-card-r06.teaching_text: Following the dashed guide arcs inside marked left-turn lanes keeps side-by-side turning traffic separated.

sec07-card-r07.question_text: How does the off-ramp divide traffic at a single point urban interchange?
sec07-card-r07.teaching_text: Notice there is no straight-across ramp lane back onto the freeway, only left-turn and right-turn channels.

sec07-card-r08.question_text: What must you do if you exit by mistake at a single point urban interchange instead of going straight across?
sec07-card-r08.teaching_text: Trying to shoot straight across from the off-ramp sends you across sweeping island curbs and conflict lanes.

sec07-card-r09.question_text: How do you complete a right turn after leaving the interstate at a single point urban interchange?
sec07-card-r09.teaching_text: Channelized right-turn islands carry crosswalks right across your path before you blend into arterial traffic.

sec07-card-r10.question_text: How do you turn left onto the cross highway from a single point urban interchange off-ramp?
sec07-card-r10.teaching_text: Keeping inside your painted guide arc and scanning the far-side crosswalk prevents drift and pedestrian conflicts.

sec07-card-r11.question_text: Which three features serve people walking or biking through the described single point urban interchange?
sec07-card-r11.teaching_text: Wide ramp geometry means drivers must expect dedicated bike and pedestrian phases crossing turn channels.

sec07-card-r12.question_text: Where do signalized crossings direct pedestrians and cyclists mid-way across a single point urban interchange?
sec07-card-r12.teaching_text: Crossing in stages via the central refuge island shortens exposure across wide high-volume arterial lanes.

sec07-card-r13.question_text: How does a diverging diamond interchange shift lanes, and what benefit does that provide?
sec07-card-r13.teaching_text: Temporarily placing traffic on the left lets freeway left-turners enter ramps without crossing oncoming lanes.

sec07-card-r14.question_text: Where do opposing lanes cross over each other at a diverging diamond interchange?
sec07-card-r14.teaching_text: Signalized crossovers on both ends of the overpass switch you cleanly left and then back right.

sec07-card-r15.question_text: Which four roadway guides steer you safely through a diverging diamond interchange?
sec07-card-r15.teaching_text: Angled concrete islands and lane stripes make the left-side crossover feel natural when you follow your lane.

sec07-card-r16.question_text: Why must you stop right at the painted stop lines inside a diverging diamond interchange?
sec07-card-r16.teaching_text: Overshooting the angled crossover stop bar blocks opposing crossover lanes and shared pedestrian-bike crossings.

sec07-card-r17.question_text: How do you drive straight across a diverging diamond interchange from entry to exit?
sec07-card-r17.teaching_text: Staying between your lane stripes carries you left across the bridge and right back to normal at the second signal.

sec07-card-r18.question_text: Which steps take you left onto the freeway through a diverging diamond interchange?
sec07-card-r18.teaching_text: Because you already crossed to the left side at the entrance signal, the freeway left-entrance ramp opens conflict-free.

sec07-card-f10.question_text: How far does a one-hundred-fifty-car freight train going fifty miles an hour need to stop?
sec07-card-f10.teaching_text: Even emergency train brakes cannot stop a massive freight consist in time once an engineer spots your car on the tracks.

sec07-card-f11.question_text: What large symbol and letter pair are commonly painted on the lane ahead of a railroad crossing?
sec07-card-f11.teaching_text: Spotting white railroad pavement markings early warns you before crossbucks even come into view around a bend.

sec07-card-f12.question_text: Which white X-shaped sign is posted right at most railroad crossings?
sec07-card-f12.teaching_text: A white crossbuck stands right beside the tracks and carries the same legal obligation as a yield sign.

sec07-card-f13.question_text: What active warning device is often paired with crossbuck signs on busy roads?
sec07-card-f13.teaching_text: High-traffic crossings add active red flashers to crossbucks so drivers get an unmistakable visual stop command.

sec07-card-f16.question_text: When should you expect a train when approaching any railroad track?
sec07-card-f16.teaching_text: Freight and work trains run unscheduled day and night in either direction, making routine complacency deadly.

sec07-card-f26.question_text: What symbol appears on the common advance warning sign for a roundabout?
sec07-card-f26.teaching_text: Seeing the circular-arrow diamond ahead tells you to shed speed and pick your lane before reaching the splitter island.

sec08-card-f01.question_text: What does Idaho's basic speed rule require on every road, even where maximum or minimum limits are posted?
sec08-card-f01.teaching_text: Driving the posted limit during whiteout snow or thick fog still earns a citation when conditions demand slower travel.

sec08-card-f02.question_text: Which road, traffic, and visibility factors must guide how fast you drive?
sec08-card-f02.teaching_text: Adjusting speed dynamically for pedestrians, bikes, blind curves, slick pavement, and intersections prevents surprises.

sec08-card-f03.question_text: How can driving below the posted speed limit still violate Idaho's basic speed rule?
sec08-card-f03.teaching_text: Creeping far below normal pace in clear weather triggers sudden braking chains and risky passing behind you.

sec08-card-f04.question_text: What is Idaho's standard maximum speed limit on interstate highways unless posted otherwise?
sec08-card-f04.teaching_text: Know the seventy-five baseline first, then watch signs closely where urban corridors drop or rural stretches rise.

sec08-card-f05.question_text: When is eighty miles an hour lawful on an Idaho interstate?
sec08-card-f05.teaching_text: Assuming every rural interstate permits eighty without seeing a posted eighty sign risks a costly speeding ticket.

sec08-card-f06.question_text: What is the standard state-highway speed limit in Idaho, and what higher limit applies where posted?
sec08-card-f06.teaching_text: Exams frequently pair sixty-five default state highways with seventy posted sections to test exact Idaho limits.

sec08-card-f07.question_text: What is the maximum speed in residential, business, or urban districts unless posted otherwise?
sec08-card-f07.teaching_text: Driveways, parked cars, and crosswalks pack tightly into urban and neighborhood streets, demanding thirty-five or less.

sec08-card-f08.question_text: What is the rule against driving unusually slowly in normal traffic?
sec08-card-f08.teaching_text: Large speed gaps between one crawling car and surrounding traffic raise rear-end crash risk dramatically.

sec08-card-f09.question_text: What is forbidden when driving in the extreme left lane of a multilane road?
sec08-card-f09.teaching_text: Lingering in the far-left lane forces faster lawful traffic to weave around your right side.

sec08-card-f10.question_text: What speed rule applies inside a posted school zone?
sec08-card-f10.teaching_text: Even five miles an hour over a school-zone posting lengthens stopping distance where children cross.

sec08-card-f11.question_text: What speed rule applies through designated highway work zones?
sec08-card-f11.teaching_text: Narrowed lanes and roadside crews leave zero room for highway-speed braking mistakes.

sec08-card-f12.question_text: What financial consequence can follow a work-zone speeding violation?
sec08-card-f12.teaching_text: Idaho enforces stiffer fixed fines in work zones to protect crews working feet from moving bumpers.

sec08-card-f14.question_text: Which traffic sign matches how you must treat a flashing red signal?
sec08-card-f14.teaching_text: Come to a dead halt first, then yield until cross-traffic and pedestrians are completely clear.

sec08-card-f15.question_text: What must you do at a steady red arrow, and when may you turn in that arrow's direction?
sec08-card-f15.teaching_text: Turning right or left on a steady red arrow violates Idaho signal law even when cross-traffic looks empty.

sec08-card-f16.question_text: Where must your vehicle stop and wait at a steady circular red signal with a stop line?
sec08-card-f16.teaching_text: Stopping cleanly behind the white bar preserves turning radius for trucks and keeps crosswalks open.

sec08-card-f17.question_text: Where must you stop at a steady circular red light if no stop line is painted?
sec08-card-f17.teaching_text: Blocking an unmarked or painted crosswalk forces walkers out into live cross-street lanes.

sec08-card-f18.question_text: Which movement is allowed when a green arrow lights up alongside a steady circular red?
sec08-card-f18.teaching_text: Going straight through while only the turn arrow is green runs a live red light.

sec08-card-f19.question_text: Apart from a legal turn on red or a lit green arrow, when may you move from a steady circular red?
sec08-card-f19.teaching_text: Jumping the red early when cross-traffic gets yellow collides with late-clearing cars.

sec08-card-f20.question_text: How must you respond to a pedestrian inside either a marked or unmarked intersection crosswalk?
sec08-card-f20.teaching_text: Every street corner forms a legal crosswalk whether paint stripes exist on the asphalt or not.

sec08-card-f21.question_text: Which railway warnings or sights require a driver to stop at a crossing?
sec08-card-f21.teaching_text: Any active signal, human watchman, lowering gate, or visible train makes stopping before the rails mandatory.

sec08-card-f22.question_text: Where must you stop and whom must you yield to when emerging from a driveway, alley, building, or private road?
sec08-card-f22.teaching_text: Pulling straight to the street curb without halting before the sidewalk strikes joggers, kids, and scooters.

sec08-card-f23.question_text: What must you do whenever a police officer signals or requests you to stop?
sec08-card-f23.teaching_text: Failing to stop promptly for law enforcement escalates a routine traffic stop into a serious offense.

sec08-card-f24.question_text: Where and how long must you stop when an emergency or police vehicle approaches with siren or flashing red-or-blue lights?
sec08-card-f24.teaching_text: Stopping inside an intersection or pulling out before every emergency unit clears blocks urgent response routes.

sec08-card-f25.question_text: What immediate action is required by law if you are involved in a traffic crash?
sec08-card-f25.teaching_text: Driving away from any collision turns an accident into a hit-and-run criminal violation.

sec08-card-f26.question_text: When must you stop for a school bus with flashing upper red lights or an extended stop arm, and what is the one highway exception?
sec08-card-f26.teaching_text: Even on a three-lane road with a center turn lane, oncoming drivers must stop when red bus lights flash.

sec08-card-f27.question_text: Once stopped for a school bus, when are you legally allowed to start moving again?
sec08-card-f27.teaching_text: Rolling forward the instant lights stop while a student still crosses near the bumper risks tragedy.

sec08-card-f28.question_text: What exact lane configuration excuses opposite-direction drivers from stopping for a school bus?
sec08-card-f28.teaching_text: Knowledge exams test the exact two-lanes-each-way requirement to trip up drivers thinking three lanes qualify.

sec08-card-f29.question_text: Which two methods let you signal drivers behind you when slowing down or stopping?
sec08-card-f29.teaching_text: Early brake-light taps or a clear hand signal prevent tailgating drivers from slamming into your rear bumper.

sec08-card-f30.question_text: Which two critical time windows change as your travel speed rises?
sec08-card-f30.teaching_text: Higher speed eats up pavement during human reaction delay and stretches total braking time dramatically.

sec08-card-f32.question_text: What visual landmark tells you that you left a safe gap when stopped behind another car?
sec08-card-f32.teaching_text: If the car ahead hides where its back tires meet the asphalt, you pulled up far too close.

sec08-card-f33.question_text: How does leaving the rear-tire gap help if a distracted driver rear-ends your stopped car?
sec08-card-f33.teaching_text: Extra space absorbs the shove from behind instead of slamming your hood into the next vehicle forward.

sec08-card-f34.question_text: How does the rear-tire stopped gap help if the vehicle ahead stalls in your lane?
sec08-card-f34.teaching_text: Pulling bumper-to-bumper pins you behind a dead vehicle and forces dangerous reversing in live traffic.

sec08-card-r01.question_text: When shifting lanes or overtaking another vehicle, what must you activate?
sec08-card-r01.teaching_text: Silent lane weaves blindside motorcycles and adjacent drivers who cannot read your steering intentions.

sec08-card-r02.question_text: What must you do with your turn signal when exiting a roundabout?
sec08-card-r02.teaching_text: Blinking out of the circle tells entering drivers at the next leg whether a safe gap is opening.

sec08-card-r03.question_text: Does turning into a private driveway require a turn signal just like turning at an intersection?
sec08-card-r03.teaching_text: Unsignaled braking for a hidden residential driveway is a prime trigger for rear-end collisions.

sec08-card-r04.question_text: When must you use your turn signal on freeway or interstate ramps?
sec08-card-r04.teaching_text: High-speed highway merges and off-ramp peels demand early signals so mainline drivers adjust smoothly.

sec08-card-r05.question_text: What must you do before pulling from a parked roadside spot into a live travel lane?
sec08-card-r05.teaching_text: Pulling away from a curb without blinking gives approaching traffic and cyclists zero warning.

sec08-card-r06.question_text: What must you do before pulling over to the side of the road?
sec08-card-r06.teaching_text: Signaling right before slowing toward the shoulder tells trailing traffic to pass cleanly instead of braking hard.

sec08-card-r07.question_text: How far ahead must you signal in a business or residential area, and what exception applies right past an intersection?
sec08-card-r07.teaching_text: Signaling too early before an intersection tricks cross-street drivers into pulling out directly in front of you.

sec08-card-r08.question_text: How many seconds ahead must you signal on a freeway or highway, and when do you wait?
sec08-card-r08.teaching_text: At sixty-five or seventy-five miles an hour, one hundred feet flashes by in a heartbeat, so five full seconds is required.

sec08-card-r09.question_text: When should you turn on your signal if your intended turn sits immediately beyond an intersection?
sec08-card-r09.teaching_text: Waiting until you clear the cross street keeps waiting drivers from thinking you are turning at the corner itself.

sec08-card-r10.question_text: Which two types of turn signals may an Idaho driver legally use?
sec08-card-r10.teaching_text: Knowing standard hand signals keeps you legal and safe if a bulb or fuse fails mid-trip.

sec08-card-r11.question_text: Which maneuver is signaled by extending your left arm and hand straight out the window?
sec08-card-r11.teaching_text: Pointing horizontally straight left mirrors the exact direction your front wheels are about to turn.

sec08-card-r12.question_text: Which maneuver is signaled by extending your left arm and hand upward out the window?
sec08-card-r12.teaching_text: Test-takers often mix up upward and downward hand positions, so link fingertips-up directly with turning right.

sec08-card-r13.question_text: What does extending your left arm and hand downward out the window tell drivers behind you?
sec08-card-r13.teaching_text: Dropping your open palm toward the pavement warns following traffic to ease off the gas immediately.

sec08-card-r14.question_text: Which lane and curb position should you take when approaching to make a right turn?
sec08-card-r14.teaching_text: Staying snug in the right lane blocks impatient cars or bikes from squeezing inside your turn radius.

sec08-card-r15.question_text: Whom must you yield to right before turning right at a corner?
sec08-card-r15.teaching_text: Pedestrians stepping into the parallel crosswalk on green hold priority over your right-turning bumper.

sec08-card-r16.question_text: Where must you check for approaching bicycles before executing a right turn?
sec08-card-r16.teaching_text: Mirrors alone miss cyclists rolling up along the curb, so a quick right-shoulder head check prevents right-hooks.

sec08-card-r17.question_text: Into which lane must you complete a right turn, and what steering error must you avoid?
