sec08-card-r17.teaching_text: Swinging wide into the middle or opposing lane collides with oncoming left-turners sharing the cross street.

sec08-card-r18.question_text: Which lane should you signal into and approach from for a left turn?
sec08-card-r18.teaching_text: Turning left from an outer lane cuts straight across same-direction drivers continuing straight.

sec08-card-r19.question_text: Where within your lane should you position your vehicle before turning left on a two-lane road?
sec08-card-r19.teaching_text: Positioning near the centerline shortens your turn path across oncoming traffic and clarifies your intent.

sec08-card-r20.question_text: Which two road users must you yield to before turning left?
sec08-card-r20.teaching_text: Fixating on an oncoming car gap makes drivers overlook pedestrians already crossing the target street.

sec08-card-r21.question_text: Which target lane must you enter when completing a left turn, and what shortcut must you avoid?
sec08-card-r21.teaching_text: Cutting the corner clips cars waiting at the cross-street stop bar, while drifting wide hits right-turners.

sec08-card-r22.question_text: Under what conditions is a right turn permitted at a steady circular red light?
sec08-card-r22.teaching_text: Skipping the full stop before turning right on red is one of the most ticketed intersection habits.

sec08-card-r23.question_text: Between what kinds of streets may you turn left on a steady circular red light unless posted otherwise?
sec08-card-r23.teaching_text: Turning left on red from a two-way street crosses opposing lanes illegally, whereas one-way-to-one-way mirrors a right turn.

sec08-card-r24.question_text: What does a posted No U-turn sign prohibit?
sec08-card-r24.teaching_text: Busy medians and tight intersections post No U-turn signs where reversing direction blocks through lanes or hits crosswalks.

sec08-card-r25.question_text: How much clear sight distance in both directions is required to make a U-turn near a curve or hillcrest?
sec08-card-r25.teaching_text: Swinging across lanes near a blind crest or bend leaves oncoming highway cars no distance to stop.

sec08-card-r26.question_text: Are U-turns allowed inside a marked no-passing zone?
sec08-card-r26.teaching_text: No-passing zones already flag restricted sightlines where swinging sideways across lanes invites head-on impacts.

sec08-card-r27.question_text: What must you do regarding all other traffic before completing a U-turn?
sec08-card-r27.teaching_text: A U-turning vehicle crosses multiple conflict paths at low speed and holds last priority behind everyone else.

sec08-card-r28.question_text: What do solid painted markings in the center of the road tell you about making a U-turn?
sec08-card-r28.teaching_text: Watch out on the test because Idaho treats solid center pavement stripes as a U-turn prohibition.

sec08-card-r29.question_text: What is the first step in the handbook's permitted U-turn procedure on an open road?
sec08-card-r29.teaching_text: Starting from the far-right edge gives your front wheels enough turning diameter to swing around in one smooth arc.

sec08-card-r30.question_text: Where must you check, and how do you steer, once stopped at the right edge for a handbook U-turn?
sec08-card-r30.teaching_text: Checking ahead, behind, and your left-rear blind spot before turning sharply at low speed prevents surprise T-bones.

sec08-card-r31.question_text: What two actions complete the handbook's U-turn procedure once your vehicle points in the new direction?
sec08-card-r31.teaching_text: Lingering at a crawl after turning around leaves you vulnerable to fast traffic closing from behind.

sec08-card-r32.question_text: Which six driving situations allow an exception to Idaho's general keep-right rule?
sec08-card-r32.teaching_text: Outside of turning left, overtaking, dodging hazards, slow-lane highways, one-ways, or multilane roads, stay right.
sec08-card-r32.must_match_memory_hook: Left-turns, passing, slow-lanes, hazards, one-ways, multilanes

visual_sync.text_span: Left-turns, passing, slow-lanes, hazards, one-ways, multilanes

sec08-card-r33.question_text: How does preparing for a left turn interact with the general keep-far-right rule?
sec08-card-r33.teaching_text: Moving left early avoids cutting across straight-through lanes at the last moment.

sec08-card-r34.question_text: How does overtaking a slower same-direction vehicle affect the keep-far-right rule?
sec08-card-r34.teaching_text: Using the left lane to pass cleanly and returning right once clear keeps two-lane and highway traffic flowing.

sec08-card-r35.question_text: When does a designated slow-traffic lane create an exception to keeping far right?
sec08-card-r35.teaching_text: Steep Idaho grades often post the far-right climbing lane for slow trucks so normal traffic holds the next lane.

sec08-card-r36.question_text: When may you temporarily enter the left lane on a road normally governed by the keep-far-right rule?
sec08-card-r36.teaching_text: Yielding to oncoming traffic first lets you swing around fallen debris, pedestrians, or wildlife safely.

sec08-card-r37.question_text: Does the general keep-far-right rule apply on a street restricted to one-way traffic?
sec08-card-r37.teaching_text: With zero opposing traffic on a one-way street, drivers may choose whichever lane matches their upcoming turn or route.

sec08-card-r38.question_text: How many lanes moving in your direction make a road an exception to the keep-far-right rule?
sec08-card-r38.teaching_text: Even on multilane roads where any same-way lane is open, remember never to impede lawful traffic in the extreme left.

sec08-card-r40.question_text: When must motor vehicles yield to a pedestrian at an intersection crosswalk?
sec08-card-r40.teaching_text: Missing paint lines never erases a pedestrian's right-of-way between opposing sidewalk corners.

sec08-card-r41.question_text: Who holds the right-of-way when a vehicle enters a street from an alley or driveway?
sec08-card-r41.teaching_text: Sidewalk users continue uninterrupted across driveway aprons while drivers wait for a clean gap.

sec08-card-r42.question_text: How do you identify a blind pedestrian to whom motor vehicles must always yield?
sec08-card-r42.teaching_text: Never honk or edge close around a person using a white cane or service dog; wait patiently until clear.

sec08-card-r43.question_text: Who must yield when a pedestrian crosses away from both a crosswalk and an intersection?
sec08-card-r43.teaching_text: Even when a mid-block walker legally owes right-of-way, smart drivers still slow early to prevent an impact.

sec08-card-r44.question_text: When must a pedestrian at an intersection yield to motor vehicles?
sec08-card-r44.teaching_text: Stepping out against a Don't Walk or steady red signal puts walkers straight into green-light traffic.

sec08-card-r45.question_text: Which three actions apply when approaching a Yield sign?
sec08-card-r45.teaching_text: Covering the brake as you slow ensures you can stop short whenever cross-traffic closes the gap.

sec08-card-r46.question_text: After stopping at an alley, driveway, or garage exit, what must you do before pulling onto the street?
sec08-card-r46.teaching_text: Traffic already established on the public street owns priority over any private driveway or garage entry.

sec08-card-r47.question_text: After coming to a full stop at a two-way stop intersection, whom must you yield to?
sec08-card-r47.teaching_text: Assuming cross-street cars also have stop signs when they do not causes severe broadside crashes.

sec08-card-r48.question_text: Who has the right-of-way when vehicles arrive at different times at a four-way stop?
sec08-card-r48.teaching_text: Watching arrival order as you roll up eliminates awkward hesitation waves at busy neighborhood corners.

sec08-card-r49.question_text: Who yields when two vehicles reach a four-way stop at the exact same moment?
sec08-card-r49.teaching_text: Remembering the vehicle on the right goes first breaks simultaneous-arrival ties cleanly without awkward corner hesitation.

sec08-card-r50.question_text: Who must yield when two drivers arrive simultaneously at an intersection with no signs or signals?
sec08-card-r50.teaching_text: Unmarked neighborhood intersections follow the exact same yield-to-the-right tiebreaker as four-way stops.

sec08-card-r51.question_text: What must a driver on the ending street do at an uncontrolled T-intersection before turning left or right?
sec08-card-r51.teaching_text: Through-road drivers from left and right hold priority over traffic on the street that dead-ends.

sec08-card-f13.question_text: Where are vehicle racing, speed exhibitions, and speed contests illegal in Idaho?
sec08-card-f13.teaching_text: Even brief acceleration stunts or side-by-side pulls on public streets violate Idaho's anti-racing statute.

sec08-card-f31.question_text: Which three kinds of problems combine dangerously with excessive speed to cause crashes?
sec08-card-f31.teaching_text: High speed magnifies a tire blowout, misjudged gap, or minor lane mistake into an unrecoverable crash.

sec08-card-r39.question_text: How does the Idaho handbook frame right-of-way between giving it and taking it?
sec08-card-r39.teaching_text: Insisting on your turn when another driver makes a mistake causes preventable crashes that yielding avoids.

sec09-card-f09.question_text: Where do hills, curves, and roadside obstructions forbid passing on a two-lane road?
sec09-card-f09.teaching_text: Blocked sightlines hide fast-closing oncoming traffic inside the exact lane you would occupy to overtake.

sec09-card-f10.question_text: Unless traffic controls permit it, within how many feet of an intersection is passing banned?
sec09-card-f10.teaching_text: Cross-street drivers turning onto the road scan their target lane, not expecting an overtaking car wrong-way.

sec09-card-f11.question_text: Within what distance of a railroad crossing is overtaking prohibited unless traffic controls say otherwise?
sec09-card-f11.teaching_text: Approaching trains and mandatory-stop buses or tankers create abrupt hazards right ahead of the tracks.

sec09-card-f12.question_text: What visibility condition bars overtaking within 100 feet of any bridge or tunnel?
sec09-card-f12.teaching_text: Narrow bridge parapets and dark tunnel portals eliminate shoulder escape room when oncoming view is blocked.

sec09-card-f13.question_text: Is overtaking allowed when a stopped school bus is loading or unloading passengers?
sec09-card-f13.teaching_text: Young riders step across lanes from blind angles around the bus bumper expecting every motorist to halt.

sec09-card-f14.question_text: Why must you never overtake a vehicle stopped ahead at a marked or unmarked crosswalk?
sec09-card-f14.teaching_text: The stopped car's hood hides the crossing pedestrian from your view until they step into your lane.

sec09-card-f15.question_text: Is a pass ever lawful if completing it forces your wheels off the pavement or roadway?
sec09-card-f15.teaching_text: Dropping tires onto soft dirt or gravel shoulders at passing speed triggers violent fishtails and rollovers.

sec09-card-f04.question_text: Which two vehicles must your passing maneuver avoid interfering with?
sec09-card-f04.teaching_text: Forcing either the oncoming car or the overtaken driver to brake or swerve proves the gap was too tight.

sec09-card-f05.question_text: What certainty must you have before pulling out to overtake?
sec09-card-f05.teaching_text: Guessing on a borderline gap at highway speed leaves nowhere to hide if oncoming traffic is faster than judged.

sec09-card-f06.question_text: What signal and mirror check come before steering back into your original lane after passing?
sec09-card-f06.teaching_text: Waiting until the passed vehicle shows clearly in your rearview mirror prevents clipping their front bumper.

sec09-card-f07.question_text: What is the safest move if you realize mid-pass that you cannot finish safely?
sec09-card-f07.teaching_text: Flooring the gas into a shrinking gap courts a head-on crash, whereas braking smoothly lets you tuck back behind.

sec09-card-f08.question_text: Even outside No Passing signs or solid stripes, who holds final responsibility for judging a safe pass?
sec09-card-f08.teaching_text: Dashed yellow paint only reflects road geometry, never accounting for fog, glare, or an oncoming pickup right ahead.

sec09-card-f16.question_text: Under what exact road, vehicle, towing, zone, and return rules does Idaho allow exceeding the limit by up to fifteen miles per hour to pass?
sec09-card-f16.teaching_text: Idaho's special passing allowance excludes towing rigs, work zones, multilane roads, and zones posted below fifty-five.

sec09-card-f17.question_text: When is passing on the right allowed on a two-lane two-way road?
sec09-card-f17.teaching_text: Only a wide paved lane beside a left-turning car permits passing right, never dropping wheels onto unpaved shoulder.

sec09-card-f18.question_text: When may you pass on the right on a one-way or multilane street?
sec09-card-f18.teaching_text: Dedicated right-hand travel lanes allow overtaking slower left-lane traffic provided you never leave the paved roadway.

sec09-card-f19.question_text: Why must you check mirrors and blind spots before pulling left to overtake?
sec09-card-f19.teaching_text: Pulling into the opposing lane without checking over your left shoulder sideswipes a faster driver already overtaking you.

sec09-card-f20.question_text: What communication step precedes steering into the left lane to pass?
sec09-card-f20.teaching_text: Warning both the driver ahead and anyone behind prevents two vehicles from claiming the passing lane simultaneously.

sec09-card-f21.question_text: Walk through the exact mirror and signal sequence for returning to the right lane after overtaking?
sec09-card-f21.teaching_text: Confirming visual clearance in your center glass before blinking right tells the passed driver you are merging cleanly.

sec09-card-f22.question_text: How should you respond if the vehicle you are overtaking begins drifting toward your lane?
sec09-card-f22.teaching_text: A sharp horn tap snaps an inattentive driver's eyes back to their mirrors before fenders make contact.

sec09-card-f23.question_text: How much distance ahead of an oncoming vehicle must remain when you finish a pass?
sec09-card-f23.teaching_text: Two highway vehicles close two hundred feet in roughly one second, making that buffer the absolute safety floor.
sec09-card-f23.must_match_memory_hook: Clear lane before two hundred feet

visual_sync.text_span: Clear lane before two hundred feet

sec09-card-f24.question_text: Where must your pass be completely finished relative to an upcoming No Passing zone?
sec09-card-f24.teaching_text: Crossing back over a solid yellow line or pennant sign means you lingered into a blind curve or crest.

sec09-card-f25.question_text: Where inside your lane should you ease when another driver overtakes you, and why?
sec09-card-f25.teaching_text: Hugging the right side of your lane widens side clearance and opens the passing driver's view down the road.

sec09-card-f26.question_text: What speed rule applies to your right foot while another vehicle is overtaking you?
sec09-card-f26.teaching_text: Speeding up while someone passes is unlawful and traps them head-on in the opposing lane.

sec09-card-f27.question_text: Why should you stay alert to the overtaking driver's progress while being passed?
sec09-card-f27.teaching_text: Being ready to brake gently opens an instant escape gap if an oncoming vehicle surprises the passer.

sec09-card-r01.question_text: When, if ever, may an uninvited motorist join or drive between vehicles in a funeral procession?
sec09-card-r01.teaching_text: Breaking into a tight low-headway procession splits escorted mourners and causes chain-reaction fender-benders.
sec09-card-r01.must_match_memory_hook: Never cut in unless police direct

visual_sync.text_span: Never cut in unless police direct

sec09-card-r02.question_text: When is passing a funeral procession in the right lane allowed on a multilane highway?
sec09-card-r02.teaching_text: Otherwise overtake on the left so procession cars exiting right toward the cemetery are never cut off.

sec09-card-r03.question_text: May you drive through an intersection across an active funeral procession when your traffic signal turns green?
sec09-card-r03.teaching_text: Idaho gives an active funeral line continuous intersection passage regardless of signal changes.

sec09-card-r04.question_text: Who holds the right-of-way when you encounter a funeral procession in Idaho?
sec09-card-r04.teaching_text: Unlike states where yielding is mere courtesy, Idaho mandates yielding right-of-way to properly lit funeral lines.

sec09-card-r05.question_text: Which exterior lights must every vehicle inside a funeral procession turn on?
sec09-card-r05.teaching_text: Continuous front and rear lamps mark every participating car clearly for cross-street motorists.

sec09-card-r06.question_text: How do the first and last vehicles in an Idaho funeral procession mark the line's start and finish?
sec09-card-r06.teaching_text: Flashing hazard or escort lights on the bookend vehicles show waiting cross traffic when the final car clears.

sec09-card-r07.question_text: How many delayed trailing vehicles require a slow driver on a rural or two-lane highway to pull off?
sec09-card-r07.teaching_text: Idaho sets the rural two-lane turnout trigger at three stacked cars, lower than five-car rules in other states.

sec09-card-r08.question_text: During what daylight window may vehicles capped at twenty-five miles per hour use public highways, and what exception applies?
sec09-card-r08.teaching_text: After-dark operation requires non-interstate farm or snow gear carrying flashing lights visible five hundred feet.

sec09-card-r09.question_text: Which two controls and rear marker must slow-moving vehicles carry?
sec09-card-r09.teaching_text: High-contrast fluorescent-and-reflective triangles warn highway traffic long before turn signals become visible.

sec09-card-r10.question_text: What does tailgating mean, and how does it rank among collision causes?
sec09-card-r10.teaching_text: Riding bumpers erases human reaction time the instant traffic ahead taps the brakes.

sec09-card-r11.question_text: What basic stopping standard governs how much space you leave behind the car ahead?
sec09-card-r11.teaching_text: Your front gap must absorb both perception-reaction delay and full tire braking footage.

sec09-card-r12.question_text: What mechanical system must stay in good working order for your following gap to protect you?
sec09-card-r12.teaching_text: Worn pads or spongy hydraulic fluid stretch stopping distance right past a three-second following cushion.

sec09-card-r13.question_text: Why should you know and test brake feel across changing surfaces, especially wet, icy, or snowy pavement?
sec09-card-r13.teaching_text: Gentle early brake checks away from traffic reveal hidden black ice before an intersection demands a hard stop.

sec09-card-r14.question_text: What minimum following interval does the Idaho handbook recommend, and when do you add more?
sec09-card-r14.teaching_text: High freeway speeds and slick storms stretch braking distance faster than dry low-speed town streets.

sec09-card-r15.question_text: What kind of roadside marker do you pick to run the three-second following check?
sec09-card-r15.teaching_text: Fixed objects beside the pavement give an unmistakable timing line unlike moving shadows or cars.

sec09-card-r16.question_text: At what exact moment do you start counting your three-second following check?
sec09-card-r16.teaching_text: Timing from their rear bumper passing the sign measures the true clear air between bumpers.

sec09-card-r17.question_text: How long should your count take before reaching the reference object in good weather versus bad weather?
sec09-card-r17.teaching_text: Notice Idaho calls for an interval several times longer when rain, snow, or ice degrades traction.

sec09-card-r18.question_text: Why should you preserve open space on all sides of your vehicle, not only ahead?
sec09-card-r18.teaching_text: Open side and rear margins give you an instant steering escape lane if obstacles block the front.

sec09-card-r19.question_text: Where within your lane should you track, and what two options should your front space preserve?
sec09-card-r19.teaching_text: Tracking centered maximizes buffer from both oncoming traffic and shoulder drop-offs while preserving sightlines.

sec09-card-r20.question_text: What is the calmest way to handle a driver following your rear bumper too closely?
sec09-card-r20.teaching_text: Gradually slowing widens your own front cushion and encourages impatient drivers to move harmlessly ahead.

sec09-card-r21.question_text: How close and in what orientation must you park along a public curb or road edge?
sec09-card-r21.teaching_text: Keeping tires within eighteen inches and facing traffic flow keeps fenders out of active lanes.

sec09-card-r22.question_text: Which transmission setting secures a parked automatic vehicle versus a manual-shift vehicle?
sec09-card-r22.teaching_text: Engaging Park or a low gear backs up the parking brake with mechanical drivetrain resistance.

sec09-card-r23.question_text: What final anti-theft and safety step applies every time you leave a parked vehicle?
sec09-card-r23.teaching_text: Removing ignition keys and locking doors prevents both joyride thefts and curious children releasing brakes.

sec09-card-f01.question_text: Unless a green arrow or sign directs otherwise, whom must a left-turning driver yield to?
sec09-card-f01.teaching_text: Straight-through opposing traffic holds continuous lane priority unless a protected turn phase holds them red.

sec09-card-f02.question_text: Whom must motorists yield to inside an active highway construction zone?
sec09-card-f02.teaching_text: Dump trucks and foot crews moving across cone tapers have restricted sightlines and statutory work-zone protection.

sec09-card-f03.question_text: Which intersection rules govern traffic when a signal goes dark during a power outage?
sec09-card-f03.teaching_text: Stopping completely on every approach prevents lethal T-bone crashes when green-and-red bulbs lose power.

sec10-card-f04.question_text: What rule applies to parking on a sidewalk or inside a dedicated bicycle lane?
sec10-card-f04.teaching_text: Forcing cyclists or pedestrians out around a parked fender pushes vulnerable users directly into live traffic.

sec10-card-f05.question_text: What violation occurs when you park alongside the street-facing side of an already parked car?
sec10-card-f05.teaching_text: Blocking an active travel lane while boxing curb-parked drivers in creates blind bottlenecks and sideswipes.

sec10-card-f06.question_text: Is parking ever allowed inside an intersection?
sec10-card-f06.teaching_text: Any stationary car inside cross-street lanes chokes turning radii and hides crossing traffic.

sec10-card-f07.question_text: Within how many feet of railroad tracks is parking prohibited?
sec10-card-f07.teaching_text: Vehicles parked near crossbucks block flashing gate arms and hide oncoming locomotives from approaching drivers.

sec10-card-f08.question_text: Where on bridges and overpasses is parking allowed?
sec10-card-f08.teaching_text: Guardrails eliminate shoulder escape width on elevated spans, turning any parked car into a lane hazard.

sec10-card-f09.question_text: What parking rule protects driveway entrances?
sec10-card-f09.teaching_text: Obstructing an apron traps residents inside their property and blocks emergency responders from entering.

sec10-card-f10.question_text: How much curb space around a fire hydrant must stay completely clear of parked vehicles?
sec10-card-f10.teaching_text: Firefighters need fast, unobstructed curb access to wrench heavy supply hoses onto pressurized hydrants.

sec10-card-f11.question_text: Within what distance of a crosswalk is parking prohibited?
sec10-card-f11.teaching_text: Setbacks let approaching motorists spot children and walkers at the curb before they step out.

sec10-card-f12.question_text: How far back from a stop sign, yield sign, or traffic signal is parking barred?
sec10-card-f12.teaching_text: Tall vans or pickups parked close to intersection posts hide critical red-and-yellow warnings from view.

sec10-card-f13.question_text: What no-parking distance applies beside a fire-station driveway?
sec10-card-f13.teaching_text: Wide ladder trucks and engines need extra curb swing room when rolling out under emergency sirens.

sec10-card-f14.question_text: May you park along a freeway or other controlled-access highway for non-emergencies?
sec10-card-f14.teaching_text: High-speed shoulders exist solely for breakdowns and emergency stops, never casual rest or phone breaks.

sec10-card-f15.question_text: What do a no-parking sign or a red-painted curb indicate in Idaho?
sec10-card-f15.teaching_text: Red paint marks fire lanes and critical sight zones where stopping blocks emergency or turning clearance.

sec10-card-f01.question_text: Which way must you turn your front wheels when parking downhill?
sec10-card-f01.teaching_text: Angling tires into the curb or shoulder stops a rolling vehicle before its nose swings into traffic.

sec10-card-f02.question_text: Which way do front wheels point when parking uphill next to a curb?
sec10-card-f02.teaching_text: Turning left lets the back of your right front tire wedge cleanly against the raised curb face.

sec10-card-f03.question_text: How do you angle your wheels when parking uphill where no curb exists?
sec10-card-f03.teaching_text: With no raised concrete to catch a left-angled tire, turning right guides any roll off the road.

sec10-card-f16.question_text: What vehicle credential is required to use disability-reserved stalls, and what faces unauthorized drivers?
sec10-card-f16.teaching_text: Reserved close-in spaces keep mobility-aid users safe from long parking-lot crossings and carry citation fines.

sec10-card-f17.question_text: What payment and time-limit rules apply when a person with a disability parks a symbol-displaying car in a reserved space?
sec10-card-f17.teaching_text: Idaho's handbook specifically notes exempting properly credentialed disability-space users from meter fees and time limits.

sec10-card-f18.question_text: Why should you inspect behind your vehicle before climbing into the driver's seat to back up?
sec10-card-f18.teaching_text: Toddlers, pets, and bikes below trunk height vanish completely inside rear blind zones once you sit down.

sec10-card-f19.question_text: How should you position your arm and head to see properly while reversing?
sec10-card-f19.teaching_text: Twisting to look directly out the rear glass exposes wide side-and-rear angles that tiny mirrors miss.

sec10-card-f20.question_text: How fast should you reverse, and how long must you keep looking backward?
sec10-card-f20.teaching_text: Turning forward while the car still rolls backward invites last-foot fender taps against poles or walkers.

sec10-card-f21.question_text: What general rule governs reversing inside active traffic?
sec10-card-f21.teaching_text: Approaching drivers expect forward flow and rarely recognize white reverse lamps until closing distance vanishes.

sec10-card-f22.question_text: What must you do if you accidentally drive past your intended interstate exit?
sec10-card-f22.teaching_text: Backing up or U-turning on an interstate pits stationary steel against eighty-mile-per-hour traffic.

sec10-card-f23.question_text: Where on freeways, expressways, and controlled-access roads is reversing prohibited?
sec10-card-f23.teaching_text: Even reversing along a paved freeway shoulder is unlawful and courts catastrophic high-speed rear-end crashes.

sec10-card-f24.question_text: On ordinary non-freeway streets, under what two conditions is reversing allowed?
sec10-card-f24.teaching_text: Backing drivers carry the burden of yielding to every moving vehicle and pedestrian nearby.

sec10-card-f25.question_text: Which two mental states must you guard against during freeway driving?
sec10-card-f25.teaching_text: Wide, signal-free lanes lull tired minds into delayed reactions unless you scan mirrors and take breaks.

sec10-card-f26.question_text: What top rural and urban interstate speeds does the Idaho handbook allow when designated, unposted lower, and weather-safe?
sec10-card-f26.teaching_text: Idaho's eighty-mile-per-hour rural cap applies only on designated stretches in good weather with no lower sign.

sec10-card-f27.question_text: Which three sequential sections make up a standard freeway entrance?
sec10-card-f27.teaching_text: Knowing each section's job prevents stopping prematurely on the ramp or merging before building speed.

sec10-card-f28.question_text: What visual check should you begin while still on the freeway entrance ramp?
sec10-card-f28.teaching_text: Spotting gaps early on the curved ramp lets you time your throttle smoothly once the lane straightens.

sec10-card-f29.question_text: How do the acceleration lane and the merging area divide your freeway entry?
sec10-card-f29.teaching_text: Matching highway velocity before crossing the broken line prevents forcing fast right-lane trucks to slam brakes.

sec10-card-r01.question_text: Which three kinds of stops should you map out ahead of a long freeway trip?
sec10-card-r01.teaching_text: Knowing rural service exits ahead of time prevents running dry or pushing past drowsiness on remote stretches.

sec10-card-r02.question_text: Even for a short local freeway hop, which four identifiers should you know before leaving?
sec10-card-r02.teaching_text: Memorizing your exit number beforehand stops frantic GPS glances and last-second dives across gore stripes.

sec10-card-r03.question_text: What four trip details should you share with someone before heading out?
sec10-card-r03.teaching_text: Across mountain and desert corridors without cell bars, an informed contact knows exactly where searchers should look.

sec10-card-r04.question_text: Why must you verify the entrance sign before taking a ramp, and what two moves are banned if wrong?
sec10-card-r04.teaching_text: Entering an off-ramp wrong-way or cutting across grass medians invites catastrophic head-on freeway collisions.

sec10-card-r05.question_text: May ordinary motorists use paved or gravel crossovers cutting through a freeway median?
sec10-card-r05.teaching_text: Authorized turnarounds serve patrol cruisers, plows, and ambulances only; civilian U-turns surprise fast left-lane traffic.

sec10-card-r06.question_text: How do you legally turn around or leave a freeway once past an exit?
sec10-card-r06.teaching_text: Overpass interchanges let you exit, cross safely at low speed, and re-enter going the opposite way.

sec10-card-r07.question_text: What traffic checks, signal, and shoulder glance help you pick a freeway gap from the ramp?
sec10-card-r07.teaching_text: Checking both the car ahead on the ramp and left-shoulder highway traffic prevents rear-ending a hesitant merger.

sec10-card-r08.question_text: As the entrance ramp straightens out, how do you balance speed and right-of-way?
sec10-card-r08.teaching_text: Through-lane freeway traffic holds legal priority, so entering drivers adjust throttle smoothly to slot into gaps.

sec10-card-r09.question_text: What final switch step completes a freeway merge once you match flow in the lane?
sec10-card-r09.teaching_text: Leaving your left signal flashing after entering tricks center-lane drivers into thinking you are moving left again.

sec10-card-r10.question_text: Which ramp design features and traffic conditions call for extra freeway-entry caution?
sec10-card-r10.teaching_text: Older urban interchanges pack short acceleration taper lengths that demand brisk throttle and early gap spotting.

sec10-card-r11.question_text: What may become necessary if bumper-to-bumper freeway traffic leaves no merge opening?
sec10-card-r11.teaching_text: Slowing early on the ramp preserves runway ahead instead of running out of pavement beside trucks.

sec10-card-r12.question_text: If heavy traffic on a short acceleration lane forces a stop, where must you halt?
sec10-card-r12.teaching_text: Stopping at the very tip of the taper forces a dangerous zero-speed pullout straight into highway traffic.

sec10-card-r13.question_text: How should you manage your speed once established on a freeway?
sec10-card-r13.teaching_text: Accordion-style surging and coasting creates phantom brake waves and raises rear-end risk.

sec10-card-r14.question_text: Alongside maximum limits, what other speed sign may a freeway post?
sec10-card-r14.teaching_text: Crawling far below fast freeway traffic creates dangerous closing-speed differentials that trigger severe rear-end collisions.

sec10-card-r15.question_text: What should you do if you or your vehicle cannot comfortably maintain freeway speed?
sec10-card-r15.teaching_text: Taking parallel surface highways keeps underpowered or nervous drivers safe without obstructing interstate traffic.

sec10-card-r16.question_text: Which freeway lanes serve normal cruising versus faster traffic and overtaking?
sec10-card-r16.teaching_text: Keeping the leftmost lane open for passing prevents frustrated drivers from weaving across right-hand lanes.

sec10-card-r17.question_text: Why should through drivers avoid the far-right freeway lane during rush hours?
sec10-card-r17.teaching_text: Cruising in the center lane past busy commuter on-ramps gives entering streams friction-free merging space.

sec10-card-r18.question_text: At least how many seconds ahead must you signal before changing freeway lanes or exiting?
sec10-card-r18.teaching_text: At seventy-five or eighty miles per hour, one hundred feet flashes by in under a second, so Idaho uses five seconds.

sec10-card-r19.question_text: Even on non-interstate divided roads, when may you cross a barrier or unpaved median?
sec10-card-r19.teaching_text: Driving across grass ditches or cable barriers damages steering gear and launches cars into opposing lanes.

sec10-card-r20.question_text: How do you set up a smooth departure from a freeway?
sec10-card-r20.teaching_text: Tracking overhead guide signs into the exit lane early prevents dangerous last-second cuts across painted gores.

sec12-card-f01.question_text: Which three attitudes keep mixed traffic safe when cars, bikes, walkers, and trucks share pavement?
sec12-card-f01.teaching_text: Different vehicle sizes and speeds coexist smoothly only when motorists stay alert and respect others' legal space.

sec12-card-f02.question_text: What immediate action is required when an emergency or police vehicle approaches with siren or flashing red or blue lights?
sec12-card-f02.teaching_text: Clearing to the right curb immediately opens a predictable center corridor for high-speed emergency responders.

sec12-card-f03.question_text: What speed adjustment applies whenever approaching a stopped police, emergency, tow, or incident-response rig flashing lights?
sec12-card-f03.teaching_text: Officers, tow operators, and stranded motorists work inches from live white fog lines.

sec12-card-f04.question_text: Along with slowing, what lane move is required near a stopped flashing responder on a road with two or more same-way lanes?
sec12-card-f04.teaching_text: Putting an entire empty lane between your mirror and roadside crews shields workers from wind blast and drift.

sec12-card-f05.question_text: Around which neighborhood, school, transit, and recreational spots must you actively scan for pedestrians?
sec12-card-f05.teaching_text: Walkers cluster wherever errands, transit stops, trails, and playgrounds meet neighborhood streets.

sec12-card-f06.question_text: Does a pedestrian lose intersection right-of-way when the corner crosswalk has no painted white lines?
sec12-card-f06.teaching_text: Every sidewalk-to-sidewalk intersection extension forms a legal unmarked crosswalk whether striped or bare asphalt.

sec12-card-f07.question_text: Who yields when a vehicle crosses a sidewalk entering a street from an alley or driveway?
sec12-card-f07.teaching_text: Fences and walls often hide approaching pedestrians until your hood nears the sidewalk edge.

sec12-card-f08.question_text: Which two mobility aids trigger mandatory yielding to a visually impaired pedestrian?
sec12-card-f08.teaching_text: Blind travelers navigate by traffic sound and cane sweep, counting on full stops from every approaching vehicle.

sec12-card-f09.question_text: Who holds legal right-of-way when a pedestrian crosses mid-block away from any crosswalk or intersection?
sec12-card-f09.teaching_text: Even when mid-block walkers owe priority to vehicles, alert drivers still stay ready to brake.

sec12-card-f10.question_text: When must pedestrians at a controlled corner yield to traffic?
sec12-card-f10.teaching_text: Steady red hands and red traffic phases clear turning and cross-street lanes safely when everyone obeys.

sec12-card-f11.question_text: What must you do if a pedestrian is already mid-street without a painted crosswalk even though you technically hold priority?
sec12-card-f11.teaching_text: Technical right-of-way never excuses striking a human being already exposed on open asphalt.

sec12-card-f12.question_text: What must you do when your red light turns green while a pedestrian is still finishing the crosswalk?
sec12-card-f12.teaching_text: A green bulb grants permission to proceed only after the intersection and crosswalk empty safely.

sec12-card-f13.question_text: Why must you stop in the left lane when a car in the right lane stops at an intersection for a pedestrian?
sec12-card-f13.teaching_text: The stopped right-lane vehicle screens the walking person from your view until they step across its left fender.

sec12-card-f14.question_text: Under what lighting and weather conditions must you exercise extreme care for pedestrians?
sec12-card-f14.teaching_text: Dark coats in rain or low sun glare blend walkers into asphalt shadows until braking margin is tight.

sec12-card-f15.question_text: What habit protects young children before you climb into a parked car in child-active areas?
sec12-card-f15.teaching_text: A five-second walk-around spots toddlers sitting or playing inside tall SUV bumper blind zones.

sec12-card-f16.question_text: What specific hazard must you watch for while backing down a residential driveway?
sec12-card-f16.teaching_text: Kids chasing toys or waving goodbye often run right behind moving tailpipes without understanding reverse gear.

sec12-card-f17.question_text: Why do visible roadside children and parked cars call for extra slowing?
sec12-card-f17.teaching_text: Playmates rarely travel solo, so spotting one child near parked bumpers warns a second may dart out.

sec12-card-f18.question_text: What legal road access, rights, and rule duties apply to horseback riders in Idaho?
sec12-card-f18.teaching_text: Mounted riders legally share most public highways and follow standard traffic rules alongside cars.

sec12-card-f19.question_text: How should you adjust speed and behavior as you near a horseback rider?
sec12-card-f19.teaching_text: Rushing past kicking up gravel or engine roar can panic a thousand-pound animal onto the roadway.

sec12-card-f20.question_text: Why must you never blow your horn near a horse?
sec12-card-f20.teaching_text: An unexpected blast triggers flight instincts that can unseat the rider or send the animal into your hood.

sec12-card-f21.question_text: What should you do if a rider ahead is visibly struggling to control a spooked animal?
sec12-card-f21.teaching_text: Halting calmly back gives the rider quiet space to regain control without adding moving sheet metal.

sec12-card-f22.question_text: What roadway status and travel direction govern bicyclists in Idaho?
sec12-card-f22.teaching_text: Wrong-way cycling doubles closing speed at driveways and corners, so bikes ride with traffic flow.

sec12-card-f23.question_text: Where do cyclists normally ride, and which four situations let them leave the right edge?
sec12-card-f23.teaching_text: Broken glass, storm grates, left turns, passing, or narrow lanes legally bring riders away from the gutter.

sec12-card-f24.question_text: How should you position your car to overtake a cyclist, including the minimum safe side margin?
sec12-card-f24.teaching_text: Moving into the adjacent lane or waiting for oncoming traffic beats squeezing past inside tight curb space.

sec12-card-f25.question_text: Why must you slow down extra when passing children riding bicycles?
sec12-card-f25.teaching_text: Glancing back at a car sound often pulls a young rider's handlebars straight toward your fender.

sec12-card-f26.question_text: How does Idaho law allow a bicyclist to treat a stop sign?
sec12-card-f26.teaching_text: Idaho pioneered letting cyclists roll cautiously through clear stop signs after yielding to any conflicting traffic.

sec12-card-f27.question_text: What stopping and yielding rule governs a bicyclist turning right at a red traffic signal in Idaho?
sec12-card-f27.teaching_text: Just like stop signs, Idaho lets right-turning cyclists treat a clear red signal as a yield.

sec12-card-f28.question_text: Where must you look before turning right from a stop so you do not clip a cyclist?
sec12-card-f28.teaching_text: A cyclist rolling up the curb side while you stared left for cars sits right beside your passenger door.

sec12-card-f29.question_text: What should you do when preparing a right turn with a bicyclist riding just ahead of you?
sec12-card-f29.teaching_text: Accelerating around a rider just to slam brakes and turn across their front wheel causes right-hook crashes.

sec12-card-f30.question_text: What specific crash name describes turning right across a straight-riding bicyclist's path?
sec12-card-f30.teaching_text: Misjudging a bike's brisk twenty-mile-per-hour pace traps the rider broadside against your passenger fender.

sec12-card-f31.question_text: Why does turning right across a striped bicycle lane require deliberate mirror-and-shoulder checks?
sec12-card-f31.teaching_text: Treat a striped bike lane like any active travel lane you would never cut across blindly.

sec12-card-f32.question_text: How many times should you scan intersection corners when driving straight through or turning?
sec12-card-f32.teaching_text: Brisk cyclists and runners cover sidewalk approaches fast enough to enter a corner after your first glance.

sec12-card-f33.question_text: What do dashed bicycle-lane lines near an intersection permit, and how do you use them for a right turn?
sec12-card-f33.teaching_text: Merging safely into the dashed zone before turning right blocks right-hook conflicts from behind.

sec12-card-f34.question_text: Are bicyclists required to ride on sidewalks in Idaho communities?
sec12-card-f34.teaching_text: Adult commuters usually belong on the street even where local ordinances allow sidewalk riding.

sec12-card-f35.question_text: Why do residential driveways require extreme caution in both directions?
sec12-card-f35.teaching_text: Low-sitting kids on small sidewalk bikes move much faster than walkers across hidden driveway aprons.

sec12-card-f36.question_text: How should you pass child cyclists differently from experienced adult riders?
sec12-card-f36.teaching_text: Kids still learning balance and hand brakes weave abruptly without checking behind.

sec12-card-f37.question_text: Why must you never rush a turn or squeeze past a cyclist just to catch a yellow light or gap?
sec12-card-f37.teaching_text: Saving thirty seconds at a red light never justifies brushing inches from an unprotected rider.

sec12-card-f38.question_text: Why might a cyclist move into the center of a narrow lane, and how should you follow?
sec12-card-f38.teaching_text: Claiming center on pinch-point bridges or curbed narrows stops cars from attempting an impossible side-by-side squeeze.

sec12-card-f39.question_text: Which three physical and motion traits make cyclists easy to overlook unless you look deliberately?
sec12-card-f39.teaching_text: Scanning consciously for slim silhouettes breaks car-only tunnel vision at busy intersections.

sec12-card-r01.question_text: What is Idaho's minimum bicycle passing clearance, and how does higher vehicle speed change it?
sec12-card-r01.teaching_text: Fifty-five-mile-per-hour air turbulence can pull a lightweight road bike sideways unless you give generous extra width.

sec12-card-r02.question_text: When must you wait before crossing into the opposing lane to pass a cyclist?
sec12-card-r02.teaching_text: Slowing to bike pace for five seconds until opposing traffic clears keeps everyone safe.

sec12-card-r03.question_text: How can you confirm nonverbally that a cyclist sees your car at an intersection?
sec12-card-r03.teaching_text: Mutual eye contact and a returned nod beat guessing whether a rider noticed your bumper.

sec12-card-r04.question_text: Why should you avoid honking right behind or beside a bicyclist?
sec12-card-r04.teaching_text: A sudden loud blast at close range can jolt a cyclist into swerving under your front wheel.

sec12-card-r05.question_text: What check is essential before swinging your driver's door open from a parallel parking spot?
sec12-card-r05.teaching_text: Dooring throws an approaching cyclist straight into handlebar steel or passing lane traffic.

sec12-card-r06.question_text: How does reaching across your body with your far hand to open the car door protect cyclists?
sec12-card-r06.teaching_text: Using your right hand on the left door naturally swivels your chest toward the mirror and rear blind spot.

sec12-card-r07.question_text: How do timely turn signals help bicyclists sharing the street with you?
sec12-card-r07.teaching_text: Early blinkers let nearby riders brake or position left before your car turns across curb lanes.

sec12-card-r08.question_text: Why is stopping or parking inside a marked bicycle lane prohibited?
sec12-card-r08.teaching_text: Treating a bike lane like a loading zone forces riders to merge suddenly into faster car lanes.

sec12-card-r09.question_text: What is a sharrow, and what does it indicate inside a travel lane?
sec12-card-r09.teaching_text: Bike-and-chevron stencils guide riders clear of the parked-car door zone inside shared lanes.

sec12-card-r10.question_text: On what lane width do engineers paint shared-lane markings?
sec12-card-r10.teaching_text: Sharrows signal that motorists should change lanes to pass rather than squeezing beside the bike.

sec12-card-r11.question_text: Which three safety jobs does a shared-lane marking perform for drivers and riders?
sec12-card-r11.teaching_text: Pointed chevrons cue motorists where bikes ride, remind safe passing, and curb wrong-way riding.

sec12-card-r12.question_text: What roadside sign can supplement or replace painted shared-lane sharrows?
sec12-card-r12.teaching_text: That sign confirms riders legitimately occupy the center of narrow lanes where side-by-side sharing is unsafe.

sec12-card-r13.question_text: How do a motorcyclist's legal rights, responsibilities, and traffic rules compare with car drivers'?
sec12-card-r13.teaching_text: Every intersection right-of-way and lane protection owed to a sedan applies equally to two wheels.

sec12-card-r14.question_text: Why are approaching motorcycles harder to spot and judge for closing speed than cars?
sec12-card-r14.teaching_text: A narrow single headlight looks farther away and slower than a wide pair of car beams.

sec12-card-r15.question_text: What double-check is vital before turning left across an oncoming motorcycle?
sec12-card-r15.teaching_text: Left-turning cars misjudging oncoming motorcycle speed cause the single deadliest two-vehicle bike crash.

sec12-card-r16.question_text: Why shouldn't you pull out immediately in front of an approaching motorcycle flashing a turn signal?
sec12-card-r16.teaching_text: Many motorcycles lack self-canceling turn switches, so riders sometimes cruise straight with an old blinker flashing.

sec12-card-r17.question_text: May a car ever share side-by-side space inside the same lane beside a motorcycle?
sec12-card-r17.teaching_text: Motorcyclists shift left and right across their lane constantly to see ahead and dodge road hazards.

sec12-card-r18.question_text: How should you adjust following distance behind a motorcycle in rain or slick conditions?
sec12-card-r18.teaching_text: Painted stripes, wet leaves, and oil slicks challenge two-wheel balance far more sharply than four tires.

sec12-card-r19.question_text: Which minor surface flaws can force a motorcyclist to swerve or slow unexpectedly?
sec12-card-r19.teaching_text: Loose pebbles, bridge grates, or slick steel manhole lids barely felt in a sedan can dump a bike.

sec12-card-r20.question_text: When must you visually check mirrors and blind spots specifically for motorcycles?
sec12-card-r20.teaching_text: Compact bikes tuck easily behind A-pillars and C-pillars whenever cars merge or clear intersections.

sec12-card-r21.question_text: How should you communicate speed and path changes to nearby motorcyclists?
sec12-card-r21.teaching_text: Early turn indicators and gentle brake-light taps let riders adjust traction smoothly without panic-locking wheels.

sec12-card-r22.question_text: How much following time does the Idaho handbook call for behind a motorcycle?
sec12-card-r22.teaching_text: Stretching beyond the standard three-second car minimum accounts for crisp motorcycle braking and sudden hazard swerves.

sec12-card-r23.question_text: Which three physical realities distinguish large trucks and buses from passenger cars?
sec12-card-r23.teaching_text: Height, length, and heavy mass demand wider turns, longer passes, and far more braking highway ahead.

sec12-card-r24.question_text: Why do operating snowplows demand extra following distance and caution?
sec12-card-r24.teaching_text: Plow blades cast dense snow plumes across lanes that erase tail lamps and road edges instantly.

sec12-card-r25.question_text: Where around a large truck or bus must you avoid lingering?
sec12-card-r25.teaching_text: Cruising beside trailer wheels traps your car invisible if wind gusts or tire blowouts push the rig.

sec12-card-r26.question_text: How do you know while following a large truck or bus that its driver cannot see you?
sec12-card-r26.teaching_text: Tucking right behind trailer doors hides your car completely from both cab-mounted side mirrors.

sec12-card-r27.question_text: Why should you widen your gap behind a tall truck or bus beyond mirror visibility?
sec12-card-r27.teaching_text: Hanging close turns the trailer into a solid wall hiding curves, debris, and overhead signs.

sec12-card-r28.question_text: How should you pace your pass around a large vehicle, and when may you merge back in?
sec12-card-r28.teaching_text: Waiting until the entire tractor cab shows in your rearview mirror preserves crucial front buffer.

sec12-card-r29.question_text: Why must you preserve a large vehicle's front safety gap when merging ahead of it?
sec12-card-r29.teaching_text: Truckers intentionally leave long front buffers because loaded rigs cannot shed highway speed quickly.

sec12-card-r30.question_text: In the Idaho handbook's dry-road example, how far does a loaded truck with adjusted brakes travel stopping from fifty-five miles per hour?
sec12-card-r30.teaching_text: Four hundred fifty feet exceeds an entire football field including end zones on dry pavement alone.

sec12-card-r31.question_text: Why must you give large trucks and buses extra intersection space during sharp turns?
sec12-card-r31.teaching_text: Long trailer wheelbases track sharply inward around corners, forcing wide setups across adjacent traffic lanes.

sec12-card-r32.question_text: Why must you never sneak up the right side of a truck that swings left before turning?
sec12-card-r32.teaching_text: Semis swing wide left only to clear the right curb, crushing any car wedged along their right flank.

sec12-card-r33.question_text: What extra expectation applies when following a diamond-placarded hazardous-material truck toward railroad tracks?
sec12-card-r33.teaching_text: Placarded tankers must halt at crossings even when warning gates stay up and lights stay dark.

sec12-card-r34.question_text: What traffic pattern should you anticipate in the right lane of four-lane mountain grades?
sec12-card-r34.teaching_text: Heavy trucks lose momentum fast on steep Idaho climbs, creating sharp closing speeds in the right lane.

sec12-card-r35.question_text: Why is parking in or near a mountain escape or runaway ramp strictly forbidden?
sec12-card-r35.teaching_text: An eighty-thousand-pound truck with smoking failed brakes hits gravel arrestor beds at lethal speed.

sec12-card-r36.question_text: What are pilot vehicles, and what job do their markings and amber lights signal?
sec12-card-r36.teaching_text: Spotting an escort pickup ahead or behind tells you an extra-wide or extra-long haul is near.

sec12-card-r37.question_text: How should you adjust speed and lane position when an oncoming pilot vehicle approaches?
sec12-card-r37.teaching_text: Manufactured homes and wide turbine blades often overhang centerlines across narrow rural bridges and curves.

sec12-card-r38.question_text: How should you follow and overtake a pilot vehicle and its oversize load?
sec12-card-r38.teaching_text: Wide loads block forward sightlines and leave minimal side margin along two-lane shoulders.

sec13-card-f01.question_text: What six types of updates does Idaho's traveler service provide to drivers?
sec13-card-f01.teaching_text: Checking traveler updates before mountain or winter trips prevents getting trapped behind highway closures, crash delays, or sudden storms.

sec13-card-f02.question_text: Which roadside controls and warnings must you obey when driving in the mountains?
sec13-card-f02.teaching_text: Advisory speeds and steep-grade signs warn you before gravity and blind switchbacks push your vehicle past tire grip limits.

sec13-card-f03.question_text: Where should you position your vehicle within your lane on mountain roads?
sec13-card-f03.teaching_text: Oncoming drivers often drift toward the centerline around tight canyon bends, so holding the right edge builds crucial clearance.

sec13-card-f04.question_text: How should you control your vehicle's speed on a long downhill mountain grade?
sec13-card-f04.teaching_text: Riding the foot brake down a long pass overheats pads until braking fades, whereas engine compression holds speed steady.

sec13-card-f05.question_text: Why must you never coast downhill in Neutral or with the clutch held down?
sec13-card-f05.teaching_text: Disengaging the drivetrain cuts off engine braking and instant throttle control right when gravity accelerates a heavy vehicle fastest.

sec13-card-f06.question_text: What pavement marking signals a no-passing zone along a mountain road?
sec13-card-f06.teaching_text: Hills and rock walls hide oncoming traffic on two-lane passes, making a solid yellow line in your lane nonnegotiable.

sec13-card-f07.question_text: When should you sound your horn before entering a curve on a narrow road?
sec13-card-f07.teaching_text: When trees or rock cuts block sightlines on a narrow road, a horn tap alerts hidden oncoming vehicles.

sec13-card-f08.question_text: When is swerving around a small animal on the road off-limits?
sec13-card-f08.teaching_text: Jerking the wheel for a squirrel or rabbit can launch your car into oncoming traffic or off a steep embankment.

sec13-card-f09.question_text: Why should you slow down and proceed cautiously after spotting one large animal near the road?
sec13-card-f09.teaching_text: Deer and elk rarely travel solo, so focusing only on the lead animal misses others bounding out behind it.

sec13-card-f10.question_text: What may be the safer choice if an animal darts out too fast to avoid safely?
sec13-card-f10.teaching_text: Staying straight under controlled braking beats panic-swerving into trees, guardrails, or head-on highway traffic.

sec13-card-f11.question_text: Who has priority when livestock are being moved under control across an Idaho road?
sec13-card-f11.teaching_text: Impatiently crowding cattle or sheep during a ranch crossing violates Idaho right-of-way rules and spooks heavy animals.

sec13-card-f12.question_text: How should you drive when meeting or passing a livestock herd on the road?
sec13-card-f12.teaching_text: Following hand signals from riders or herders prevents startling thousand-pound livestock into bolting against your vehicle.

sec13-card-f13.question_text: How does the Idaho handbook define open-range land?
sec13-card-f13.teaching_text: Outside city boundaries and designated herd districts, cattle and sheep legally roam across unfenced or grazed rural corridors.

sec13-card-f14.question_text: Does seeing a roadside fence guarantee that livestock are absent or lack priority?
sec13-card-f14.teaching_text: Dark hides blend into unlit pavement after sunset, and gates or breaks still let open-range stock wander onto highways.

sec13-card-f15.question_text: Who bears financial liability in a crash with open-range livestock or a controlled herd?
sec13-card-f15.teaching_text: Test takers are often surprised that striking open-range cattle leaves you paying your own repairs and potentially the rancher's loss.

sec13-card-f16.question_text: How fast may you safely travel at night relative to your headlight reach?
sec13-card-f16.teaching_text: Outrunning your headlight beam means that by the time an obstacle appears in the glow, stopping in time is impossible.

sec13-card-f17.question_text: How should you adjust your following gap behind traffic after dark?
sec13-card-f17.teaching_text: Judging closing speed off two red taillights is harder in the dark, so extra cushion prevents rear-end surprises.

sec13-card-f18.question_text: When must you turn on full headlights instead of driving with parking lights?
sec13-card-f18.teaching_text: Parking lights mark a stationary car and never project forward illumination when darkness or weather drops sightlines below five hundred feet.

sec13-card-f19.question_text: Which hard-to-spot road users and hazards require extra scanning at night?
sec13-card-f19.teaching_text: Slow farm gear, dark-clothed pedestrians, cyclists, and wildlife reflect almost no light until you are close.

sec13-card-f20.question_text: What extra precaution should you take when passing another vehicle at night?
sec13-card-f20.teaching_text: Oncoming headlights in the dark look farther away than they really are, so rush passes misjudge closing gaps.

sec13-card-f21.question_text: What two habits must you avoid regarding tiredness and eyewear during night or low-light driving?
sec13-card-f21.teaching_text: Driving tired slows reactions while tinted lenses starve your eyes of dim contrast cues needed to spot hazards.

sec13-card-f22.question_text: How should you maintain your windshield and headlights for clear night vision?
sec13-card-f22.teaching_text: Interior film scatters oncoming glare while road grime on headlamp lenses cuts forward beam brightness dramatically.

sec13-card-f23.question_text: Where should you direct your eyes when bright oncoming headlights approach at night?
sec13-card-f23.teaching_text: Staring into high beams bleaches night vision for crucial moments, whereas tracking the right lane edge guides steering safely.

sec13-card-f24.question_text: In which three situations should you select low-beam headlights?
sec13-card-f24.teaching_text: High beams blind oncoming drivers and bounce blindingly off a lead car's mirrors, while streetlit corridors already illuminate hazards.

sec13-card-f25.question_text: Which lights should you activate if forced to park on a highway shoulder at night?
sec13-card-f25.teaching_text: Unlit cars on dark shoulders risk getting struck by tired drivers, so hazard flashers or parking lights warn approaching traffic.

sec13-card-f26.question_text: Why must you keep extra caution and space around snow-removal equipment?
sec13-card-f26.teaching_text: Riding into a plow's whiteout plume erases lane edges and hides sudden stops or wide wing blades ahead.

sec13-card-f27.question_text: How many car lengths should you stay behind a snowplow for every ten miles an hour of speed?
sec13-card-f27.teaching_text: Giving two lengths per ten miles an hour keeps your windshield clear of flying sand, ice chunks, and blinding spray.

sec13-card-f28.question_text: When may you pass a snowplow, and which side is strictly off-limits?
sec13-card-f28.teaching_text: Snowplows often run offset wing blades inside the discharge plume that will shear off a passing vehicle.

sec13-card-f29.question_text: Why must you wait for extra room before merging back in front of a snowplow?
sec13-card-f29.teaching_text: Cutting back in tightly can clip a wide front plow blade hidden beneath billowing snow spray.

sec13-card-f30.question_text: Why should you avoid sudden braking when driving in front of a snowplow?
sec13-card-f30.teaching_text: Loaded sanders and plows carry massive momentum on slick pavement and cannot match a passenger car's stopping distance.

sec13-card-f31.question_text: What rule applies to abandoning a vehicle during snow-clearing operations?
sec13-card-f31.teaching_text: Cars left near travel lanes block plows from clearing the highway and risk getting buried or struck inside whiteouts.

sec13-card-f32.question_text: Which headlight beam works best in reduced daytime visibility, and what should you verify when switching on?
sec13-card-f32.teaching_text: High beams reflect glaringly off fog, snow, or dust, so check your dash indicator to confirm low beams are active.

sec13-card-f33.question_text: What should you do regarding fog, dust storms, or heavy rain?
sec13-card-f33.teaching_text: Postponing travel beats battling blinding dust or downpours, and slowing down immediately is vital whenever you must drive.

sec13-card-f34.question_text: When must you keep cruise control turned off?
sec13-card-f34.teaching_text: Cruise control keeps applying power when tires lose grip on water or ice, worsening wheelspin and sudden skids.

sec13-card-f35.question_text: Why should you slow even more when red taillights appear ahead in poor visibility?
sec13-card-f35.teaching_text: In thick fog or blowing snow, glowing red lamps ahead could belong to a dead-stopped or barely creeping vehicle.

sec13-card-r01.question_text: What should you do if visibility drops too severely to continue safely?
sec13-card-r01.teaching_text: Creeping slowly down an active travel lane in a whiteout or dust wall invites high-speed rear-end collisions.

sec13-card-r02.question_text: Why should you avoid driving with emergency flashers on in poor visibility?
sec13-card-r02.teaching_text: Drivers emerging through fog or snow associate four-way hazards with a parked breakdown and misjudge your movement.

sec13-card-r03.question_text: Why must you reduce speed during wet weather?
sec13-card-r03.teaching_text: Water reduces tire friction against asphalt, stretching braking distances and turning sharp steering inputs into skids.

sec13-card-r04.question_text: Why is the start of a light rain often the slickest moment on pavement?
sec13-card-r04.teaching_text: Light moisture floats accumulated grease and oil droplets to the surface before heavier rain washes that film away.

sec13-card-r05.question_text: What happens to your tires and vehicle control during hydroplaning?
sec13-card-r05.teaching_text: Once tires lift onto a wedge of water above the asphalt, steering, braking, and throttle inputs lose grip.

sec13-card-r06.question_text: Which three steps lower your risk of hydroplaning?
sec13-card-r06.teaching_text: Deep tire grooves and proper air pressure channel water out from under the tread while lower speed prevents planing.

sec13-card-r07.question_text: How should you respond right as your car enters a slick patch or starts hydroplaning?
sec13-card-r07.teaching_text: Easing off the gas shifts weight forward smoothly so tires settle back through the water layer onto pavement.

sec13-card-r08.question_text: Why must you avoid sudden turns or hard braking while hydroplaning?
sec13-card-r08.teaching_text: Turning the front wheels while floating on water spins the car violently sideways the instant pavement traction returns.

sec13-card-r09.question_text: How should you brake if slowing is necessary on a slick patch in a vehicle without ABS?
sec13-card-r09.teaching_text: Light brake pumping slows wheels without locking them solid so you keep directional steering control on slick surfaces.

sec13-card-r10.question_text: When must you take immediate protective action against flash flooding?
sec13-card-r10.teaching_text: Canyon and desert runoff surges in minutes, so act immediately upon a Flash Flood Warning or visibly rising water.

sec13-card-r11.question_text: What should you do when water covers the road ahead?
sec13-card-r11.teaching_text: Murky floodwater hides washed-out culverts and swift currents that trap drivers who try splashing through.

sec13-card-r12.question_text: Which terrain features should you evacuate for higher ground during flood danger?
sec13-card-r12.teaching_text: Dry washes, low dips, narrow canyons, and stream corridors channel upstream cloudbursts into sudden walls of water.

sec13-card-r13.question_text: Why must you stay away from rivers, streams, and already-flooded roads?
sec13-card-r13.teaching_text: Even shallow-looking water over a road can conceal a collapsed bridge approach or deep eroded crater underneath.

sec13-card-r14.question_text: What must you do immediately if your vehicle stalls inside rising floodwater?
sec13-card-r14.teaching_text: Staying inside a stalled car to restart it can trap occupants as buoyant floodwater sweeps the vehicle downstream.

sec13-card-r15.question_text: Why do flood conditions demand extra caution after dark?
sec13-card-r15.teaching_text: Black water across dark asphalt looks just like wet pavement until your front tires hit deep current.

sec13-card-r16.question_text: Where must you never camp or park when flood conditions threaten?
sec13-card-r16.teaching_text: Upstream storms miles away can send flash floods surging down a dry creek bed while your camp sky stays clear.

sec13-card-r17.question_text: How little fast-flowing water can knock a person down or carry away a vehicle?
sec13-card-r17.teaching_text: Fast water packs immense lateral force, sweeping adults off their feet at six inches and floating vehicles at two feet.

sec13-card-r18.question_text: What three driving adjustments belong on icy or snowy roads?
sec13-card-r18.teaching_text: Lowering speed, smoothing out turns and stops, and stretching following space prevent breaking scarce winter tire traction.

sec13-card-r19.question_text: Which six vehicle systems should you prepare before winter driving?
sec13-card-r19.teaching_text: Pre-season maintenance on lights, tires, brakes, wipers, defroster, and radiator prevents cold-weather breakdowns far from help.

sec13-card-r20.question_text: What window and washer-fluid steps apply before even a short winter trip?
sec13-card-r20.teaching_text: Peeking through a scraped porthole hides cross traffic, and plain water freezes solid on subzero windshields.

sec13-card-r21.question_text: What occupant restraints should be worn during winter travel?
sec13-card-r21.teaching_text: Bulky winter coats never replace properly snugged lap and shoulder belts if ice sends your car sliding.

sec13-card-r22.question_text: How should you pull out and accelerate on snowy or icy roads?
sec13-card-r22.teaching_text: Easing onto the throttle prevents wheelspin while an early low-speed feel check reveals how slick the surface is.

sec13-card-r23.question_text: How much earlier than normal should you start slowing for a winter turn or stop?
sec13-card-r23.teaching_text: Packed snow and glare ice multiply stopping distances, so starting deceleration three times earlier avoids sliding through intersections.

sec13-card-r24.question_text: How should you steer and apply brakes when stopping on slick winter roads?
sec13-card-r24.teaching_text: Check your owner's manual beforehand so you pump gently without ABS or hold steady pressure when ABS applies.

sec13-card-r25.question_text: When does the handbook recommend tire chains, and what should out-of-state travelers check?
sec13-card-r25.teaching_text: Severe mountain ice calls for tire chains, and neighboring states enforce their own chain-carry and installation laws.

sec13-card-r26.question_text: Where does road ice form earlier and linger longer than on sunlit pavement?
sec13-card-r26.teaching_text: Cold air circulates both above and below elevated bridge decks while tree or canyon shade blocks warming sunlight.

sec13-card-r27.question_text: What is Idaho's usual calendar window for studded snow tires?
sec13-card-r27.teaching_text: Metal studs chew up bare summer asphalt, so the seasonal window applies unless unusual weather prompts state date adjustments.

sec13-card-r28.question_text: Why should you carry a winter emergency kit in your vehicle?
sec13-card-r28.teaching_text: A rural spinout or highway closure can trap occupants in freezing conditions hours before tow or plow crews arrive.

sec13-card-r29.question_text: Which lighting, medical, tool, and warmth items start the winter emergency kit list?
sec13-card-r29.teaching_text: Having working light, medical supplies, a pocket knife, and a warm blanket or sleeping bag handles dark subzero waits.

sec13-card-r30.question_text: Which clothing and dig-out supplies belong in your winter stranding kit?
sec13-card-r30.teaching_text: Dry gloves, socks, and a wool cap prevent frostbite while a small shovel and sand or cat litter free spinning tires.

sec13-card-r31.question_text: Which food, water, signaling, power, and navigation items round out the winter kit?
sec13-card-r31.teaching_text: Packing water, nonperishable snacks, jumper cables, flares, bright cloth, waterproof fire starters, paper maps, and a charger covers long delays.

sec13-card-r32.question_text: What critical check must you make before running the engine for heat while stranded in snow?
sec13-card-r32.teaching_text: A snow-plugged tailpipe forces odorless deadly carbon monoxide gas straight back into the passenger cabin within minutes.

sec13-card-r33.question_text: How can you help snow crews spot your stranded car in deep drifts?
sec13-card-r33.teaching_text: Drifting snow quickly camouflages a parked car, whereas a bright scarf or cloth fluttering high flags down plow operators.

sec14-card-f01.question_text: Why must you think ahead instead of relying on instinctive reactions when a skid starts?
sec14-card-f01.teaching_text: Panicking and slamming the brake pedal during a slide locks traction further and spins the car out of control.

sec14-card-f02.question_text: How should you approach stops on slick pavement?
sec14-card-f02.teaching_text: Locked tires cannot steer around obstacles, so shedding speed early keeps rolling grip under your front wheels.

sec14-card-f03.question_text: On which road surfaces and driving conditions can skids happen?
sec14-card-f03.teaching_text: Do not assume bare summer asphalt makes you immune because high-speed travel or slamming the brakes skids dry tires too.

sec14-card-f04.question_text: How do you recover when your rear wheels start sliding sideways?
sec14-card-f04.teaching_text: Staying off both pedals while steering toward the sliding rear realigns the tires with your forward path.

sec14-card-f05.question_text: If the rear of your vehicle slides to the right, which way do you steer the front wheels?
sec14-card-f05.teaching_text: Turning left when the tail swings right whips the vehicle into a full spin instead of straightening out.

sec14-card-f06.question_text: Where should a driver practice winter stopping and skid recovery before hitting snowy roads?
sec14-card-f06.teaching_text: Learning how your car slides and regains grip in an empty private area beats improvising during rush-hour traffic.

sec14-card-f07.question_text: Where should you check the exact operating instructions for your vehicle's anti-lock braking system?
sec14-card-f07.teaching_text: Spending five minutes in the owner's manual tells you how your specific brake system behaves before an emergency strikes.

sec14-card-f08.question_text: How should you use the brake pedal during a hard emergency stop with ABS?
sec14-card-f08.teaching_text: Pumping an anti-lock pedal overrides the computer's rapid modulation and stretches your emergency stopping distance.

sec14-card-f09.question_text: What sound and pedal sensation can occur during hard braking with ABS?
sec14-card-f09.teaching_text: Rapid computer valve cycling creates mechanical chatter and pedal vibration as it prevents wheel lockup.

sec14-card-f10.question_text: Should you lift your foot when you hear ABS noise or feel the brake pedal pulse?
sec14-card-f10.teaching_text: Startled drivers who lift off a vibrating pedal throw away crucial stopping power right when ABS is working properly.

sec14-card-f11.question_text: How should you press the brake pedal for a quick stop in a car without ABS?
sec14-card-f11.teaching_text: Squeezing right up to the threshold just short of wheel lockup delivers maximum braking while preserving steering.

sec14-card-f12.question_text: What should you do right away if non-ABS brakes lock up and the car starts skidding?
sec14-card-f12.teaching_text: Letting off pedal pressure lets locked tires start rolling again so steering authority comes back immediately.

sec14-card-f13.question_text: After easing off to stop a non-ABS skid, how do you finish bringing the vehicle to a halt?
sec14-card-f13.teaching_text: Cycling smooth release and firm reapplication keeps non-ABS tires biting pavement all the way to zero speed.

sec14-card-f14.question_text: Where should you position a stalled car that still rolls, and which lights go on?
sec14-card-f14.teaching_text: Clearing every inch of the travel lane and switching on four-way hazards shields a disabled car from highway traffic.

sec14-card-f15.question_text: What physical cue on your vehicle signals to passing drivers and patrols that your car is stalled?
sec14-card-f15.teaching_text: Propping open the hood communicates mechanical trouble from far upstream so troopers and motorists recognize a breakdown.

sec14-card-f16.question_text: If your stalled car cannot get off the road, where should you try to stop and which blind spots must you avoid?
sec14-card-f16.teaching_text: Stopping just over a crest or around a bend gives fast-approaching drivers zero sight distance to brake.

sec14-card-f17.question_text: How far behind a disabled vehicle should you place warning flares when available?
sec14-card-f17.teaching_text: Placing flares two hundred to three hundred feet upstream warns highway drivers early enough to slow or change lanes.

sec14-card-f18.question_text: How can you warn approaching traffic if your breakdown kit has no flares?
sec14-card-f18.teaching_text: Signal with a white cloth or flag from well off the pavement rather than standing inside live traffic lanes.

sec14-card-f19.question_text: Which two categories of vehicle control can help avoid an imminent crash?
sec14-card-f19.teaching_text: Avoiding a wreck is not limited to slamming brakes when steering clear or accelerating out of danger works faster.

sec14-card-f20.question_text: When stopping in time looks impossible, how should you steer clear to keep control?
sec14-card-f20.teaching_text: Stomping the brakes mid-swerve overloads front tire grip and plows the car straight into the hazard.

sec14-card-f21.question_text: Against which crash angles can brisk acceleration prevent or lessen an impact?
sec14-card-f21.teaching_text: When an intersection runner or tailgating rig closes fast from the side or rear, speeding ahead clears the impact zone.

sec14-card-f22.question_text: What simple pre-drive step protects occupants if crash avoidance fails?
sec14-card-f22.teaching_text: Even skilled evasive steering cannot prevent every collision, making properly worn seat belts your primary survival layer.

sec14-card-f23.question_text: If an oncoming vehicle drifts into your lane with time to react, how do you slow and alert that driver?
sec14-card-f23.teaching_text: Shedding speed cuts impact energy while horn blasts and headlight flashes snap a drowsy or distracted driver awake.

sec14-card-f24.question_text: Why must you dodge to the right rather than swerving left against a head-on threat?
sec14-card-f24.teaching_text: When the drifting oncoming driver looks up and jerks back into their own lane, swerving left puts you nose-to-nose.

sec14-card-f25.question_text: If a collision cannot be escaped completely, which impact angle is safer than hitting head-on?
sec14-card-f25.teaching_text: Glancing off at an angle deflects crash forces instead of combining both vehicles' full speeds nose-to-nose.

sec14-card-f26.question_text: What is your immediate steering and pedal rule when a tire blows out?
sec14-card-f26.teaching_text: Slamming the brakes during a blowout yanks the rim hard toward the flat side and flips or spins the car.

sec14-card-f27.question_text: How should you shed speed right after stabilizing a tire blowout?
sec14-card-f27.teaching_text: Letting engine drag bleed speed off smoothly stabilizes the wobbling corner before any brake pressure touches the wheels.

sec14-card-f28.question_text: Once a vehicle with a blown tire is fully under control, how do you finish stopping?
sec14-card-f28.teaching_text: Light progressive braking guides the disabled vehicle onto a flat shoulder away from fast travel lanes.

sec14-card-f29.question_text: What should you do first if your wheels drop off the pavement edge onto a clear shoulder?
sec14-card-f29.teaching_text: Yanking the wheel immediately against a high pavement lip catches the tire edge and slingshots you across traffic.

sec14-card-f30.question_text: How should you reduce speed after your wheels drop onto the shoulder?
sec14-card-f30.teaching_text: Gravel and dirt shoulders offer uneven grip compared with asphalt, so hard braking pulls the car sideways.

sec14-card-f31.question_text: After slowing on the shoulder, how do you return onto the roadway safely?
sec14-card-f31.teaching_text: Waiting for an open traffic gap and easing smoothly over the lip prevents shooting across the centerline into oncoming lanes.

sec14-card-r01.question_text: What trip details should you share beforehand, and what phone prep belongs on winter travel?
sec14-card-r01.teaching_text: If a blizzard traps you in a dead zone, people knowing your exact route, schedule, and lodging speeds search rescue.

sec14-card-r02.question_text: What should you do if your car gets stranded while heavy snow is falling?
sec14-card-r02.teaching_text: Walking for help in blowing snow quickly causes disorientation and hypothermia, whereas rescuers spot vehicles far easier.

sec14-card-r03.question_text: Whom should you contact during a medical emergency when roads are unplowed?
sec14-card-r03.teaching_text: Law enforcement dispatches plows, snowcats, or emergency responders together instead of letting family cars get stuck too.

sec14-card-r04.question_text: What should you prepare to do if a side-impact collision cannot be avoided?
